墳丘（中央に後円部、右奥に前方部） |別名 = |所属 = |所在地 = [[栃木県]][[宇都宮市]]西川田町東原 |位置 = |形状 = [[帆立貝形古墳]] |規模 = 墳丘長63.1m
高さ6.7m（後円部） |埋葬施設 = 不明 |出土品 = [[埴輪]]・[[須恵器]] |陪塚 = |築造時期 = [[5世紀]]後葉 |被葬者 = |陵墓 = |史跡 = 栃木県指定史跡「塚山西古墳」 |有形文化財 = |特記事項 = }} '''塚山西古墳'''（つかやまにしこふん）は、塚山古墳の南西にある古墳。形状は[[帆立貝形古墳]]。栃木県指定史跡に指定されている。 墳形は、前方部が短小な帆立貝形の前方後円形で、前方部を南南東方向に向ける。墳丘の規模は次の通り{{Sfn|塚山西古墳・塚山南古墳|2003}}。 * 古墳総長：74.1メートル - 周濠を含めた古墳全長。 * 墳丘長：63.1メートル * 後円部 ** 直径：44.5メートル ** 高さ：6.7メートル * 前方部 ** 長さ：約18メートル ** 幅：約22メートル ** 高さ：約1.5メートル 墳丘は2段以上の築成（2段目以上は撹乱が著しく不明）{{Sfn|塚山西古墳・塚山南古墳|2003}}。墳丘外表では円筒埴輪・須恵器（TK208-TK23型式）が検出されている{{Sfn|塚山西古墳・塚山南古墳|2003}}。また墳丘周囲には馬蹄形の周濠が巡らされる（東側は塚山古墳の制約のため浅い）{{Sfn|塚山西古墳・塚山南古墳|2003}}。埋葬施設は後円部墳頂に存在するが、一部の検出に留まるため詳らかでない（粘土・石材の検出はなし）{{Sfn|塚山西古墳・塚山南古墳|2003}}。副葬品は詳らかでない。 築造時期は古墳時代中期の5世紀後葉頃と推定され、塚山古墳に後続し塚山南古墳に先行する時期に想定される{{Sfn|塚山古墳群（続古墳）|2002}}。 === 塚山南古墳 === {{日本の古墳 |名称 = 塚山南古墳 |画像 = [[File:Tsukayama Minami Kofun (Utsunomiya), funkyu-2.jpg|280px]]
墳丘（中央に後円部、右奥に前方部） |別名 = |所属 = |所在地 = [[栃木県]][[宇都宮市]]西川田町東原 |位置 = |形状 = [[帆立貝形古墳]] |規模 = 墳丘長58m
高さ6.8m（後円部） |埋葬施設 = 不明 |出土品 = [[埴輪]]・[[須恵器]]・[[土師器]] |陪塚 = |築造時期 = [[5世紀]]末葉 |被葬者 = |陵墓 = |史跡 = 栃木県指定史跡「塚山南古墳」 |有形文化財 = 出土土器（宇都宮市指定文化財） |特記事項 = }} '''塚山南古墳'''（つかやまみなみこふん）は、塚山西古墳の南にある古墳。形状は帆立貝形古墳。栃木県指定史跡に指定されている。 墳形は、前方部が短小な帆立貝形の前方後円形で、前方部を南方向に向ける。墳丘の規模は次の通り{{Sfn|塚山西古墳・塚山南古墳|2003}}。 * 古墳総長：70.6メートル - 周濠を含めた古墳全長。 * 墳丘長：58.0メートル * 後円部 ** 直径：42.1メートル ** 高さ：6.8メートル * 前方部 ** 長さ：13.5メートル ** 高さ：4.1メートル 墳丘は2段築成{{Sfn|塚山西古墳・塚山南古墳|2003}}。墳丘外表では円筒埴輪・形象埴輪（人物形・馬形・鹿形・家形埴輪）のほか、多数の須恵器（大甕・高坏形器台・装飾付脚付壺・二重𤭯：TK208-TK23型式）・[[土師器]]が検出されているが、葺石は認められていない{{Sfn|塚山西古墳・塚山南古墳|2003}}。また墳丘周囲には馬蹄形の周濠が巡らされる（後円部北西側は塚山西古墳の制約のため狭い）{{Sfn|塚山西古墳・塚山南古墳|2003}}。埋葬施設は未調査のため明らかでないが、墳頂に窪みや赤彩の石が存在することから、後円部墳頂における竪穴系施設であるが盗掘を受けていると推測される{{Sfn|塚山西古墳・塚山南古墳|2003}}。副葬品は詳らかでない。 築造時期は古墳時代後期の5世紀末葉{{Sfn|塚山古墳群（続古墳）|2002}}（5世紀末葉-6世紀初頭{{Sfn|塚山西古墳・塚山南古墳|2003}}）頃と推定され、塚山西古墳に後続する時期に想定される{{Sfn|塚山古墳群（続古墳）|2002}}。 == 文化財 == === 栃木県指定文化財 === * 史跡 ** 塚山古墳 - 1953年（昭和28年）11月10日指定[http://www.tochigi-edu.ed.jp/center/bunkazai/2341001.htm 塚山古墳]（栃木県教育委員会事務局文化財課「とちぎの文化財」）。[https://utsunomiya-8story.jp/search_post/%e5%a1%9a%e5%b1%b1%e5%8f%a4%e5%a2%b3/ 塚山古墳]（宇都宮市歴史文化資源活用推進協議会「宇都宮の歴史と文化財」）。。 ** 塚山西古墳 - 1973年（昭和48年）4月13日指定[http://www.tochigi-edu.ed.jp/center/bunkazai/2341039.htm 塚山西古墳]（栃木県教育委員会事務局文化財課「とちぎの文化財」）。[https://utsunomiya-8story.jp/search_post/%e5%a1%9a%e5%b1%b1%e8%a5%bf%e5%8f%a4%e5%a2%b3/ 塚山西古墳]（宇都宮市歴史文化資源活用推進協議会「宇都宮の歴史と文化財」）。。 ** 塚山南古墳 - ### Tsukayama Kofun (塚山古墳) The **Tsukayama Kofun**, located in Nishikawada Town, Utsunomiya City, Tochigi Prefecture, is a keyhole-shaped tumulus (*zenpō-kōen-fun*). It is part of the **Tsukayama Kofun Group**, designated as a Tochigi Prefectural Historic Site. This article also describes the Tsukayama Kofun Group, with the Tsukayama Kofun as its main tumulus. --- ### Overview The **Tsukayama Kofun** is a large keyhole-shaped tumulus constructed atop a plateau between the Tagawa and Sugata Rivers in southern Tochigi. It is the largest kofun in the Tsukayama Kofun Group, which includes other kofun such as the shell-shaped *hotategai* tumuli, Tsukayama Nishi Kofun and Tsukayama Minami Kofun. Over time, the rear circular portion of the mound has been partially damaged by road construction. Between 1989 and 1991, surveys and excavations were carried out in four phases. - **Shape**: The tumulus has a "sword-hilt" keyhole shape, with a prominent anterior portion extending to the west. The mound features three construction stages (*dan*) and external covering stones (*fukiishi*). - **Artifacts**: Finds include cylindrical *haniwa*, *Sue ware* (TK216-208 type), and *haji ware* pottery. A platform (*tsukuridashi*) exists on the southern constricted section of the mound. A shield-shaped moat encircles the tumulus, with a total length of 119.2 meters when including the moat. - **Age**: The kofun is believed to have been constructed in the mid-5th century during the Kofun period. It served as a large burial site for a regional leader in the Shimotsuke area. The mound is now part of a landscaped historical park, with azaleas planted to enhance its unique appearance. --- ### Historical Timeline 1. **1953 (Showa 28)**: Tsukayama Kofun designated a Tochigi Prefectural Historic Site. 2. **1966 (Showa 41)**: Plans for a new highway led to design changes to protect the kofun group, including the construction of a tunnel nearby. 3. **1973 (Showa 48)**: Tsukayama Nishi Kofun and Tsukayama Minami Kofun were also designated as historic sites. 4. **1989–1991**: Excavation surveys were conducted by the Utsunomiya University Archaeology Research Association. Further excavations and preservation efforts continued through the 1990s. 5. **2005 (Heisei 17)**: Artifacts from Tsukayama Minami Kofun were designated as tangible cultural properties by Utsunomiya City. --- ### Mound Specifications - **Overall Length (with Moat)**: 119.2 meters - **Mound Length**: 98.3 meters - **Rear Circular Section**: Diameter 55.9 meters - **Front Rectangular Section**: Width 59.9 meters Images of the tumulus and surrounding moat show its well-preserved features, including a clear distinction between the front and rear sections. --- ### Tsukayama Kofun Group The **Tsukayama Kofun Group** comprises several tumuli surrounding the Tsukayama Kofun. At its peak, the group included more than ten burial mounds, though many have since been lost. Today, notable surviving mounds include: 1. **Tsukayama Kofun (Main Tumulus)**: - Keyhole-shaped (*zenpō-kōen-fun*) - Length: 98.3 meters - Artifacts: *Haniwa* and *Sue ware* - Age: Mid-5th century - Designated a prefectural historic site in 1953. 2. **Tsukayama Nishi Kofun**: - Shell-shaped (*hotategai*) - Length: 63.1 meters - Artifacts: *Haniwa* and *Sue ware* - Age: Late 5th century - Designated a prefectural historic site in 1973. 3. **Tsukayama Minami Kofun**: - Shell-shaped (*hotategai*) - Length: 58 meters - Artifacts: Cylindrical and figurative *haniwa* (horses, deer, houses) and pottery (*Sue ware* and *haji ware*) - Age: Late 5th to early 6th century - Designated a prefectural historic site in 1973. Other smaller tumuli include: - **6th Tumulus**: A small round burial mound, 20 meters in diameter, with *haniwa* remains. - **Disappeared Mounds**: Several smaller round burial mounds and *haniwa* caskets were lost to development. --- ### Cultural Artifacts and Significance Artifacts from the group, including cylindrical and decorative *haniwa*, highlight the sophisticated burial practices of the Kofun period. Of particular note are engravings on a *haniwa* casket, depicting alternating male and female deer—symbolic of fertility and vitality. The group offers valuable insights into the sociopolitical landscape of the Shimotsuke region, reflecting its transition during the Kofun period. --- ### Conservation and Visitor Information The **Tsukayama Kofun Group** is part of Utsunomiya's cultural heritage preservation program. Detailed signage and maintained pathways make the site accessible to visitors. Additional resources include a pamphlet published by the Utsunomiya City Board of Education and historical survey reports, which are available online. --- ### Related Sites and Resources - **Sasazuka Kofun**: Another notable tumulus in Tochigi Prefecture. - **Tochigi Prefectural Comprehensive Sports Park**: A nearby recreational facility. External links: - [Tsukayama Kofun (Tochigi Education Board)](http://www.tochigi-edu.ed.jp) - [Utsunomiya Cultural Heritage Website](https://utsunomiya-8story.jp) --- This comprehensive description provides a detailed understanding of the historical, cultural, and archaeological significance of the Tsukayama Kofun and its associated group. It is the largest kofun in the Tsukayama Kofun Group, which includes other kofun such as the shell-shaped *hotategai* tumuli, Tsukayama Nishi Kofun and Tsukayama Minami Kofun. Over time, the rear circular portion of the mound has been partially damaged by road construction. Between 1989 and 1991, surveys and excavations were carried out in four phases. - **Shape**: The tumulus has a "sword-hilt" keyhole shape, with a prominent anterior portion extending to the west. The mound features three construction stages (*dan*) and external covering stones (*fukiishi*). - **Artifacts**: Finds include cylindrical *haniwa*, *Sue ware* (TK216-208 type), and *haji ware* pottery. A platform (*tsukuridashi*) exists on the southern constricted section of the mound. A shield-shaped moat encircles the tumulus, with a total length of 119.2 meters when including the moat. - **Age**: The kofun is believed to have been constructed in the mid-5th century during the Kofun period. It served as a large burial site for a regional leader in the Shimotsuke area. Further excavations and preservation efforts continued through the 1990s. 5. **2005 (Heisei 17)**: Artifacts from Tsukayama Minami Kofun were designated as tangible cultural properties by Utsunomiya City. --- ### Mound Specifications - **Overall Length (with Moat)**: 119.2 meters - **Mound Length**: 98.3 meters - **Rear Circular Section**: Diameter 55.9 meters - **Front Rectangular Section**: Width 59.9 meters Images of the tumulus and surrounding moat show its well-preserved features, including a clear distinction between the front and rear sections. --- ### Tsukayama Kofun Group The **Tsukayama Kofun Group** comprises several tumuli surrounding the Tsukayama Kofun. ''Tsukayama-nishi kofun'' || [[Utsunomiy ... 37 KB (4,206 words) - 21:20, 12 January[[Category:original pages]][[Category:most recent 100 pages]][[Category:kofun stubs]] [[Category:Original pages]][[Category:Most recent 100 pages]] [[Category:mass bump]] [[Category:making categorization show up on newly imported categories and templates]] [[Category:Https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/]][[ja:%E5%A1%9A%E5%B1%B1%E5%8F%A4%E5%A2%B3 (%E5%AE%87%E9%83%BD%E5%AE%AE%E5%B8%82)#%E5%A1%9A%E5%B1%B1%E8%A5%BF%E5%8F%A4%E5%A2%B3]] 2025

The **Tsukayama Kofun**, located in Nishikawada Town, Utsunomiya City, Tochigi Prefecture, is a keyhole-shaped tumulus (*zenpō-kōen-fun*). It is part of the **Tsukayama Kofun Group**, designated as a Tochigi Prefectural Historic Site. This article also describes the Tsukayama Kofun Group, with the Tsukayama Kofun as its main tumulus. --- == Overview == The **Tsukayama Kofun** is a large keyhole-shaped tumulus constructed atop a plateau between the Tagawa and Sugata Rivers in southern Tochigi. It is the largest kofun in the Tsukayama Kofun Group, which includes other kofun such as the shell-shaped *hotategai* tumuli, Tsukayama Nishi Kofun and Tsukayama Minami Kofun. Over time, the rear circular portion of the mound has been partially damaged by road construction. Between 1989 and 1991, surveys and excavations were carried out in four phases. - **Shape**: The tumulus has a "sword-hilt" keyhole shape, with a prominent anterior portion extending to the west. The mound features three construction stages (*dan*) and external covering stones (*fukiishi*). - **Artifacts**: Finds include cylindrical *haniwa*, *Sue ware* (TK216-208 type), and *haji ware* pottery. A platform (*tsukuridashi*) exists on the southern constricted section of the mound. A shield-shaped moat encircles the tumulus, with a total length of 119.2 meters when including the moat. - **Age**: The kofun is believed to have been constructed in the mid-5th century during the Kofun period. It served as a large burial site for a regional leader in the Shimotsuke area. The mound is now part of a landscaped historical park, with azaleas planted to enhance its unique appearance. --- == Historical Timeline == 1. **1953 (Showa 28)**: Tsukayama Kofun designated a Tochigi Prefectural Historic Site. 2. **1966 (Showa 41)**: Plans for a new highway led to design changes to protect the kofun group, including the construction of a tunnel nearby. 3. **1973 (Showa 48)**: Tsukayama Nishi Kofun and Tsukayama Minami Kofun were also designated as historic sites. 4. **1989–1991**: Excavation surveys were conducted by the Utsunomiya University Archaeology Research Association. Further excavations and preservation efforts continued through the 1990s. 5. **2005 (Heisei 17)**: Artifacts from Tsukayama Minami Kofun were designated as tangible cultural properties by Utsunomiya City. --- == Mound Specifications == - **Overall Length (with Moat)**: 119.2 meters - **Mound Length**: 98.3 meters - **Rear Circular Section**: Diameter 55.9 meters - **Front Rectangular Section**: Width 59.9 meters Images of the tumulus and surrounding moat show its well-preserved features, including a clear distinction between the front and rear sections. --- == Tsukayama Kofun Group == The **Tsukayama Kofun Group** comprises several tumuli surrounding the Tsukayama Kofun. At its peak, the group included more than ten burial mounds, though many have since been lost. Today, notable surviving mounds include: 1. **Tsukayama Kofun (Main Tumulus)**: - Keyhole-shaped (*zenpō-kōen-fun*) - Length: 98.3 meters - Artifacts: *Haniwa* and *Sue ware* - Age: Mid-5th century - Designated a prefectural historic site in 1953. 2. **Tsukayama Nishi Kofun**: - Shell-shaped (*hotategai*) - Length: 63.1 meters - Artifacts: *Haniwa* and *Sue ware* - Age: Late 5th century - Designated a prefectural historic site in 1973. 3. **Tsukayama Minami Kofun**: - Shell-shaped (*hotategai*) - Length: 58 meters - Artifacts: Cylindrical and figurative *haniwa* (horses, deer, houses) and pottery (*Sue ware* and *haji ware*) - Age: Late 5th to early 6th century - Designated a prefectural historic site in 1973. Other smaller tumuli include: - **6th Tumulus**: A small round burial mound, 20 meters in diameter, with *haniwa* remains. - **Disappeared Mounds**: Several smaller round burial mounds and *haniwa* caskets were lost to development. --- == Cultural Artifacts and Significance == Artifacts from the group, including cylindrical and decorative *haniwa*, highlight the sophisticated burial practices of the Kofun period. Of particular note are engravings on a *haniwa* casket, depicting alternating male and female deer—symbolic of fertility and vitality. The group offers valuable insights into the sociopolitical landscape of the Shimotsuke region, reflecting its transition during the Kofun period. --- == Conservation and Visitor Information == The **Tsukayama Kofun Group** is part of Utsunomiya's cultural heritage preservation program. Detailed signage and maintained pathways make the site accessible to visitors. Additional resources include a pamphlet published by the Utsunomiya City Board of Education and historical survey reports, which are available online. --- == Related Sites and Resources == - **Sasazuka Kofun**: Another notable tumulus in Tochigi Prefecture. - **Tochigi Prefectural Comprehensive Sports Park**: A nearby recreational facility. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳}} and part of the {{ill|Tsukayama Kofun Cluster|ja|塚山古墳群}}. It has been designated as a Tochigi Prefecture-designated historical site. This article also covers the {{ill|Tsukayama Kofun Cluster|ja|塚山古墳群}}, for which Tsukayama Kofun serves as the main mound. == Overview == [[File:100425 Tsukayama Kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|{{center|Aerial view of the Tsukayama Kofun Cluster (2010)}}{{small|Top right: Tsukayama Kofun; Left: Tsukayama West Kofun; Bottom left: Tsukayama South Kofun. {{ill|Aerial photographs of Japan|ja|国土航空写真}}.}}]] Located in southern Tochigi Prefecture, the mound was constructed on a plateau between the {{ill|Tagawa River (Tone River System)|ja|田川 (利根川水系)}} and {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}}. It is the largest keyhole-shaped kofun in the Tsukayama Kofun Cluster, which includes several mounds such as the scallop-shaped Tsukayama West and South Kofun, as well as {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}}-based coffins. The rear circular section has been partially leveled by road construction. In 1989 (Heisei 1), a survey was conducted, followed by four excavation campaigns from 1989 to 1991. The mound has a "Kenbishi-style" keyhole shape with a protruding front section oriented westward. It is constructed in three tiers, with external surfaces featuring {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}}. Cylindrical {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}}, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}} (TK216-208 style), and {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}} have been excavated. The southern neck of the mound features a {{ill|tsukuridashi|ja|造出}}, and the shield-shaped moat surrounding the mound brings the total length to 119.2 meters. The burial facility remains unexamined, and grave goods are largely unknown. The mound is estimated to date from the mid-5th century, during the middle {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} (or the late 5th century, according to other estimates). It served as a prominent burial site for regional leaders in the southern Utsunomiya area and is considered critical for studying the political dynamics of the {{ill|Shimotsukeno region|ja|下毛野地方}}. The site was designated as a Tochigi Prefecture historical site in 1953 (Shōwa 28). Today, the mound is adorned with {{ill|Dodantsutsuji shrubs|ja|ドウダンツツジ}}, offering a unique landscape that has been developed for preservation. == Historical Timeline == 1. **1953 (Showa 28)**: Tsukayama Kofun designated a Tochigi Prefectural Historic Site. 2. **1966 (Showa 41)**: Plans for a new highway led to design changes to protect the kofun group, including the construction of a tunnel nearby. 3. **1973 (Showa 48)**: Tsukayama Nishi Kofun and Tsukayama Minami Kofun were also designated as historic sites. 4. **1989–1991**: Excavation surveys were conducted by the Utsunomiya University Archaeology Research Association. Further excavations and preservation efforts continued through the 1990s. 5. **2005 (Heisei 17)**: Artifacts from Tsukayama Minami Kofun were designated as tangible cultural properties by Utsunomiya City. --- == Mound Specifications == - **Overall Length (with Moat)**: 119.2 meters - **Mound Length**: 98.3 meters - **Rear Circular Section**: Diameter 55.9 meters - **Front Rectangular Section**: Width 59.9 meters Images of the tumulus and surrounding moat show its well-preserved features, including a clear distinction between the front and rear sections. --- == Tsukayama Kofun Group == The **Tsukayama Kofun Group** comprises several tumuli surrounding the Tsukayama Kofun. At its peak, the group included more than ten burial mounds, though many have since been lost. Today, notable surviving mounds include: 1. **Tsukayama Kofun (Main Tumulus)**: - Keyhole-shaped (*zenpō-kōen-fun*) - Length: 98.3 meters - Artifacts: *Haniwa* and *Sue ware* - Age: Mid-5th century - Designated a prefectural historic site in 1953. 2. **Tsukayama Nishi Kofun**: - Shell-shaped (*hotategai*) - Length: 63.1 meters - Artifacts: *Haniwa* and *Sue ware* - Age: Late 5th century - Designated a prefectural historic site in 1973. 3. **Tsukayama Minami Kofun**: - Shell-shaped (*hotategai*) - Length: 58 meters - Artifacts: Cylindrical and figurative *haniwa* (horses, deer, houses) and pottery (*Sue ware* and *haji ware*) - Age: Late 5th to early 6th century - Designated a prefectural historic site in 1973. Other smaller tumuli include: - **6th Tumulus**: A small round burial mound, 20 meters in diameter, with *haniwa* remains. - **Disappeared Mounds**: Several smaller round burial mounds and *haniwa* caskets were lost to development. --- == Cultural Artifacts and Significance == Artifacts from the group, including cylindrical and decorative *haniwa*, highlight the sophisticated burial practices of the Kofun period. Of particular note are engravings on a *haniwa* casket, depicting alternating male and female deer—symbolic of fertility and vitality. The group offers valuable insights into the sociopolitical landscape of the Shimotsuke region, reflecting its transition during the Kofun period. --- == Conservation and Visitor Information == The **Tsukayama Kofun Group** is part of Utsunomiya's cultural heritage preservation program. Mound (Right: front section; Left-back: rear circular section) | Alternate Name = Hyōgo-zuka Kofun | Group = Tsukayama Kofun Cluster | Location = Nishikawada-machi 7-chome, {{ill|Utsunomiya City|ja|宇都宮市}}, Tochigi Prefecture | Coordinates = {{Coord|36|30|22.05|N|139|51|39.50|E|region:JP-09_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Tsukayama Kofun}} | Shape = {{ill|Keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳}} (Kenbishi-style) | Dimensions = Total mound length: 98.3 meters | Burial Facility = Unknown | Artifacts = {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}}, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}} | Burial Mounds = | Construction Era = Mid-5th century | Buried Figure = | Mausoleum = | Historical Site = Tochigi Prefecture-designated Historical Site (Tsukayama Kofun) | Cultural Asset = | Notes = | Map2 = {{Location map|Japan Tochigi|label=Tsukayama Kofun|lat_deg=36|lat_min=30|lat_sec=22.05|lon_deg=139|lon_min=51|lon_sec=39.5|mark=前方後円墳-西南西.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=top|width=200|caption=}} }} {{OSM Location map | coord = {{Coord|36|30|20|N|139|51|38|E}} | zoom = 17 | float = right | width = 300 | height = 250 | caption = {{center|Distribution map of the Tsukayama Kofun Cluster}} | scalemark = 60 | mark-coord1 = {{Coord|36|30|22.05|N|139|51|39.50|E}} | label1 = Tsukayama Kofun | label-pos1 = top | label-color1 = black | mark1 = 前方後円墳-西南西.svg | mark-size1 = 70 | mark-coord2 = {{Coord|36|30|20.25|N|139|51|36.35|E}} | label2 = Tsukayama West Kofun | label-pos2 = top | label-color2 = black | mark2 = 帆立貝形古墳-南南東.svg | mark-size2 = 60 | mark-coord3 = {{Coord|36|30|17.93|N|139|51|37.23|E}} | label3 = Tsukayama South Kofun | label-pos3 = left | label-color3 = black | mark3 = 帆立貝形古墳-南.svg | mark-size3 = 60 }} '''Tsukayama Kofun''' (塚山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in Nishikawada-machi, {{ill|Utsunomiya City|ja|宇都宮市}}, Tochigi Prefecture. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳}} and part of the {{ill|Tsukayama Kofun Cluster|ja|塚山古墳群}}. It has been designated as a Tochigi Prefecture-designated historical site. This article also covers the {{ill|Tsukayama Kofun Cluster|ja|塚山古墳群}}, for which Tsukayama Kofun serves as the main mound. == Overview == [[File:100425 Tsukayama Kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|{{center|Aerial view of the Tsukayama Kofun Cluster (2010)}}{{small|Top right: Tsukayama Kofun; Left: Tsukayama West Kofun; Bottom left: Tsukayama South Kofun. {{ill|Aerial photographs of Japan|ja|国土航空写真}}.}}]] Located in southern Tochigi Prefecture, the mound was constructed on a plateau between the {{ill|Tagawa River (Tone River System)|ja|田川 (利根川水系)}} and {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}}. It is the largest keyhole-shaped kofun in the Tsukayama Kofun Cluster, which includes several mounds such as the scallop-shaped Tsukayama West and South Kofun, as well as {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}}-based coffins. The rear circular section has been partially leveled by road construction. In 1989 (Heisei 1), a survey was conducted, followed by four excavation campaigns from 1989 to 1991. The mound has a "Kenbishi-style" keyhole shape with a protruding front section oriented westward. It is constructed in three tiers, with external surfaces featuring {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}}. Cylindrical {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}}, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}} (TK216-208 style), and {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}} have been excavated. The southern neck of the mound features a {{ill|tsukuridashi|ja|造出}}, and the shield-shaped moat surrounding the mound brings the total length to 119.2 meters. The burial facility remains unexamined, and grave goods are largely unknown. The mound is estimated to date from the mid-5th century, during the middle {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} (or the late 5th century, according to other estimates). It served as a prominent burial site for regional leaders in the southern Utsunomiya area and is considered critical for studying the political dynamics of the {{ill|Shimotsukeno region|ja|下毛野地方}}. The site was designated as a Tochigi Prefecture historical site in 1953 (Shōwa 28). Today, the mound is adorned with {{ill|Dodantsutsuji shrubs|ja|ドウダンツツジ}}, offering a unique landscape that has been developed for preservation. == Historical Timeline == 1. **1953 (Showa 28)**: Tsukayama Kofun designated a Tochigi Prefectural Historic Site. 2. **1966 (Showa 41)**: Plans for a new highway led to design changes to protect the kofun group, including the construction of a tunnel nearby. 3. **1973 (Showa 48)**: Tsukayama Nishi Kofun and Tsukayama Minami Kofun were also designated as historic sites. 4. **1989–1991**: Excavation surveys were conducted by the Utsunomiya University Archaeology Research Association. Further excavations and preservation efforts continued through the 1990s. 5. **2005 (Heisei 17)**: Artifacts from Tsukayama Minami Kofun were designated as tangible cultural properties by Utsunomiya City. --- == Mound Specifications == - **Overall Length (with Moat)**: 119.2 meters - **Mound Length**: 98.3 meters - **Rear Circular Section**: Diameter 55.9 meters - **Front Rectangular Section**: Width 59.9 meters Images of the tumulus and surrounding moat show its well-preserved features, including a clear distinction between the front and rear sections. --- == Tsukayama Kofun Group == The **Tsukayama Kofun Group** comprises several tumuli surrounding the Tsukayama Kofun. At its peak, the group included more than ten burial mounds, though many have since been lost. Today, notable surviving mounds include: 1. **Tsukayama Kofun (Main Tumulus)**: - Keyhole-shaped (*zenpō-kōen-fun*) - Length: 98.3 meters - Artifacts: *Haniwa* and *Sue ware* - Age: Mid-5th century - Designated a prefectural historic site in 1953. 2. **Tsukayama Nishi Kofun**: - Shell-shaped (*hotategai*) - Length: 63.1 meters - Artifacts: *Haniwa* and *Sue ware* - Age: Late 5th century - Designated a prefectural historic site in 1973. 3. **Tsukayama Minami Kofun**: - Shell-shaped (*hotategai*) - Length: 58 meters - Artifacts: Cylindrical and figurative *haniwa* (horses, deer, houses) and pottery (*Sue ware* and *haji ware*) - Age: Late 5th to early 6th century - Designated a prefectural historic site in 1973. Other smaller tumuli include: - **6th Tumulus**: A small round burial mound, 20 meters in diameter, with *haniwa* remains. - **Disappeared Mounds**: Several smaller round burial mounds and *haniwa* caskets were lost to development. --- == Cultural Artifacts and Significance == Artifacts from the group, including cylindrical and decorative *haniwa*, highlight the sophisticated burial practices of the Kofun period. Of particular note are engravings on a *haniwa* casket, depicting alternating male and female deer—symbolic of fertility and vitality. The group offers valuable insights into the sociopolitical landscape of the Shimotsuke region, reflecting its transition during the Kofun period. --- == Conservation and Visitor Information == The **Tsukayama Kofun Group** is part of Utsunomiya's cultural heritage preservation program. Detailed signage and maintained pathways make the site accessible to visitors. Additional resources include a pamphlet published by the Utsunomiya City Board of Education and historical survey reports, which are available online. --- == Related Sites and Resources == - **Sasazuka Kofun**: Another notable tumulus in Tochigi Prefecture. - **Tochigi Prefectural Comprehensive Sports Park**: A nearby recreational facility. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳}} and part of the {{ill|Tsukayama Kofun Cluster|ja|塚山古墳群}}. It has been designated as a Tochigi Prefecture-designated historical site. This article also covers the {{ill|Tsukayama Kofun Cluster|ja|塚山古墳群}}, for which Tsukayama Kofun serves as the main mound. == Overview == [[File:100425 Tsukayama Kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|{{center|Aerial view of the Tsukayama Kofun Cluster (2010)}}{{small|Top right: Tsukayama Kofun; Left: Tsukayama West Kofun; Bottom left: Tsukayama South Kofun. {{ill|Aerial photographs of Japan|ja|国土航空写真}}.}}]] Located in southern Tochigi Prefecture, the mound was constructed on a plateau between the {{ill|Tagawa River (Tone River System)|ja|田川 (利根川水系)}} and {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}}. It is the largest keyhole-shaped kofun in the Tsukayama Kofun Cluster, which includes several mounds such as the scallop-shaped Tsukayama West and South Kofun, as well as {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}}-based coffins. The rear circular section has been partially leveled by road construction. In 1989 (Heisei 1), a survey was conducted, followed by four excavation campaigns from 1989 to 1991. The mound has a "Kenbishi-style" keyhole shape with a protruding front section oriented westward. It is constructed in three tiers, with external surfaces featuring {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}}. Cylindrical {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}}, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}} (TK216-208 style), and {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}} have been excavated. The southern neck of the mound features a {{ill|tsukuridashi|ja|造出}}, and the shield-shaped moat surrounding the mound brings the total length to 119.2 meters. The burial facility remains unexamined, and grave goods are largely unknown. The mound is estimated to date from the mid-5th century, during the middle {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} (or the late 5th century, according to other estimates). It served as a prominent burial site for regional leaders in the southern Utsunomiya area and is considered critical for studying the political dynamics of the {{ill|Shimotsukeno region|ja|下毛野地方}}. The site was designated as a Tochigi Prefecture historical site in 1953 (Shōwa 28). Today, the mound is adorned with {{ill|Dodantsutsuji shrubs|ja|ドウダンツツジ}}, offering a unique landscape that has been developed for preservation. == Historical Timeline == 1. **1953 (Showa 28)**: Tsukayama Kofun designated a Tochigi Prefectural Historic Site. 2. **1966 (Showa 41)**: Plans for a new highway led to design changes to protect the kofun group, including the construction of a tunnel nearby. 3. **1973 (Showa 48)**: Tsukayama Nishi Kofun and Tsukayama Minami Kofun were also designated as historic sites. 4. **1989–1991**: Excavation surveys were conducted by the Utsunomiya University Archaeology Research Association. Further excavations and preservation efforts continued through the 1990s. 5. **2005 (Heisei 17)**: Artifacts from Tsukayama Minami Kofun were designated as tangible cultural properties by Utsunomiya City. --- == Mound Specifications == - **Overall Length (with Moat)**: 119.2 meters - **Mound Length**: 98.3 meters - **Rear Circular Section**: Diameter 55.9 meters - **Front Rectangular Section**: Width 59.9 meters Images of the tumulus and surrounding moat show its well-preserved features, including a clear distinction between the front and rear sections. --- == Tsukayama Kofun Group == The **Tsukayama Kofun Group** comprises several tumuli surrounding the Tsukayama Kofun. At its peak, the group included more than ten burial mounds, though many have since been lost. Today, notable surviving mounds include: 1. **Tsukayama Kofun (Main Tumulus)**: - Keyhole-shaped (*zenpō-kōen-fun*) - Length: 98.3 meters - Artifacts: *Haniwa* and *Sue ware* - Age: Mid-5th century - Designated a prefectural historic site in 1953. 2. **Tsukayama Nishi Kofun**: - Shell-shaped (*hotategai*) - Length: 63.1 meters - Artifacts: *Haniwa* and *Sue ware* - Age: Late 5th century - Designated a prefectural historic site in 1973. 3. **Tsukayama Minami Kofun**: - Shell-shaped (*hotategai*) - Length: 58 meters - Artifacts: Cylindrical and figurative *haniwa* (horses, deer, houses) and pottery (*Sue ware* and *haji ware*) - Age: Late 5th to early 6th century - Designated a prefectural historic site in 1973. Other smaller tumuli include: - **6th Tumulus**: A small round burial mound, 20 meters in diameter, with *haniwa* remains. - **Disappeared Mounds**: Several smaller round burial mounds and *haniwa* caskets were lost to development. --- == Cultural Artifacts and Significance == Artifacts from the group, including cylindrical and decorative *haniwa*, highlight the sophisticated burial practices of the Kofun period. Of particular note are engravings on a *haniwa* casket, depicting alternating male and female deer—symbolic of fertility and vitality. The group offers valuable insights into the sociopolitical landscape of the Shimotsuke region, reflecting its transition during the Kofun period. --- == Conservation and Visitor Information == The **Tsukayama Kofun Group** is part of Utsunomiya's cultural heritage preservation program. Detailed signage and maintained pathways make the site accessible to visitors. Additional resources include a pamphlet published by the Utsunomiya City Board of Education and historical survey reports, which are available online. --- == Related Sites and Resources == - **Sasazuka Kofun**: Another notable tumulus in Tochigi Prefecture. - **Tochigi Prefectural Comprehensive Sports Park**: A nearby recreational facility. External links: - [Tsukayama Kofun (Tochigi Education Board)](http://www.tochigi-edu.ed.jp) - [Utsunomiya Cultural Heritage Website](https://utsunomiya-8story.jp) == Cultural Properties == === Tochigi Prefectural Cultural Properties === * Historic Sites ** {{ill|Tsukayama Kofun|ja|塚山古墳}} - Designated on November 10, 1953 (Showa 28).[http://www.tochigi-edu.ed.jp/center/bunkazai/2341001.htm 塚山古墳] (Cultural Property Section, Tochigi Prefectural Board of Education).[https://utsunomiya-8story.jp/search_post/%e5%a1%9a%e5%b1%b1%e5%8f%a4%e5%a2%b3/ 塚山古墳] (Utsunomiya Historical and Cultural Resources Promotion Council). ** {{ill|Tsukayama Nishi Kofun|ja|塚山西古墳}} - Designated on April 13, 1973 (Showa 48).[http://www.tochigi-edu.ed.jp/center/bunkazai/2341039.htm 塚山西古墳] (Cultural Property Section, Tochigi Prefectural Board of Education).[https://utsunomiya-8story.jp/search_post/%e5%a1%9a%e5%b1%b1%e8%a5%bf%e5%8f%a4%e5%a2%b3/ 塚山西古墳] (Utsunomiya Historical and Cultural Resources Promotion Council). ** {{ill|Tsukayama Minami Kofun|ja|塚山南古墳}} - Designated on April 13, 1973 (Showa 48).[http://www.tochigi-edu.ed.jp/center/bunkazai/2341040.htm 塚山南古墳] (Cultural Property Section, Tochigi Prefectural Board of Education).[https://utsunomiya-8story.jp/search_post/%e5%a1%9a%e5%b1%b1%e5%8d%97%e5%8f%a4%e5%a2%b3/ 塚山南古墳] (Utsunomiya Historical and Cultural Resources Promotion Council). === Utsunomiya City Designated Cultural Properties === * Tangible Cultural Properties ** Artifacts excavated from {{ill|Tsukayama Minami Kofun|ja|塚山南古墳}} (archaeological materials) - Designated on November 7, 2005 (Heisei 17). {{Japanese Ancient Tombs | Name = Tsukayama Kofun | Image = [[File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), funkyu-2.jpg|280px]]
Mound (Right: front section; Left-back: rear circular section) | Alternate Name = Hyōgo-zuka Kofun | Group = Tsukayama Kofun Cluster | Location = Nishikawada-machi 7-chome, {{ill|Utsunomiya City|ja|宇都宮市}}, Tochigi Prefecture | Coordinates = {{Coord|36|30|22.05|N|139|51|39.50|E|region:JP-09_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Tsukayama Kofun}} | Shape = {{ill|Keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳}} (Kenbishi-style) | Dimensions = Total mound length: 98.3 meters | Burial Facility = Unknown | Artifacts = {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}}, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}} | Burial Mounds = | Construction Era = Mid-5th century | Buried Figure = | Mausoleum = | Historical Site = Tochigi Prefecture-designated Historical Site (Tsukayama Kofun) | Cultural Asset = | Notes = | Map2 = {{Location map|Japan Tochigi|label=Tsukayama Kofun|lat_deg=36|lat_min=30|lat_sec=22.05|lon_deg=139|lon_min=51|lon_sec=39.5|mark=前方後円墳-西南西.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=top|width=200|caption=}} }} {{OSM Location map | coord = {{Coord|36|30|20|N|139|51|38|E}} | zoom = 17 | float = right | width = 300 | height = 250 | caption = {{center|Distribution map of the Tsukayama Kofun Cluster}} | scalemark = 60 | mark-coord1 = {{Coord|36|30|22.05|N|139|51|39.50|E}} | label1 = Tsukayama Kofun | label-pos1 = top | label-color1 = black | mark1 = 前方後円墳-西南西.svg | mark-size1 = 70 | mark-coord2 = {{Coord|36|30|20.25|N|139|51|36.35|E}} | label2 = Tsukayama West Kofun | label-pos2 = top | label-color2 = black | mark2 = 帆立貝形古墳-南南東.svg | mark-size2 = 60 | mark-coord3 = {{Coord|36|30|17.93|N|139|51|37.23|E}} | label3 = Tsukayama South Kofun | label-pos3 = left | label-color3 = black | mark3 = 帆立貝形古墳-南.svg | mark-size3 = 60 }} '''Tsukayama Kofun''' (塚山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in Nishikawada-machi, {{ill|Utsunomiya City|ja|宇都宮市}}, Tochigi Prefecture. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳}} and part of the {{ill|Tsukayama Kofun Cluster|ja|塚山古墳群}}. It has been designated as a Tochigi Prefecture-designated historical site. This article also covers the {{ill|Tsukayama Kofun Cluster|ja|塚山古墳群}}, for which Tsukayama Kofun serves as the main mound. [[ja:塚山古墳 (宇都宮市)]] == Overview == [[File:100425 Tsukayama Kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|{{center|Aerial view of the Tsukayama Kofun Cluster (2010)}}{{small|Top right: Tsukayama Kofun; Left: Tsukayama West Kofun; Bottom left: Tsukayama South Kofun. {{ill|Aerial photographs of Japan|ja|国土航空写真}}.}}]] Located in southern Tochigi Prefecture, the mound was constructed on a plateau between the {{ill|Tagawa River (Tone River System)|ja|田川 (利根川水系)}} and {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}}. It is the largest keyhole-shaped kofun in the Tsukayama Kofun Cluster, which includes several mounds such as the scallop-shaped Tsukayama West and South Kofun, as well as {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}}-based coffins. The rear circular section has been partially leveled by road construction. In 1989 (Heisei 1), a survey was conducted, followed by four excavation campaigns from 1989 to 1991. The mound has a "Kenbishi-style" keyhole shape with a protruding front section oriented westward. It is constructed in three tiers, with external surfaces featuring {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}}. Cylindrical {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}}, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}} (TK216-208 style), and {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}} have been excavated. The southern neck of the mound features a {{ill|tsukuridashi|ja|造出}}, and the shield-shaped moat surrounding the mound brings the total length to 119.2 meters. The burial facility remains unexamined, and grave goods are largely unknown. The mound is estimated to date from the mid-5th century, during the middle {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} (or the late 5th century, according to other estimates). It served as a prominent burial site for regional leaders in the southern Utsunomiya area and is considered critical for studying the political dynamics of the {{ill|Shimotsukeno region|ja|下毛野地方}}. The site was designated as a Tochigi Prefecture historical site in 1953 (Shōwa 28). Today, the mound is adorned with {{ill|Dodantsutsuji shrubs|ja|ドウダンツツジ}}, offering a unique landscape that has been developed for preservation. == Ruins History == * [[1953]] (Showa 28), November 10: Tsukayama Kofun was designated as a historic site by Tochigi Prefecture. * [[1966]] (Showa 41): Construction planning for [[National Route 121]] (part of the [[Utsunomiya Ring Road]]) began. The plans were revised to include a tunnel near the kofun group to protect cultural properties. * [[1973]] (Showa 48), April 13: Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun were designated as historic sites by Tochigi Prefecture. * [[1976]] (Showa 51): Excavations of Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama East Kofun were conducted due to road construction (reported by the Tochigi Prefectural Board of Education in [[1979]]). * [[1989]]-[[1991]] (Heisei 1-3): Excavations of Tsukayama Kofun were carried out by the Archaeological Research Society of [[Utsunomiya University]] (findings published in [[1995]]). * [[1991]]-[[1992]] (Heisei 3-4): Excavations of the Tsukayama Kofun Group were conducted during road improvement work by the Utsunomiya City Board of Education (findings published in [[1996]]). * [[1995]]-[[1997]] (Heisei 7-9): Excavations of Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun were carried out for historic site conservation by the Utsunomiya City Board of Education, Utsunomiya University, and [[Utsunomiya Bunsei Junior College]] (findings published in [[2003]]). * [[2005]] (Heisei 17), November 7: Artifacts excavated from Tsukayama South Kofun were designated as tangible cultural properties by Utsunomiya City. [[Category:Kofun in Japan]] [[ja:塚山古墳群の歴史]] == Mound Specifications == - **Overall Length (with Moat)**: 119.2 meters - **Mound Length**: 98.3 meters - **Rear Circular Section**: Diameter 55.9 meters - **Front Rectangular Section**: Width 59.9 meters Images of the tumulus and surrounding moat show its well-preserved features, including a clear distinction between the front and rear sections. --- == Tsukayama Kofun Group == The **Tsukayama Kofun Group** comprises several tumuli surrounding the Tsukayama Kofun. At its peak, the group included more than ten burial mounds, though many have since been lost. Today, notable surviving mounds include: 1. **Tsukayama Kofun (Main Tumulus)**: - Keyhole-shaped (*zenpō-kōen-fun*) - Length: 98.3 meters - Artifacts: *Haniwa* and *Sue ware* - Age: Mid-5th century - Designated a prefectural historic site in 1953. 2. **Tsukayama Nishi Kofun**: - Shell-shaped (*hotategai*) - Length: 63.1 meters - Artifacts: *Haniwa* and *Sue ware* - Age: Late 5th century - Designated a prefectural historic site in 1973. 3. **Tsukayama Minami Kofun**: - Shell-shaped (*hotategai*) - Length: 58 meters - Artifacts: Cylindrical and figurative *haniwa* (horses, deer, houses) and pottery (*Sue ware* and *haji ware*) - Age: Late 5th to early 6th century - Designated a prefectural historic site in 1973. Other smaller tumuli include: - **6th Tumulus**: A small round burial mound, 20 meters in diameter, with *haniwa* remains. - **Disappeared Mounds**: Several smaller round burial mounds and *haniwa* caskets were lost to development. --- == Cultural Artifacts and Significance == Artifacts from the group, including cylindrical and decorative *haniwa*, highlight the sophisticated burial practices of the Kofun period. Of particular note are engravings on a *haniwa* casket, depicting alternating male and female deer—symbolic of fertility and vitality. The group offers valuable insights into the sociopolitical landscape of the Shimotsuke region, reflecting its transition during the Kofun period. --- == Conservation and Visitor Information == The **Tsukayama Kofun Group** is part of Utsunomiya's cultural heritage preservation program. Detailed signage and maintained pathways make the site accessible to visitors. Additional resources include a pamphlet published by the Utsunomiya City Board of Education and historical survey reports, which are available online. --- == Related Sites and Resources == - **Sasazuka Kofun**: Another notable tumulus in Tochigi Prefecture. - **Tochigi Prefectural Comprehensive Sports Park**: A nearby recreational facility. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳}} and part of the {{ill|Tsukayama Kofun Cluster|ja|塚山古墳群}}. It has been designated as a Tochigi Prefecture-designated historical site. This article also covers the {{ill|Tsukayama Kofun Cluster|ja|塚山古墳群}}, for which Tsukayama Kofun serves as the main mound. [[ja:塚山古墳 (宇都宮市)]] == Overview == [[File:100425 Tsukayama Kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|{{center|Aerial view of the Tsukayama Kofun Cluster (2010)}}{{small|Top right: Tsukayama Kofun; Left: Tsukayama West Kofun; Bottom left: Tsukayama South Kofun. {{ill|Aerial photographs of Japan|ja|国土航空写真}}.}}]] Located in southern Tochigi Prefecture, the mound was constructed on a plateau between the {{ill|Tagawa River (Tone River System)|ja|田川 (利根川水系)}} and {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}}. It is the largest keyhole-shaped kofun in the Tsukayama Kofun Cluster, which includes several mounds such as the scallop-shaped Tsukayama West and South Kofun, as well as {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}}-based coffins. The rear circular section has been partially leveled by road construction. In 1989 (Heisei 1), a survey was conducted, followed by four excavation campaigns from 1989 to 1991. The mound has a "Kenbishi-style" keyhole shape with a protruding front section oriented westward. It is constructed in three tiers, with external surfaces featuring {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}}. Cylindrical {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}}, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}} (TK216-208 style), and {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}} have been excavated. The southern neck of the mound features a {{ill|tsukuridashi|ja|造出}}, and the shield-shaped moat surrounding the mound brings the total length to 119.2 meters. The burial facility remains unexamined, and grave goods are largely unknown. The mound is estimated to date from the mid-5th century, during the middle {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} (or the late 5th century, according to other estimates). It served as a prominent burial site for regional leaders in the southern Utsunomiya area and is considered critical for studying the political dynamics of the {{ill|Shimotsukeno region|ja|下毛野地方}}. The site was designated as a Tochigi Prefecture historical site in 1953 (Shōwa 28). Today, the mound is adorned with {{ill|Dodantsutsuji shrubs|ja|ドウダンツツジ}}, offering a unique landscape that has been developed for preservation. == Ruins History == * [[1953]] (Showa 28), November 10: Tsukayama Kofun was designated as a historic site by Tochigi Prefecture. * [[1966]] (Showa 41): Construction planning for [[National Route 121]] (part of the [[Utsunomiya Ring Road]]) began. The plans were revised to include a tunnel near the kofun group to protect cultural properties. * [[1973]] (Showa 48), April 13: Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun were designated as historic sites by Tochigi Prefecture. * [[1976]] (Showa 51): Excavations of Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama East Kofun were conducted due to road construction (reported by the Tochigi Prefectural Board of Education in [[1979]]). * [[1989]]-[[1991]] (Heisei 1-3): Excavations of Tsukayama Kofun were carried out by the Archaeological Research Society of [[Utsunomiya University]] (findings published in [[1995]]). * [[1991]]-[[1992]] (Heisei 3-4): Excavations of the Tsukayama Kofun Group were conducted during road improvement work by the Utsunomiya City Board of Education (findings published in [[1996]]). * [[1995]]-[[1997]] (Heisei 7-9): Excavations of Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun were carried out for historic site conservation by the Utsunomiya City Board of Education, Utsunomiya University, and [[Utsunomiya Bunsei Junior College]] (findings published in [[2003]]). * [[2005]] (Heisei 17), November 7: Artifacts excavated from Tsukayama South Kofun were designated as tangible cultural properties by Utsunomiya City. [[Category:Kofun in Japan]] [[ja:塚山古墳群の歴史]] == Mound == The dimensions of the mound are as follows{{Sfn|Tsukayama Kofun Group (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}: * Total Kofun Length: 119.2 meters - The overall length of the kofun, including the surrounding moat. * Mound Length: 98.3 meters * Rear Circular Section Diameter: 55.9 meters * Front Section Width: 59.9 meters File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), funkyu-4.jpg|Mound and surrounding moat. [[Category:Kofun in Japan]] [[ja:塚山古墳群の墳丘]] == Tsukayama Kofun Group == The **Tsukayama Kofun Group** comprises several tumuli surrounding the Tsukayama Kofun. At its peak, the group included more than ten burial mounds, though many have since been lost. Today, notable surviving mounds include: 1. **Tsukayama Kofun (Main Tumulus)**: - Keyhole-shaped (*zenpō-kōen-fun*) - Length: 98.3 meters - Artifacts: *Haniwa* and *Sue ware* - Age: Mid-5th century - Designated a prefectural historic site in 1953. 2. **Tsukayama Nishi Kofun**: - Shell-shaped (*hotategai*) - Length: 63.1 meters - Artifacts: *Haniwa* and *Sue ware* - Age: Late 5th century - Designated a prefectural historic site in 1973. 3. **Tsukayama Minami Kofun**: - Shell-shaped (*hotategai*) - Length: 58 meters - Artifacts: Cylindrical and figurative *haniwa* (horses, deer, houses) and pottery (*Sue ware* and *haji ware*) - Age: Late 5th to early 6th century - Designated a prefectural historic site in 1973. Other smaller tumuli include: - **6th Tumulus**: A small round burial mound, 20 meters in diameter, with *haniwa* remains. - **Disappeared Mounds**: Several smaller round burial mounds and *haniwa* caskets were lost to development. --- == Cultural Artifacts and Significance == Artifacts from the group, including cylindrical and decorative *haniwa*, highlight the sophisticated burial practices of the Kofun period. Of particular note are engravings on a *haniwa* casket, depicting alternating male and female deer—symbolic of fertility and vitality. The group offers valuable insights into the sociopolitical landscape of the Shimotsuke region, reflecting its transition during the Kofun period. --- == Conservation and Visitor Information == The **Tsukayama Kofun Group** is part of Utsunomiya's cultural heritage preservation program. Detailed signage and maintained pathways make the site accessible to visitors. Additional resources include a pamphlet published by the Utsunomiya City Board of Education and historical survey reports, which are available online. --- == Related Sites and Resources == - **Sasazuka Kofun**: Another notable tumulus in Tochigi Prefecture. - **Tochigi Prefectural Comprehensive Sports Park**: A nearby recreational facility. [[Category:Kofun in Japan]] [[ja:塚山古墳群の歴史]] == Mound == The dimensions of the mound are as follows{{Sfn|Tsukayama Kofun Group (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}: * Total Kofun Length: 119.2 meters - The overall length of the kofun, including the surrounding moat. * Mound Length: 98.3 meters * Rear Circular Section Diameter: 55.9 meters * Front Section Width: 59.9 meters File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), funkyu-4.jpg|Mound and surrounding moat. [[Category:Kofun in Japan]] [[ja:塚山古墳群の墳丘]] == Tsukayama Kofun Group == The '''Tsukayama Kofun Group''' consists of a cluster of kofun (ancient burial mounds) with Tsukayama Kofun as the main mound. Originally composed of over 10 kofun, it currently includes one [[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped kofun]] (Tsukayama Kofun), two [[Scallop-shaped kofun|scallop-shaped kofun]] (Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun), and one round kofun (No. 6 Kofun). Investigations have identified six small round kofun (Nos. 4, 5, 7, 8, and two within the old shooting range) to the north of Tsukayama Kofun. To the west and southwest, from north to south, lie a mid-sized round kofun (No. 6), Tsukayama West Kofun, and Tsukayama South Kofun. Haniwa sarcophagi have also been discovered in the area, with one featuring an engraved depiction of four deer in alternating male and female pairs. The construction period is estimated to span the mid-5th century to the early 6th century during the mid- to late-Kofun period, following the [[Mobara Kofun Group]] and the {{ill|Higashitani Kofun Group|ja|東谷古墳群}}. Mound (rear circular section in the center, front section in the background) |Alias = |Location = [[Tochigi Prefecture|Tochigi]], [[Utsunomiya]] Nishikawada Town Higashihara |Shape = [[Scallop-shaped kofun]] |Size = Mound length: 63.1 m
Height: 6.7 m (rear section) |Burial Facility = Unknown |Artifacts Found = [[Haniwa]], [[Sue ware]] |Construction Period = [[5th century]] late |Historic Site Designation = Prefectural Historic Site: "Tsukayama West Kofun" |Special Notes = }} '''Tsukayama West Kofun''' (塚山西古墳) is a kofun located southwest of Tsukayama Kofun. It is [[Scallop-shaped kofun|scallop-shaped]] and designated as a historic site by Tochigi Prefecture. The mound has a short front section and a rear circular section, oriented to the south-southeast. The dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}: * Total Kofun Length: 74.1 meters (including moat). * Mound Length: 63.1 meters. * Rear Circular Section ** Diameter: 44.5 meters ** Height: 6.7 meters * Front Section ** Length: ~18 meters ** Width: ~22 meters ** Height: ~1.5 meters The mound comprises two or more tiers (upper tiers heavily disturbed){{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. Cylindrical haniwa and Sue ware (TK208-TK23 styles) were found on the mound's surface{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. A horseshoe-shaped moat surrounds the mound (shallow on the east side due to proximity to Tsukayama Kofun){{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. Burial facilities are unknown due to limited findings; no clay or stone structures have been detected{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. The construction period is estimated to be the late 5th century, following Tsukayama Kofun and preceding Tsukayama South Kofun{{Sfn|Tsukayama Kofun Group (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}. === Tsukayama South Kofun === {{Japan kofun |Name = Tsukayama South Kofun |Image = [[File:Tsukayama Minami Kofun (Utsunomiya), funkyu-2.jpg|280px]]
Mound (rear circular section in the center, front section in the background) |Alias = |Location = [[Tochigi Prefecture|Tochigi]], [[Utsunomiya]] Nishikawada Town Higashihara |Shape = [[Scallop-shaped kofun]] |Size = Mound length: 58 m
Height: 6.8 m (rear section) |Burial Facility = Unknown |Artifacts Found = [[Haniwa]], [[Sue ware]], [[Haji ware]] |Construction Period = [[5th century]] late |Historic Site Designation = Prefectural Historic Site: "Tsukayama South Kofun" |Special Notes = Excavated artifacts designated as cultural properties of Utsunomiya City }} '''Tsukayama South Kofun''' (塚山南古墳) is a kofun located south of Tsukayama West Kofun. It is [[Scallop-shaped kofun|scallop-shaped]] and designated as a historic site by Tochigi Prefecture. The mound has a short front section and a rear circular section, oriented southward. The dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}: * Total Kofun Length: 70.6 meters (including moat). * Mound Length: 58.0 meters. * Rear Circular Section ** Diameter: 42.1 meters ** Height: 6.8 meters * Front Section ** Length: 13.5 meters ** Height: 4.1 meters The mound is two-tiered{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. Numerous artifacts, including cylindrical haniwa, figurative haniwa (human, horse, deer, and house shapes), large Sue ware vessels, and Haji ware, were recovered, though no evidence of surface stones was found{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. A horseshoe-shaped moat surrounds the mound (narrower on the northwest side due to proximity to Tsukayama West Kofun){{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. Burial facilities have not been fully investigated, but depressions and red-painted stones suggest a vertical burial system at the mound's summit, likely plundered{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. The construction period is estimated to be the late 5th century to early 6th century, following Tsukayama West Kofun{{Sfn|Tsukayama Kofun Group (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}. [[Category:Kofun in Japan]] [[ja:塚山古墳群]] == Cultural Artifacts and Significance == Artifacts from the group, including cylindrical and decorative *haniwa*, highlight the sophisticated burial practices of the Kofun period. Of particular note are engravings on a *haniwa* casket, depicting alternating male and female deer—symbolic of fertility and vitality. The group offers valuable insights into the sociopolitical landscape of the Shimotsuke region, reflecting its transition during the Kofun period. --- == Conservation and Visitor Information == The **Tsukayama Kofun Group** is part of Utsunomiya's cultural heritage preservation program. Detailed signage and maintained pathways make the site accessible to visitors. Additional resources include a pamphlet published by the Utsunomiya City Board of Education and historical survey reports, which are available online. --- == Related Sites and Resources == - **Sasazuka Kofun**: Another notable tumulus in Tochigi Prefecture. - **Tochigi Prefectural Comprehensive Sports Park**: A nearby recreational facility. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳}} and part of the {{ill|Tsukayama Kofun Cluster|ja|塚山古墳群}}. It has been designated as a Tochigi Prefecture-designated historical site. This article also covers the {{ill|Tsukayama Kofun Cluster|ja|塚山古墳群}}, for which Tsukayama Kofun serves as the main mound. [[ja:塚山古墳 (宇都宮市)]] == Overview == [[File:100425 Tsukayama Kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|{{center|Aerial view of the Tsukayama Kofun Cluster (2010)}}{{small|Top right: Tsukayama Kofun; Left: Tsukayama West Kofun; Bottom left: Tsukayama South Kofun. {{ill|Aerial photographs of Japan|ja|国土航空写真}}.}}]] Located in southern Tochigi Prefecture, the mound was constructed on a plateau between the {{ill|Tagawa River (Tone River System)|ja|田川 (利根川水系)}} and {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}}. It is the largest keyhole-shaped kofun in the Tsukayama Kofun Cluster, which includes several mounds such as the scallop-shaped Tsukayama West and South Kofun, as well as {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}}-based coffins. The rear circular section has been partially leveled by road construction. In 1989 (Heisei 1), a survey was conducted, followed by four excavation campaigns from 1989 to 1991. The mound has a "Kenbishi-style" keyhole shape with a protruding front section oriented westward. It is constructed in three tiers, with external surfaces featuring {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}}. Cylindrical {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}}, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}} (TK216-208 style), and {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}} have been excavated. The southern neck of the mound features a {{ill|tsukuridashi|ja|造出}}, and the shield-shaped moat surrounding the mound brings the total length to 119.2 meters. The burial facility remains unexamined, and grave goods are largely unknown. The mound is estimated to date from the mid-5th century, during the middle {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} (or the late 5th century, according to other estimates). It served as a prominent burial site for regional leaders in the southern Utsunomiya area and is considered critical for studying the political dynamics of the {{ill|Shimotsukeno region|ja|下毛野地方}}. The site was designated as a Tochigi Prefecture historical site in 1953 (Shōwa 28). Today, the mound is adorned with {{ill|Dodantsutsuji shrubs|ja|ドウダンツツジ}}, offering a unique landscape that has been developed for preservation. == Ruins History == * [[1953]] (Showa 28), November 10: Tsukayama Kofun was designated as a historic site by Tochigi Prefecture. * [[1966]] (Showa 41): Construction planning for [[National Route 121]] (part of the [[Utsunomiya Ring Road]]) began. The plans were revised to include a tunnel near the kofun group to protect cultural properties. * [[1973]] (Showa 48), April 13: Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun were designated as historic sites by Tochigi Prefecture. * [[1976]] (Showa 51): Excavations of Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama East Kofun were conducted due to road construction (reported by the Tochigi Prefectural Board of Education in [[1979]]). * [[1989]]-[[1991]] (Heisei 1-3): Excavations of Tsukayama Kofun were carried out by the Archaeological Research Society of [[Utsunomiya University]] (findings published in [[1995]]). * [[1991]]-[[1992]] (Heisei 3-4): Excavations of the Tsukayama Kofun Group were conducted during road improvement work by the Utsunomiya City Board of Education (findings published in [[1996]]). * [[1995]]-[[1997]] (Heisei 7-9): Excavations of Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun were carried out for historic site conservation by the Utsunomiya City Board of Education, Utsunomiya University, and [[Utsunomiya Bunsei Junior College]] (findings published in [[2003]]). * [[2005]] (Heisei 17), November 7: Artifacts excavated from Tsukayama South Kofun were designated as tangible cultural properties by Utsunomiya City. [[Category:Kofun in Japan]] [[ja:塚山古墳群の歴史]] == Mound == The dimensions of the mound are as follows{{Sfn|Tsukayama Kofun Group (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}: * Total Kofun Length: 119.2 meters - The overall length of the kofun, including the surrounding moat. * Mound Length: 98.3 meters * Rear Circular Section Diameter: 55.9 meters * Front Section Width: 59.9 meters File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), funkyu-4.jpg|Mound and surrounding moat. [[Category:Kofun in Japan]] [[ja:塚山古墳群の墳丘]] == Tsukayama Kofun Group == The '''Tsukayama Kofun Group''' consists of a cluster of kofun (ancient burial mounds) with Tsukayama Kofun as the main mound. Originally composed of over 10 kofun, it currently includes one [[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped kofun]] (Tsukayama Kofun), two [[Scallop-shaped kofun|scallop-shaped kofun]] (Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun), and one round kofun (No. 6 Kofun). Investigations have identified six small round kofun (Nos. 4, 5, 7, 8, and two within the old shooting range) to the north of Tsukayama Kofun. To the west and southwest, from north to south, lie a mid-sized round kofun (No. 6), Tsukayama West Kofun, and Tsukayama South Kofun. Haniwa sarcophagi have also been discovered in the area, with one featuring an engraved depiction of four deer in alternating male and female pairs. The construction period is estimated to span the mid-5th century to the early 6th century during the mid- to late-Kofun period, following the [[Mobara Kofun Group]] and the {{ill|Higashitani Kofun Group|ja|東谷古墳群}}. Mound (rear circular section in the center, front section in the background) |Alias = |Location = [[Tochigi Prefecture|Tochigi]], [[Utsunomiya]] Nishikawada Town Higashihara |Shape = [[Scallop-shaped kofun]] |Size = Mound length: 63.1 m
Height: 6.7 m (rear section) |Burial Facility = Unknown |Artifacts Found = [[Haniwa]], [[Sue ware]] |Construction Period = [[5th century]] late |Historic Site Designation = Prefectural Historic Site: "Tsukayama West Kofun" |Special Notes = }} '''Tsukayama West Kofun''' (塚山西古墳) is a kofun located southwest of Tsukayama Kofun. It is [[Scallop-shaped kofun|scallop-shaped]] and designated as a historic site by Tochigi Prefecture. The mound has a short front section and a rear circular section, oriented to the south-southeast. The dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}: * Total Kofun Length: 74.1 meters (including moat). * Mound Length: 63.1 meters. * Rear Circular Section ** Diameter: 44.5 meters ** Height: 6.7 meters * Front Section ** Length: ~18 meters ** Width: ~22 meters ** Height: ~1.5 meters The mound comprises two or more tiers (upper tiers heavily disturbed){{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. Cylindrical haniwa and Sue ware (TK208-TK23 styles) were found on the mound's surface{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. A horseshoe-shaped moat surrounds the mound (shallow on the east side due to proximity to Tsukayama Kofun){{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. Burial facilities are unknown due to limited findings; no clay or stone structures have been detected{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. The construction period is estimated to be the late 5th century, following Tsukayama Kofun and preceding Tsukayama South Kofun{{Sfn|Tsukayama Kofun Group (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}. === Tsukayama South Kofun === {{Japan kofun |Name = Tsukayama South Kofun |Image = [[File:Tsukayama Minami Kofun (Utsunomiya), funkyu-2.jpg|280px]]
Mound (rear circular section in the center, front section in the background) |Alias = |Location = [[Tochigi Prefecture|Tochigi]], [[Utsunomiya]] Nishikawada Town Higashihara |Shape = [[Scallop-shaped kofun]] |Size = Mound length: 58 m
Height: 6.8 m (rear section) |Burial Facility = Unknown |Artifacts Found = [[Haniwa]], [[Sue ware]], [[Haji ware]] |Construction Period = [[5th century]] late |Historic Site Designation = Prefectural Historic Site: "Tsukayama South Kofun" |Special Notes = Excavated artifacts designated as cultural properties of Utsunomiya City }} '''Tsukayama South Kofun''' (塚山南古墳) is a kofun located south of Tsukayama West Kofun. It is [[Scallop-shaped kofun|scallop-shaped]] and designated as a historic site by Tochigi Prefecture. The mound has a short front section and a rear circular section, oriented southward. The dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}: * Total Kofun Length: 70.6 meters (including moat). * Mound Length: 58.0 meters. * Rear Circular Section ** Diameter: 42.1 meters ** Height: 6.8 meters * Front Section ** Length: 13.5 meters ** Height: 4.1 meters The mound is two-tiered{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. Numerous artifacts, including cylindrical haniwa, figurative haniwa (human, horse, deer, and house shapes), large Sue ware vessels, and Haji ware, were recovered, though no evidence of surface stones was found{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. A horseshoe-shaped moat surrounds the mound (narrower on the northwest side due to proximity to Tsukayama West Kofun){{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. Burial facilities have not been fully investigated, but depressions and red-painted stones suggest a vertical burial system at the mound's summit, likely plundered{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. [[Category:Kofun in Japan]] [[ja:塚山古墳群]] The construction period is estimated to be the late 5th century to early 6th century, following Tsukayama West Kofun{{Sfn|Tsukayama Kofun Group (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}. == Cultural Properties == === Tochigi Prefectural Cultural Properties === * Historic Sites ** {{ill|Tsukayama Kofun|ja|塚山古墳}} - Designated on November 10, 1953 (Showa 28).[http://www.tochigi-edu.ed.jp/center/bunkazai/2341001.htm 塚山古墳] (Cultural Property Section, Tochigi Prefectural Board of Education).[https://utsunomiya-8story.jp/search_post/%e5%a1%9a%e5%b1%b1%e5%8f%a4%e5%a2%b3/ 塚山古墳] (Utsunomiya Historical and Cultural Resources Promotion Council). ** {{ill|Tsukayama Nishi Kofun|ja|塚山西古墳}} - Designated on April 13, 1973 (Showa 48).[http://www.tochigi-edu.ed.jp/center/bunkazai/2341039.htm 塚山西古墳] (Cultural Property Section, Tochigi Prefectural Board of Education).[https://utsunomiya-8story.jp/search_post/%e5%a1%9a%e5%b1%b1%e8%a5%bf%e5%8f%a4%e5%a2%b3/ 塚山西古墳] (Utsunomiya Historical and Cultural Resources Promotion Council). ** {{ill|Tsukayama Minami Kofun|ja|塚山南古墳}} - Designated on April 13, 1973 (Showa 48).[http://www.tochigi-edu.ed.jp/center/bunkazai/2341040.htm 塚山南古墳] (Cultural Property Section, Tochigi Prefectural Board of Education).[https://utsunomiya-8story.jp/search_post/%e5%a1%9a%e5%b1%b1%e5%8d%97%e5%8f%a4%e5%a2%b3/ 塚山南古墳] (Utsunomiya Historical and Cultural Resources Promotion Council). === Utsunomiya City Designated Cultural Properties === * Tangible Cultural Properties ** Artifacts excavated from {{ill|Tsukayama Minami Kofun|ja|塚山南古墳}} (archaeological materials) - Designated on November 7, 2005 (Heisei 17). It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳}} and part of the {{ill|Tsukayama Kofun Cluster|ja|塚山古墳群}}. It has been designated as a Tochigi Prefecture-designated historical site. This article also covers the {{ill|Tsukayama Kofun Cluster|ja|塚山古墳群}}, for which Tsukayama Kofun serves as the main mound. [[ja:塚山古墳 (宇都宮市)]] == Overview == [[File:100425 Tsukayama Kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|{{center|Aerial view of the Tsukayama Kofun Cluster (2010)}}{{small|Top right: Tsukayama Kofun; Left: Tsukayama West Kofun; Bottom left: Tsukayama South Kofun. {{ill|Aerial photographs of Japan|ja|国土航空写真}}.}}]] Located in southern Tochigi Prefecture, the mound was constructed on a plateau between the {{ill|Tagawa River (Tone River System)|ja|田川 (利根川水系)}} and {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}}. It is the largest keyhole-shaped kofun in the Tsukayama Kofun Cluster, which includes several mounds such as the scallop-shaped Tsukayama West and South Kofun, as well as {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}}-based coffins. The rear circular section has been partially leveled by road construction. In 1989 (Heisei 1), a survey was conducted, followed by four excavation campaigns from 1989 to 1991. The mound has a "Kenbishi-style" keyhole shape with a protruding front section oriented westward. It is constructed in three tiers, with external surfaces featuring {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}}. Cylindrical {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}}, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}} (TK216-208 style), and {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}} have been excavated. The southern neck of the mound features a {{ill|tsukuridashi|ja|造出}}, and the shield-shaped moat surrounding the mound brings the total length to 119.2 meters. The burial facility remains unexamined, and grave goods are largely unknown. The mound is estimated to date from the mid-5th century, during the middle {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} (or the late 5th century, according to other estimates). It served as a prominent burial site for regional leaders in the southern Utsunomiya area and is considered critical for studying the political dynamics of the {{ill|Shimotsukeno region|ja|下毛野地方}}. The site was designated as a Tochigi Prefecture historical site in 1953 (Shōwa 28). Today, the mound is adorned with {{ill|Dodantsutsuji shrubs|ja|ドウダンツツジ}}, offering a unique landscape that has been developed for preservation. == Ruins History == * [[1953]] (Showa 28), November 10: Tsukayama Kofun was designated as a historic site by Tochigi Prefecture. * [[1966]] (Showa 41): Construction planning for [[National Route 121]] (part of the [[Utsunomiya Ring Road]]) began. The plans were revised to include a tunnel near the kofun group to protect cultural properties. * [[1973]] (Showa 48), April 13: Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun were designated as historic sites by Tochigi Prefecture. * [[1976]] (Showa 51): Excavations of Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama East Kofun were conducted due to road construction (reported by the Tochigi Prefectural Board of Education in [[1979]]). * [[1989]]-[[1991]] (Heisei 1-3): Excavations of Tsukayama Kofun were carried out by the Archaeological Research Society of [[Utsunomiya University]] (findings published in [[1995]]). * [[1991]]-[[1992]] (Heisei 3-4): Excavations of the Tsukayama Kofun Group were conducted during road improvement work by the Utsunomiya City Board of Education (findings published in [[1996]]). * [[1995]]-[[1997]] (Heisei 7-9): Excavations of Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun were carried out for historic site conservation by the Utsunomiya City Board of Education, Utsunomiya University, and [[Utsunomiya Bunsei Junior College]] (findings published in [[2003]]). * [[2005]] (Heisei 17), November 7: Artifacts excavated from Tsukayama South Kofun were designated as tangible cultural properties by Utsunomiya City. [[Category:Kofun in Japan]] [[ja:塚山古墳群の歴史]] == Mound == The dimensions of the mound are as follows{{Sfn|Tsukayama Kofun Group (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}: * Total Kofun Length: 119.2 meters - The overall length of the kofun, including the surrounding moat. * Mound Length: 98.3 meters * Rear Circular Section Diameter: 55.9 meters * Front Section Width: 59.9 meters File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), funkyu-4.jpg|Mound and surrounding moat. [[Category:Kofun in Japan]] [[ja:塚山古墳群の墳丘]] == Tsukayama Kofun Group == The '''Tsukayama Kofun Group''' consists of a cluster of kofun (ancient burial mounds) with Tsukayama Kofun as the main mound. Originally composed of over 10 kofun, it currently includes one [[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped kofun]] (Tsukayama Kofun), two [[Scallop-shaped kofun|scallop-shaped kofun]] (Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun), and one round kofun (No. 6 Kofun). Investigations have identified six small round kofun (Nos. 4, 5, 7, 8, and two within the old shooting range) to the north of Tsukayama Kofun. To the west and southwest, from north to south, lie a mid-sized round kofun (No. 6), Tsukayama West Kofun, and Tsukayama South Kofun. Haniwa sarcophagi have also been discovered in the area, with one featuring an engraved depiction of four deer in alternating male and female pairs. The construction period is estimated to span the mid-5th century to the early 6th century during the mid- to late-Kofun period, following the [[Mobara Kofun Group]] and the {{ill|Higashitani Kofun Group|ja|東谷古墳群}}. Mound (rear circular section in the center, front section in the background) |Alias = |Location = [[Tochigi Prefecture|Tochigi]], [[Utsunomiya]] Nishikawada Town Higashihara |Shape = [[Scallop-shaped kofun]] |Size = Mound length: 63.1 m
Height: 6.7 m (rear section) |Burial Facility = Unknown |Artifacts Found = [[Haniwa]], [[Sue ware]] |Construction Period = [[5th century]] late |Historic Site Designation = Prefectural Historic Site: "Tsukayama West Kofun" |Special Notes = }} '''Tsukayama West Kofun''' (塚山西古墳) is a kofun located southwest of Tsukayama Kofun. It is [[Scallop-shaped kofun|scallop-shaped]] and designated as a historic site by Tochigi Prefecture. The mound has a short front section and a rear circular section, oriented to the south-southeast. The dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}: * Total Kofun Length: 74.1 meters (including moat). * Mound Length: 63.1 meters. * Rear Circular Section ** Diameter: 44.5 meters ** Height: 6.7 meters * Front Section ** Length: ~18 meters ** Width: ~22 meters ** Height: ~1.5 meters The mound comprises two or more tiers (upper tiers heavily disturbed){{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. Cylindrical haniwa and Sue ware (TK208-TK23 styles) were found on the mound's surface{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. A horseshoe-shaped moat surrounds the mound (shallow on the east side due to proximity to Tsukayama Kofun){{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. Burial facilities are unknown due to limited findings; no clay or stone structures have been detected{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. The construction period is estimated to be the late 5th century, following Tsukayama Kofun and preceding Tsukayama South Kofun{{Sfn|Tsukayama Kofun Group (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}. === Tsukayama South Kofun === {{Japan kofun |Name = Tsukayama South Kofun |image = [[File:Tsukayama Minami Kofun (Utsunomiya), funkyu-2.jpg|280px]]
Mound (rear circular section in the center, front section in the background) |Alias = |Location = [[Tochigi Prefecture|Tochigi]], [[Utsunomiya]] Nishikawada Town Higashihara |Shape = [[Scallop-shaped kofun]] |Size = Mound length: 58 m
Height: 6.8 m (rear section) |Burial Facility = Unknown |Artifacts Found = [[Haniwa]], [[Sue ware]], [[Haji ware]] |Construction Period = [[5th century]] late |Historic Site Designation = Prefectural Historic Site: "Tsukayama South Kofun" |Special Notes = Excavated artifacts designated as cultural properties of Utsunomiya City }} '''Tsukayama South Kofun''' (塚山南古墳) is a kofun located south of Tsukayama West Kofun. It is [[Scallop-shaped kofun|scallop-shaped]] and designated as a historic site by Tochigi Prefecture. The mound has a short front section and a rear circular section, oriented southward. The dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}: * Total Kofun Length: 70.6 meters (including moat). * Mound Length: 58.0 meters. * Rear Circular Section ** Diameter: 42.1 meters ** Height: 6.8 meters * Front Section ** Length: 13.5 meters ** Height: 4.1 meters The mound is two-tiered{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. Numerous artifacts, including cylindrical haniwa, figurative haniwa (human, horse, deer, and house shapes), large Sue ware vessels, and Haji ware, were recovered, though no evidence of surface stones was found{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. A horseshoe-shaped moat surrounds the mound (narrower on the northwest side due to proximity to Tsukayama West Kofun){{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. Burial facilities have not been fully investigated, but depressions and red-painted stones suggest a vertical burial system at the mound's summit, likely plundered{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. [[Category:Kofun in Japan]] [[ja:塚山古墳群]] The construction period is estimated to be the late 5th century to early 6th century, following Tsukayama West Kofun{{Sfn|Tsukayama Kofun Group (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}. == Cultural Properties == === Tochigi Prefectural Cultural Properties === * Historic Sites ** {{ill|Tsukayama Kofun|ja|塚山古墳}} - Designated on November 10, 1953 (Showa 28).[http://www.tochigi-edu.ed.jp/center/bunkazai/2341001.htm 塚山古墳] (Cultural Property Section, Tochigi Prefectural Board of Education).[https://utsunomiya-8story.jp/search_post/%e5%a1%9a%e5%b1%b1%e5%8f%a4%e5%a2%b3/ 塚山古墳] (Utsunomiya Historical and Cultural Resources Promotion Council). ** {{ill|Tsukayama Nishi Kofun|ja|塚山西古墳}} - Designated on April 13, 1973 (Showa 48).[http://www.tochigi-edu.ed.jp/center/bunkazai/2341039.htm 塚山西古墳] (Cultural Property Section, Tochigi Prefectural Board of Education).[https://utsunomiya-8story.jp/search_post/%e5%a1%9a%e5%b1%b1%e8%a5%bf%e5%8f%a4%e5%a2%b3/ 塚山西古墳] (Utsunomiya Historical and Cultural Resources Promotion Council). ** {{ill|Tsukayama Minami Kofun|ja|塚山南古墳}} - Designated on April 13, 1973 (Showa 48).[http://www.tochigi-edu.ed.jp/center/bunkazai/2341040.htm 塚山南古墳] (Cultural Property Section, Tochigi Prefectural Board of Education).[https://utsunomiya-8story.jp/search_post/%e5%a1%9a%e5%b1%b1%e5%8d%97%e5%8f%a4%e5%a2%b3/ 塚山南古墳] (Utsunomiya Historical and Cultural Resources Promotion Council). === Utsunomiya City Designated Cultural Properties === * Tangible Cultural Properties ** Artifacts excavated from {{ill|Tsukayama Minami Kofun|ja|塚山南古墳}} (archaeological materials) - Designated on November 7, 2005 (Heisei 17).
