Mound (Right: front section; Left-back: rear circular section) | Alternate name = Hyōgo-zuka Kofun | Group = Tsukayama Kofun Cluster | location = Nishikawada-machi 7-chome, {{ill|Utsunomiya City|ja|宇都宮市}}, Tochigi Prefecture | Coordinates = {{Coord|36|30|22.05|N|139|51|39.50|E|region:JP-09_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Tsukayama Kofun}} | Shape = {{ill|Keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} (Kenbishi-style) | Dimensions = Total mound length: 98.3 meters | Burial Facility = Unknown | Artifacts = {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}}, {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器}}, {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器}} | Kofuns = | Construction Era = Mid-5th century | Buried Figure = | Mausoleum = | Historical Site = Tochigi Prefecture-designated Historical Site (Tsukayama Kofun) | Cultural Asset = | Notes = | Map2 = {{location map|Japan Tochigi|label=Tsukayama Kofun|lat_deg=36|lat_min=30|lat_sec=22.05|lon_deg=139|lon_min=51|lon_sec=39.5|mark=前方後円墳-西南西.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=top|width=200|caption=}} }} {{OSM location map | coord = {{Coord|36|30|20|N|139|51|38|E}} | zoom = 17 | float = right | width = 300 | height = 250 | caption = {{center|Distribution map of the Tsukayama Kofun Cluster}} | scalemark = 60 | mark-coord1 = {{Coord|36|30|22.05|N|139|51|39.50|E}} | label1 = Tsukayama Kofun | label-pos1 = top | label-color1 = black | mark1 = 前方後円墳-西南西.svg | mark-size1 = 70 | mark-coord2 = {{Coord|36|30|20.25|N|139|51|36.35|E}} | label2 = Tsukayama West Kofun | label-pos2 = top | label-color2 = black | mark2 = 帆立貝形古墳-南南東.svg | mark-size2 = 60 | mark-coord3 = {{Coord|36|30|17.93|N|139|51|37.23|E}} | label3 = Tsukayama South Kofun | label-pos3 = left | label-color3 = black | mark3 = 帆立貝形古墳-南.svg | mark-size3 = 60 }} '''Tsukayama Kofun''' (塚山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in Nishikawada-machi, {{ill|Utsunomiya City|ja|宇都宮市}}, Tochigi Prefecture. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} and part of the {{ill|Tsukayama Kofun Cluster|ja|塚山古墳群}}. It has been designated as a Tochigi Prefecture-designated historical site. This article also covers the {{ill|Tsukayama Kofun Cluster|ja|塚山古墳群}}, for which Tsukayama Kofun serves as the main mound. [[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]] [[Category:Completion tier 6]][[Category: tier 6]][[Category: tier 6]] [[Category:11]][[sn:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya)]][[Category:11]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya)]][[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:01-17]][[ja:塚山古墳 (宇都宮市)]] == Overview == [[File:100425 Tsukayama Kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|{{center|Aerial view of the Tsukayama Kofun Cluster (2010)}}{{small|Top right: Tsukayama Kofun; Left: Tsukayama West Kofun; Bottom left: Tsukayama South Kofun. {{ill|Aerial photographs of Japan|ja|国土航空写真}}.}}]] Located in southern Tochigi Prefecture, the mound was constructed on a plateau between the {{ill|Tagawa River (Tone River System)|ja|田川 (利根川水系)}} and {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}}. It is the largest keyhole-shaped kofun in the Tsukayama Kofun Cluster, which includes several mounds such as the scallop-shaped Tsukayama West and South Kofun, as well as {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}}-based coffins. The rear circular section has been partially leveled by road construction. In 1989 (Heisei 1), a survey was conducted, followed by four excavation campaigns from 1989 to 1991. The mound has a "Kenbishi-style" keyhole shape with a protruding front section oriented westward. It is constructed in three tiers, with external surfaces featuring {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}}. Cylindrical {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}}, {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器}} (TK216-208 style), and {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器}} have been excavated. The southern neck of the mound features a {{ill|tsukuridashi|ja|造出|1=Platform-style projection}}, and the shield-shaped moat surrounding the mound brings the total length to 119.2 meters. The burial facility remains unexamined, and grave goods are largely unknown. The mound is estimated to date from the mid-5th century, during the middle {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} (or the late 5th century, according to other estimates). It served as a prominent burial site for regional leaders in the southern Utsunomiya area and is considered critical for studying the political dynamics of the {{ill|Shimotsukeno region|ja|下毛野地方}}. The site was designated as a Tochigi Prefecture historical site in 1953 (Shōwa 28). Today, the mound is adorned with {{ill|Dodantsutsuji shrubs|ja|ドウダンツツジ}}, offering a unique landscape that has been developed for preservation. == Ruins History == * [[1953]] (Showa 28), November 10: Tsukayama Kofun was designated as a historic site by Tochigi Prefecture. * [[1966]] (Showa 41): Construction planning for [[National Route 121]] (part of the [[Utsunomiya Ring Road]]) began. The plans were revised to include a tunnel near the kofun group to protect cultural properties. * [[1973]] (Showa 48), April 13: Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun were designated as historic sites by Tochigi Prefecture. * [[1976]] (Showa 51): Excavations of Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama East Kofun were conducted due to road construction (reported by the Tochigi Prefectural Board of Education in [[1979]]). * [[1989]]-[[1991]] (Heisei 1-3): Excavations of Tsukayama Kofun were carried out by the Archaeological Research Society of [[Utsunomiya University]] (findings published in [[1995]]). * [[1991]]-[[1992]] (Heisei 3-4): Excavations of the Tsukayama Kofun Group were conducted during road improvement work by the Utsunomiya City Board of Education (findings published in [[1996]]). * [[1995]]-[[1997]] (Heisei 7-9): Excavations of Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun were carried out for historic site conservation by the Utsunomiya City Board of Education, Utsunomiya University, and [[Utsunomiya Bunsei Junior College]] (findings published in [[2003]]). * [[2005]] (Heisei 17), November 7: Artifacts excavated from Tsukayama South Kofun were designated as tangible cultural properties by Utsunomiya City. [[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kofun in Japan]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]] [[Category:11]][[sn:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya)]][[Category:11]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya)]][[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:01-17]][[ja:塚山古墳群の墳丘]] == Tsukayama Kofun Group == The '''Tsukayama Kofun Group''' consists of a cluster of kofun (ancient Kofuns) with Tsukayama Kofun as the main mound. Originally composed of over 10 kofun, it currently includes one [[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped kofun]] (Tsukayama Kofun), two [[Scallop-shaped kofun|scallop-shaped kofun]] (Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun), and one round kofun (No. 6 Kofun). Investigations have identified six small round kofun (Nos. 4, 5, 7, 8, and two within the old shooting range) to the north of Tsukayama Kofun. To the west and southwest, from north to south, lie a mid-sized round kofun (No. 6), Tsukayama West Kofun, and Tsukayama South Kofun. Haniwa sarcophagi have also been discovered in the area, with one featuring an engraved depiction of four deer in alternating male and female pairs. The construction period is estimated to span the mid-5th century to the early 6th century during the mid- to late-Kofun period, following the [[Mobara Kofun Group]] and the {{ill|Higashitani Kofun Group|ja|東谷古墳群}}. Mound (rear circular section in the center, front section in the background) |Alias = |location = [[Tochigi Prefecture|Tochigi]], [[Utsunomiya]] Nishikawada Town Higashihara |Shape = [[Scallop-shaped kofun]] |Size = Mound length: 63.1 m
Height: 6.7 m (rear section) |Burial Facility = Unknown |Artifacts Found = [[Haniwa]], [[Sue pottery]] |Construction Period = [[5th century]] late |Historic Site Designation = Prefectural Historic Site: "Tsukayama West Kofun" |Special Notes = }} '''Tsukayama West Kofun''' (塚山西古墳) is a kofun located southwest of Tsukayama Kofun. It is [[Scallop-shaped kofun|scallop-shaped]] and designated as a historic site by Tochigi Prefecture. The mound has a short front section and a rear circular section, oriented to the south-southeast. The dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}: * Total Kofun Length: 74.1 meters (including moat). * Mound Length: 63.1 meters. * Rear Circular Section ** Diameter: 44.5 meters ** Height: 6.7 meters * Front Section ** Length: ~18 meters ** Width: ~22 meters ** Height: ~1.5 meters The mound comprises two or more tiers (upper tiers heavily disturbed){{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. Cylindrical haniwa and Sue pottery (TK208-TK23 styles) were found on the mound's surface{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. A horseshoe-shaped moat surrounds the mound (shallow on the east side due to proximity to Tsukayama Kofun){{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. Burial facilities are unknown due to limited findings; no clay or stone structures have been detected{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. The construction period is estimated to be the late 5th century, following Tsukayama Kofun and preceding Tsukayama South Kofun{{Sfn|Tsukayama Kofun Group (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}. === Tsukayama South Kofun === {{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]] |name = Tsukayama South Kofun |image = [[File:Tsukayama Minami Kofun (Utsunomiya), funkyu-2.jpg|280px]]
Mound (rear circular section in the center, front section in the background) |Alias = |location = [[Tochigi Prefecture|Tochigi]], [[Utsunomiya]] Nishikawada Town Higashihara |Shape = [[Scallop-shaped kofun]] |Size = Mound length: 58 m
Height: 6.8 m (rear section) |Burial Facility = Unknown |Artifacts Found = [[Haniwa]], [[Sue pottery]], [[Haji pottery]] |Construction Period = [[5th century]] late |Historic Site Designation = Prefectural Historic Site: "Tsukayama South Kofun" |Special Notes = Excavated artifacts designated as cultural properties of Utsunomiya City }} '''Tsukayama South Kofun''' (塚山南古墳) is a kofun located south of Tsukayama West Kofun. It is [[Scallop-shaped kofun|scallop-shaped]] and designated as a historic site by Tochigi Prefecture. The mound has a short front section and a rear circular section, oriented southward. The dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}: * Total Kofun Length: 70.6 meters (including moat). * Mound Length: 58.0 meters. * Rear Circular Section ** Diameter: 42.1 meters ** Height: 6.8 meters * Front Section ** Length: 13.5 meters ** Height: 4.1 meters The mound is two-tiered{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. Numerous artifacts, including cylindrical haniwa, figurative haniwa (human, horse, deer, and house shapes), large Sue pottery vessels, and Haji pottery, were recovered, though no evidence of surface stones was found{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. A horseshoe-shaped moat surrounds the mound (narrower on the northwest side due to proximity to Tsukayama West Kofun){{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. Burial facilities have not been fully investigated, but depressions and red-painted stones suggest a vertical burial system at the mound's summit, likely plundered{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} and part of the {{ill|Tsukayama Kofun Cluster|ja|塚山古墳群}}. It has been designated as a Tochigi Prefecture-designated historical site. This article also covers the {{ill|Tsukayama Kofun Cluster|ja|塚山古墳群}}, for which Tsukayama Kofun serves as the main mound. [[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]] [[Category:Completion tier 6]][[Category: tier 6]][[Category: tier 6]] [[Category:11]][[sn:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya)]][[Category:11]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya)]][[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:01-17]][[ja:塚山古墳 (宇都宮市)]] == Overview == [[File:100425 Tsukayama Kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|{{center|Aerial view of the Tsukayama Kofun Cluster (2010)}}{{small|Top right: Tsukayama Kofun; Left: Tsukayama West Kofun; Bottom left: Tsukayama South Kofun. {{ill|Aerial photographs of Japan|ja|国土航空写真}}.}}]] Located in southern Tochigi Prefecture, the mound was constructed on a plateau between the {{ill|Tagawa River (Tone River System)|ja|田川 (利根川水系)}} and {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}}. It is the largest keyhole-shaped kofun in the Tsukayama Kofun Cluster, which includes several mounds such as the scallop-shaped Tsukayama West and South Kofun, as well as {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}}-based coffins. The rear circular section has been partially leveled by road construction. In 1989 (Heisei 1), a survey was conducted, followed by four excavation campaigns from 1989 to 1991. The mound has a "Kenbishi-style" keyhole shape with a protruding front section oriented westward. It is constructed in three tiers, with external surfaces featuring {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}}. Cylindrical {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}}, {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器}} (TK216-208 style), and {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器}} have been excavated. The southern neck of the mound features a {{ill|tsukuridashi|ja|造出|1=Platform-style projection}}, and the shield-shaped moat surrounding the mound brings the total length to 119.2 meters. The burial facility remains unexamined, and grave goods are largely unknown. The mound is estimated to date from the mid-5th century, during the middle {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} (or the late 5th century, according to other estimates). It served as a prominent burial site for regional leaders in the southern Utsunomiya area and is considered critical for studying the political dynamics of the {{ill|Shimotsukeno region|ja|下毛野地方}}. The site was designated as a Tochigi Prefecture historical site in 1953 (Shōwa 28). Today, the mound is adorned with {{ill|Dodantsutsuji shrubs|ja|ドウダンツツジ}}, offering a unique landscape that has been developed for preservation. == Ruins History == * [[1953]] (Showa 28), November 10: Tsukayama Kofun was designated as a historic site by Tochigi Prefecture. * [[1966]] (Showa 41): Construction planning for [[National Route 121]] (part of the [[Utsunomiya Ring Road]]) began. The plans were revised to include a tunnel near the kofun group to protect cultural properties. * [[1973]] (Showa 48), April 13: Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun were designated as historic sites by Tochigi Prefecture. * [[1976]] (Showa 51): Excavations of Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama East Kofun were conducted due to road construction (reported by the Tochigi Prefectural Board of Education in [[1979]]). * [[1989]]-[[1991]] (Heisei 1-3): Excavations of Tsukayama Kofun were carried out by the Archaeological Research Society of [[Utsunomiya University]] (findings published in [[1995]]). * [[1991]]-[[1992]] (Heisei 3-4): Excavations of the Tsukayama Kofun Group were conducted during road improvement work by the Utsunomiya City Board of Education (findings published in [[1996]]). * [[1995]]-[[1997]] (Heisei 7-9): Excavations of Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun were carried out for historic site conservation by the Utsunomiya City Board of Education, Utsunomiya University, and [[Utsunomiya Bunsei Junior College]] (findings published in [[2003]]). * [[2005]] (Heisei 17), November 7: Artifacts excavated from Tsukayama South Kofun were designated as tangible cultural properties by Utsunomiya City. [[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kofun in Japan]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]] [[Category:11]][[sn:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya)]][[Category:11]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya)]][[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:01-17]][[ja:塚山古墳群の墳丘]] == Tsukayama Kofun Group == The '''Tsukayama Kofun Group''' consists of a cluster of kofun (ancient Kofuns) with Tsukayama Kofun as the main mound. Originally composed of over 10 kofun, it currently includes one [[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped kofun]] (Tsukayama Kofun), two [[Scallop-shaped kofun|scallop-shaped kofun]] (Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun), and one round kofun (No. 6 Kofun). Investigations have identified six small round kofun (Nos. 4, 5, 7, 8, and two within the old shooting range) to the north of Tsukayama Kofun. To the west and southwest, from north to south, lie a mid-sized round kofun (No. 6), Tsukayama West Kofun, and Tsukayama South Kofun. Haniwa sarcophagi have also been discovered in the area, with one featuring an engraved depiction of four deer in alternating male and female pairs. The construction period is estimated to span the mid-5th century to the early 6th century during the mid- to late-Kofun period, following the [[Mobara Kofun Group]] and the {{ill|Higashitani Kofun Group|ja|東谷古墳群}}. Mound (rear circular section in the center, front section in the background) |Alias = |location = [[Tochigi Prefecture|Tochigi]], [[Utsunomiya]] Nishikawada Town Higashihara |Shape = [[Scallop-shaped kofun]] |Size = Mound length: 63.1 m
Height: 6.7 m (rear section) |Burial Facility = Unknown |burial goods Found = [[Haniwa]], [[Sue pottery]] |Construction Period = [[5th century]] late |Historic Site Designation = Prefectural Historic Site: "Tsukayama West Kofun" |Special Notes = }} '''Tsukayama West Kofun''' (塚山西古墳) is a kofun located southwest of Tsukayama Kofun. It is [[Scallop-shaped kofun|scallop-shaped]] and designated as a historic site by Tochigi Prefecture. The mound has a short front section and a rear circular section, oriented to the south-southeast. The dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}: * Total Kofun Length: 74.1 meters (including moat). * Mound Length: 63.1 meters. * Rear Circular Section ** Diameter: 44.5 meters ** Height: 6.7 meters * Front Section ** Length: ~18 meters ** Width: ~22 meters ** Height: ~1.5 meters The mound comprises two or more tiers (upper tiers heavily disturbed){{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. Cylindrical haniwa and Sue pottery (TK208-TK23 styles) were found on the mound's surface{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. A horseshoe-shaped moat surrounds the mound (shallow on the east side due to proximity to Tsukayama Kofun){{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. Burial facilities are unknown due to limited findings; no clay or stone structures have been detected{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. The construction period is estimated to be the late 5th century, following Tsukayama Kofun and preceding Tsukayama South Kofun{{Sfn|Tsukayama Kofun Group (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}. === Tsukayama South Kofun === {{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]] |name = Tsukayama South Kofun |image = [[File:Tsukayama Minami Kofun (Utsunomiya), funkyu-2.jpg|280px]]
Mound (rear circular section in the center, front section in the background) |Alias = |location = [[Tochigi Prefecture|Tochigi]], [[Utsunomiya]] Nishikawada Town Higashihara |Shape = [[Scallop-shaped kofun]] |Size = Mound length: 58 m
Height: 6.8 m (rear section) |Burial Facility = Unknown |burial goods Found = [[Haniwa]], [[Sue pottery]], [[Haji pottery]] |Construction Period = [[5th century]] late |Historic Site Designation = Prefectural Historic Site: "Tsukayama South Kofun" |Special Notes = Excavated artifacts designated as cultural properties of Utsunomiya City }} '''Tsukayama South Kofun''' (塚山南古墳) is a kofun located south of Tsukayama West Kofun. It is [[Scallop-shaped kofun|scallop-shaped]] and designated as a historic site by Tochigi Prefecture. The mound has a short front section and a rear circular section, oriented southward. The dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}: * Total Kofun Length: 70.6 meters (including moat). * Mound Length: 58.0 meters. * Rear Circular Section ** Diameter: 42.1 meters ** Height: 6.8 meters * Front Section ** Length: 13.5 meters ** Height: 4.1 meters The mound is two-tiered{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. Numerous artifacts, including cylindrical haniwa, figurative haniwa (human, horse, deer, and house shapes), large Sue pottery vessels, and Haji pottery, were recovered, though no evidence of surface stones was found{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. A horseshoe-shaped moat surrounds the mound (narrower on the northwest side due to proximity to Tsukayama West Kofun){{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. Burial facilities have not been fully investigated, but depressions and red-painted stones suggest a vertical burial system at the mound's summit, likely plundered{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. Mound (Right: front section; Left-back: rear circular section) | Alternate name = Hyōgo-zuka Kofun | Group = Tsukayama Kofun Cluster | location = Nishikawada-machi 7-chome, {{ill|Utsunomiya City|ja|宇都宮市}}, Tochigi Prefecture | Coordinates = {{Coord|36|30|22.05|N|139|51|39.50|E|region:JP-09_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Tsukayama Kofun}} | Shape = {{ill|Keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} (Kenbishi-style) | Dimensions = Total mound length: 98.3 meters | Burial Facility = Unknown | Artifacts = {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}}, {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器}}, {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器}} | Kofuns = | Construction Era = Mid-5th century | Buried Figure = | Mausoleum = | Historical Site = Tochigi Prefecture-designated Historical Site (Tsukayama Kofun) | Cultural Asset = | Notes = | Map2 = {{location map|Japan Tochigi|label=Tsukayama Kofun|lat_deg=36|lat_min=30|lat_sec=22.05|lon_deg=139|lon_min=51|lon_sec=39.5|mark=前方後円墳-西南西.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=top|width=200|caption=}} }} {{OSM location map | coord = {{Coord|36|30|20|N|139|51|38|E}} | zoom = 17 | float = right | width = 300 | height = 250 | caption = {{center|Distribution map of the Tsukayama Kofun Cluster}} | scalemark = 60 | mark-coord1 = {{Coord|36|30|22.05|N|139|51|39.50|E}} | label1 = Tsukayama Kofun | label-pos1 = top | label-color1 = black | mark1 = 前方後円墳-西南西.svg | mark-size1 = 70 | mark-coord2 = {{Coord|36|30|20.25|N|139|51|36.35|E}} | label2 = Tsukayama West Kofun | label-pos2 = top | label-color2 = black | mark2 = 帆立貝形古墳-南南東.svg | mark-size2 = 60 | mark-coord3 = {{Coord|36|30|17.93|N|139|51|37.23|E}} | label3 = Tsukayama South Kofun | label-pos3 = left | label-color3 = black | mark3 = 帆立貝形古墳-南.svg | mark-size3 = 60 }} '''Tsukayama Kofun''' (塚山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in Nishikawada-machi, {{ill|Utsunomiya City|ja|宇都宮市}}, Tochigi Prefecture. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} and part of the {{ill|Tsukayama Kofun Cluster|ja|塚山古墳群}}. It has been designated as a Tochigi Prefecture-designated historical site. This article also covers the {{ill|Tsukayama Kofun Cluster|ja|塚山古墳群}}, for which Tsukayama Kofun serves as the main mound. [[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]] [[Category:Completion tier 6]][[Category: tier 6]][[Category: tier 6]] [[Category:11]][[sn:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya)]][[Category:11]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya)]][[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:01-17]][[ja:塚山古墳 (宇都宮市)]] == Overview == [[File:100425 Tsukayama Kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|{{center|Aerial view of the Tsukayama Kofun Cluster (2010)}}{{small|Top right: Tsukayama Kofun; Left: Tsukayama West Kofun; Bottom left: Tsukayama South Kofun. {{ill|Aerial photographs of Japan|ja|国土航空写真}}.}}]] Located in southern Tochigi Prefecture, the mound was constructed on a plateau between the {{ill|Tagawa River (Tone River System)|ja|田川 (利根川水系)}} and {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}}. It is the largest keyhole-shaped kofun in the Tsukayama Kofun Cluster, which includes several mounds such as the scallop-shaped Tsukayama West and South Kofun, as well as {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}}-based coffins. The rear circular section has been partially leveled by road construction. In 1989 (Heisei 1), a survey was conducted, followed by four excavation campaigns from 1989 to 1991. The mound has a "Kenbishi-style" keyhole shape with a protruding front section oriented westward. It is constructed in three tiers, with external surfaces featuring {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}}. Cylindrical {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}}, {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器}} (TK216-208 style), and {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器}} have been excavated. The southern neck of the mound features a {{ill|tsukuridashi|ja|造出|1=Platform-style projection}}, and the shield-shaped moat surrounding the mound brings the total length to 119.2 meters. The burial facility remains unexamined, and grave goods are largely unknown. The mound is estimated to date from the mid-5th century, during the middle {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} (or the late 5th century, according to other estimates). It served as a prominent burial site for regional leaders in the southern Utsunomiya area and is considered critical for studying the political dynamics of the {{ill|Shimotsukeno region|ja|下毛野地方}}. The site was designated as a Tochigi Prefecture historical site in 1953 (Shōwa 28). Today, the mound is adorned with {{ill|Dodantsutsuji shrubs|ja|ドウダンツツジ}}, offering a unique landscape that has been developed for preservation. == Ruins History == * [[1953]] (Showa 28), November 10: Tsukayama Kofun was designated as a historic site by Tochigi Prefecture. * [[1966]] (Showa 41): Construction planning for [[National Route 121]] (part of the [[Utsunomiya Ring Road]]) began. The plans were revised to include a tunnel near the kofun group to protect cultural properties. * [[1973]] (Showa 48), April 13: Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun were designated as historic sites by Tochigi Prefecture. * [[1976]] (Showa 51): Excavations of Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama East Kofun were conducted due to road construction (reported by the Tochigi Prefectural Board of Education in [[1979]]). * [[1989]]-[[1991]] (Heisei 1-3): Excavations of Tsukayama Kofun were carried out by the Archaeological Research Society of [[Utsunomiya University]] (findings published in [[1995]]). * [[1991]]-[[1992]] (Heisei 3-4): Excavations of the Tsukayama Kofun Group were conducted during road improvement work by the Utsunomiya City Board of Education (findings published in [[1996]]). * [[1995]]-[[1997]] (Heisei 7-9): Excavations of Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun were carried out for historic site conservation by the Utsunomiya City Board of Education, Utsunomiya University, and [[Utsunomiya Bunsei Junior College]] (findings published in [[2003]]). * [[2005]] (Heisei 17), November 7: Artifacts excavated from Tsukayama South Kofun were designated as tangible cultural properties by Utsunomiya City. [[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kofun in Japan]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]] [[Category:11]][[sn:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya)]][[Category:11]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya)]][[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:01-17]][[ja:塚山古墳群の歴史]] == Mound == The dimensions of the mound are as follows{{Sfn|Tsukayama Kofun Group (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}: * Total Kofun Length: 119.2 meters - The overall length of the kofun, including the surrounding moat. * Mound Length: 98.3 meters * Rear Circular Section Diameter: 55.9 meters * Front Section Width: 59.9 meters File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), funkyu-4.jpg|Mound and surrounding moat. File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), funkyu-3.jpg|Mound
{{small|Rear circular section on the left, front section in the right background.}} File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), funcho.jpg|Summit of the rear circular section. File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), kouenbu.jpg|View from the front section toward the rear circular section. File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), zenpoubu.jpg|View from the rear circular section toward the front section. [[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kofun in Japan]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]] [[Category:11]][[sn:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya)]][[Category:11]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya)]][[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:01-17]][[ja:塚山古墳群の墳丘]] == Tsukayama Kofun Group == The '''Tsukayama Kofun Group''' consists of a cluster of kofun (ancient Kofuns) with Tsukayama Kofun as the main mound. Originally composed of over 10 kofun, it currently includes one [[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped kofun]] (Tsukayama Kofun), two [[Scallop-shaped kofun|scallop-shaped kofun]] (Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun), and one round kofun (No. 6 Kofun). Investigations have identified six small round kofun (Nos. 4, 5, 7, 8, and two within the old shooting range) to the north of Tsukayama Kofun. To the west and southwest, from north to south, lie a mid-sized round kofun (No. 6), Tsukayama West Kofun, and Tsukayama South Kofun. Haniwa sarcophagi have also been discovered in the area, with one featuring an engraved depiction of four deer in alternating male and female pairs. The construction period is estimated to span the mid-5th century to the early 6th century during the mid- to late-Kofun period, following the [[Mobara Kofun Group]] and the {{ill|Higashitani Kofun Group|ja|東谷古墳群}}. The kofun group is detailed as follows: {| class="wikitable" style="text-align:center;background:#ffffff;white-space:nowrap;font-size:85%" |+List of Tsukayama Kofun GroupTsukayama Kofun Group Pamphlet.Historic Site Information Board. ! Artifacts designated as cultural properties of Utsunomiya City |- |'''No. 4 Kofun'''||[[Enpun|Round kofun]]||Diameter: 8 m||style="text-align:left"|Pottery|| ||(Destroyed)|| |- |'''No. 5 Kofun'''||Round kofun||Diameter: 7 m||style="text-align:left"|Traces of wooden coffins, cylindrical haniwa, pottery, jewelry|| ||(Destroyed)|| |- |'''No. 6 Kofun'''||Round kofun||Diameter: 20 m||style="text-align:left"|Cylindrical haniwa, pottery|| ||None|| |- |'''No. 7 Kofun'''||Round kofun|| ||style="text-align:left"|Figurative haniwa (birds), pottery|| ||(Destroyed)|| |- |'''No. 8 Kofun'''||Round kofun|| ||style="text-align:left"|Cylindrical haniwa, pottery|| ||(Destroyed)|| |- |Two Kofun within Old Shooting Range||Round kofun|| ||style="text-align:left"|Cylindrical haniwa, figurative haniwa (birds, armor)|| ||(Destroyed)|| |- |Five Haniwa Sarcophagi||Haniwa Sarcophagi|| ||style="text-align:left"|Cylindrical haniwa|| ||(Destroyed)|| |} File:Tsukayama Kofun Group (Utsunomiya)-6, funkyu.jpg|No. 6 Kofun === Tsukayama West Kofun === {{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]] |name = Tsukayama West Kofun |image = [[File:Tsukayama Nishi Kofun (Utsunomiya), funkyu-2.jpg|280px]]
Mound (rear circular section in the center, front section in the background) |Alias = |location = [[Tochigi Prefecture|Tochigi]], [[Utsunomiya]] Nishikawada Town Higashihara |Shape = [[Scallop-shaped kofun]] |Size = Mound length: 63.1 m
Height: 6.7 m (rear section) |Burial Facility = Unknown |burial goods Found = [[Haniwa]], [[Sue pottery]] |Construction Period = [[5th century]] late |Historic Site Designation = Prefectural Historic Site: "Tsukayama West Kofun" |Special Notes = }} '''Tsukayama West Kofun''' (塚山西古墳) is a kofun located southwest of Tsukayama Kofun. It is [[Scallop-shaped kofun|scallop-shaped]] and designated as a historic site by Tochigi Prefecture. The mound has a short front section and a rear circular section, oriented to the south-southeast. The dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}: * Total Kofun Length: 74.1 meters (including moat). * Mound Length: 63.1 meters. * Rear Circular Section ** Diameter: 44.5 meters ** Height: 6.7 meters * Front Section ** Length: ~18 meters ** Width: ~22 meters ** Height: ~1.5 meters The mound comprises two or more tiers (upper tiers heavily disturbed){{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. Cylindrical haniwa and Sue pottery (TK208-TK23 styles) were found on the mound's surface{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. A horseshoe-shaped moat surrounds the mound (shallow on the east side due to proximity to Tsukayama Kofun){{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. Burial facilities are unknown due to limited findings; no clay or stone structures have been detected{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. The construction period is estimated to be the late 5th century, following Tsukayama Kofun and preceding Tsukayama South Kofun{{Sfn|Tsukayama Kofun Group (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}. === Tsukayama South Kofun === {{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]] |name = Tsukayama South Kofun |image = [[File:Tsukayama Minami Kofun (Utsunomiya), funkyu-2.jpg|280px]]
Mound (rear circular section in the center, front section in the background) |Alias = |location = [[Tochigi Prefecture|Tochigi]], [[Utsunomiya]] Nishikawada Town Higashihara |Shape = [[Scallop-shaped kofun]] |Size = Mound length: 58 m
Height: 6.8 m (rear section) |Burial Facility = Unknown |burial goods Found = [[Haniwa]], [[Sue pottery]], [[Haji pottery]] |Construction Period = [[5th century]] late |Historic Site Designation = Prefectural Historic Site: "Tsukayama South Kofun" |Special Notes = Excavated artifacts designated as cultural properties of Utsunomiya City }} '''Tsukayama South Kofun''' (塚山南古墳) is a kofun located south of Tsukayama West Kofun. It is [[Scallop-shaped kofun|scallop-shaped]] and designated as a historic site by Tochigi Prefecture. The mound has a short front section and a rear circular section, oriented southward. The dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}: * Total Kofun Length: 70.6 meters (including moat). * Mound Length: 58.0 meters. * Rear Circular Section ** Diameter: 42.1 meters ** Height: 6.8 meters * Front Section ** Length: 13.5 meters ** Height: 4.1 meters The mound is two-tiered{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. Numerous artifacts, including cylindrical haniwa, figurative haniwa (human, horse, deer, and house shapes), large Sue pottery vessels, and Haji pottery, were recovered, though no evidence of surface stones was found{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. A horseshoe-shaped moat surrounds the mound (narrower on the northwest side due to proximity to Tsukayama West Kofun){{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. Burial facilities have not been fully investigated, but depressions and red-painted stones suggest a vertical burial system at the mound's summit, likely plundered{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. [[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kofun in Japan]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]] [[Category:11]][[sn:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya)]][[Category:11]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya)]][[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:01-17]][[ja:塚山古墳群]] The construction period is estimated to be the late 5th century to early 6th century, following Tsukayama West Kofun{{Sfn|Tsukayama Kofun Group (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}. == Cultural Properties == === Tochigi Prefectural Cultural Properties === * Historic Sites ** {{ill|Tsukayama Kofun|ja|塚山古墳}} - Designated on April 13, 1973 (Showa 48).[http://www.tochigi-edu.ed.jp/center/bunkazai/2341040.htm 塚山南古墳] (Cultural Property Section, Tochigi Prefectural Board of Education).[https://utsunomiya-8story.jp/search_post/%e5%a1%9a%e5%b1%b1%e5%8d%97%e5%8f%a4%e5%a2%b3/ 塚山南古墳] (Utsunomiya Historical and Cultural Resources Promotion Council). === Utsunomiya City Designated Cultural Properties === * Tangible Cultural Properties ** Artifacts excavated from {{ill|Tsukayama Minami Kofun|ja|塚山南古墳}} (archaeological materials) - Designated on November 7, 2005 (Heisei 17). Mound (Right: front section; Left-back: rear circular section) | Alternate name = Hyōgo-zuka Kofun | Group = Tsukayama Kofun Cluster | location = Nishikawada-machi 7-chome, {{ill|Utsunomiya City|ja|宇都宮市}}, Tochigi Prefecture | Coordinates = {{Coord|36|30|22.05|N|139|51|39.50|E|region:JP-09_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Tsukayama Kofun}} | Shape = {{ill|Keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} (Kenbishi-style) | Dimensions = Total mound length: 98.3 meters | Burial Facility = Unknown | Artifacts = {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}}, {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器}}, {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器}} | Kofuns = | Construction Era = Mid-5th century | Buried Figure = | Mausoleum = | Historical Site = Tochigi Prefecture-designated Historical Site (Tsukayama Kofun) | Cultural Asset = | Notes = | Map2 = {{location map|Japan Tochigi|label=Tsukayama Kofun|lat_deg=36|lat_min=30|lat_sec=22.05|lon_deg=139|lon_min=51|lon_sec=39.5|mark=前方後円墳-西南西.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=top|width=200|caption=}} }} {{OSM location map | coord = {{Coord|36|30|20|N|139|51|38|E}} | zoom = 17 | float = right | width = 300 | height = 250 | caption = {{center|Distribution map of the Tsukayama Kofun Cluster}} | scalemark = 60 | mark-coord1 = {{Coord|36|30|22.05|N|139|51|39.50|E}} | label1 = Tsukayama Kofun | label-pos1 = top | label-color1 = black | mark1 = 前方後円墳-西南西.svg | mark-size1 = 70 | mark-coord2 = {{Coord|36|30|20.25|N|139|51|36.35|E}} | label2 = Tsukayama West Kofun | label-pos2 = top | label-color2 = black | mark2 = 帆立貝形古墳-南南東.svg | mark-size2 = 60 | mark-coord3 = {{Coord|36|30|17.93|N|139|51|37.23|E}} | label3 = Tsukayama South Kofun | label-pos3 = left | label-color3 = black | mark3 = 帆立貝形古墳-南.svg | mark-size3 = 60 }} '''Tsukayama Kofun''' (塚山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in Nishikawada-machi, {{ill|Utsunomiya City|ja|宇都宮市}}, Tochigi Prefecture. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} and part of the {{ill|Tsukayama Kofun Cluster|ja|塚山古墳群}}. It has been designated as a Tochigi Prefecture-designated historical site. This article also covers the {{ill|Tsukayama Kofun Cluster|ja|塚山古墳群}}, for which Tsukayama Kofun serves as the main mound. [[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]] [[Category:Completion tier 6]][[Category: tier 6]][[Category: tier 6]] [[Category:11]][[sn:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya)]][[Category:11]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya)]][[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:01-17]][[ja:塚山古墳 (宇都宮市)]] == Overview == [[File:100425 Tsukayama Kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|{{center|Aerial view of the Tsukayama Kofun Cluster (2010)}}{{small|Top right: Tsukayama Kofun; Left: Tsukayama West Kofun; Bottom left: Tsukayama South Kofun. {{ill|Aerial photographs of Japan|ja|国土航空写真}}.}}]] Located in southern Tochigi Prefecture, the mound was constructed on a plateau between the {{ill|Tagawa River (Tone River System)|ja|田川 (利根川水系)}} and {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}}. It is the largest keyhole-shaped kofun in the Tsukayama Kofun Cluster, which includes several mounds such as the scallop-shaped Tsukayama West and South Kofun, as well as {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}}-based coffins. The rear circular section has been partially leveled by road construction. In 1989 (Heisei 1), a survey was conducted, followed by four excavation campaigns from 1989 to 1991. The mound has a "Kenbishi-style" keyhole shape with a protruding front section oriented westward. It is constructed in three tiers, with external surfaces featuring {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}}. Cylindrical {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}}, {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器}} (TK216-208 style), and {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器}} have been excavated. The southern neck of the mound features a {{ill|tsukuridashi|ja|造出|1=Platform-style projection}}, and the shield-shaped moat surrounding the mound brings the total length to 119.2 meters. The burial facility remains unexamined, and grave goods are largely unknown. The mound is estimated to date from the mid-5th century, during the middle {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} (or the late 5th century, according to other estimates). It served as a prominent burial site for regional leaders in the southern Utsunomiya area and is considered critical for studying the political dynamics of the {{ill|Shimotsukeno region|ja|下毛野地方}}. The site was designated as a Tochigi Prefecture historical site in 1953 (Shōwa 28). Today, the mound is adorned with {{ill|Dodantsutsuji shrubs|ja|ドウダンツツジ}}, offering a unique landscape that has been developed for preservation. == Ruins History == * [[1953]] (Showa 28), November 10: Tsukayama Kofun was designated as a historic site by Tochigi Prefecture. * [[1966]] (Showa 41): Construction planning for [[National Route 121]] (part of the [[Utsunomiya Ring Road]]) began. The plans were revised to include a tunnel near the kofun group to protect cultural properties. * [[1973]] (Showa 48), April 13: Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun were designated as historic sites by Tochigi Prefecture. * [[1976]] (Showa 51): Excavations of Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama East Kofun were conducted due to road construction (reported by the Tochigi Prefectural Board of Education in [[1979]]). * [[1989]]-[[1991]] (Heisei 1-3): Excavations of Tsukayama Kofun were carried out by the Archaeological Research Society of [[Utsunomiya University]] (findings published in [[1995]]). * [[1991]]-[[1992]] (Heisei 3-4): Excavations of the Tsukayama Kofun Group were conducted during road improvement work by the Utsunomiya City Board of Education (findings published in [[1996]]). * [[1995]]-[[1997]] (Heisei 7-9): Excavations of Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun were carried out for historic site conservation by the Utsunomiya City Board of Education, Utsunomiya University, and [[Utsunomiya Bunsei Junior College]] (findings published in [[2003]]). * [[2005]] (Heisei 17), November 7: Artifacts excavated from Tsukayama South Kofun were designated as tangible cultural properties by Utsunomiya City. [[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kofun in Japan]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]] [[Category:11]][[sn:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya)]][[Category:11]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya)]][[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:01-17]][[ja:塚山古墳群の歴史]] == Mound == The dimensions of the mound are as follows{{Sfn|Tsukayama Kofun Group (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}: * Total Kofun Length: 119.2 meters - The overall length of the kofun, including the surrounding moat. * Mound Length: 98.3 meters * Rear Circular Section Diameter: 55.9 meters * Front Section Width: 59.9 meters File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), funkyu-4.jpg|Mound and surrounding moat. File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), funkyu-3.jpg|Mound
{{small|Rear circular section on the left, front section in the right background.}} File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), funcho.jpg|Summit of the rear circular section. File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), kouenbu.jpg|View from the front section toward the rear circular section. File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), zenpoubu.jpg|View from the rear circular section toward the front section. [[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kofun in Japan]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]] [[Category:11]][[sn:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya)]][[Category:11]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya)]][[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:01-17]][[ja:塚山古墳群の墳丘]] == Tsukayama Kofun Group == The '''Tsukayama Kofun Group''' consists of a cluster of kofun (ancient Kofuns) with Tsukayama Kofun as the main mound. Originally composed of over 10 kofun, it currently includes one [[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped kofun]] (Tsukayama Kofun), two [[Scallop-shaped kofun|scallop-shaped kofun]] (Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun), and one round kofun (No. 6 Kofun). Investigations have identified six small round kofun (Nos. 4, 5, 7, 8, and two within the old shooting range) to the north of Tsukayama Kofun. To the west and southwest, from north to south, lie a mid-sized round kofun (No. 6), Tsukayama West Kofun, and Tsukayama South Kofun. Haniwa sarcophagi have also been discovered in the area, with one featuring an engraved depiction of four deer in alternating male and female pairs. The construction period is estimated to span the mid-5th century to the early 6th century during the mid- to late-Kofun period, following the [[Mobara Kofun Group]] and the {{ill|Higashitani Kofun Group|ja|東谷古墳群}}. The kofun group is detailed as follows: {| class="wikitable" style="text-align:center;background:#ffffff;white-space:nowrap;font-size:85%" |+List of Tsukayama Kofun GroupTsukayama Kofun Group Pamphlet.Historic Site Information Board. ! Artifacts designated as cultural properties of Utsunomiya City |- |'''No. 4 Kofun'''||[[Enpun|Round kofun]]||Diameter: 8 m||style="text-align:left"|Pottery|| ||(Destroyed)|| |- |'''No. 5 Kofun'''||Round kofun||Diameter: 7 m||style="text-align:left"|Traces of wooden coffins, cylindrical haniwa, pottery, jewelry|| ||(Destroyed)|| |- |'''No. 6 Kofun'''||Round kofun||Diameter: 20 m||style="text-align:left"|Cylindrical haniwa, pottery|| ||None|| |- |'''No. 7 Kofun'''||Round kofun|| ||style="text-align:left"|Figurative haniwa (birds), pottery|| ||(Destroyed)|| |- |'''No. 8 Kofun'''||Round kofun|| ||style="text-align:left"|Cylindrical haniwa, pottery|| ||(Destroyed)|| |- |Two Kofun within Old Shooting Range||Round kofun|| ||style="text-align:left"|Cylindrical haniwa, figurative haniwa (birds, armor)|| ||(Destroyed)|| |- |Five Haniwa Sarcophagi||Haniwa Sarcophagi|| ||style="text-align:left"|Cylindrical haniwa|| ||(Destroyed)|| |} File:Tsukayama Kofun Group (Utsunomiya)-6, funkyu.jpg|No. 6 Kofun === Tsukayama West Kofun === {{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]] |name = Tsukayama West Kofun |image = [[File:Tsukayama Nishi Kofun (Utsunomiya), funkyu-2.jpg|280px]]
Mound (rear circular section in the center, front section in the background) |Alias = |location = [[Tochigi Prefecture|Tochigi]], [[Utsunomiya]] Nishikawada Town Higashihara |Shape = [[Scallop-shaped kofun]] |Size = Mound length: 63.1 m
Height: 6.7 m (rear section) |Burial Facility = Unknown |burial goods Found = [[Haniwa]], [[Sue pottery]] |Construction Period = [[5th century]] late |Historic Site Designation = Prefectural Historic Site: "Tsukayama West Kofun" |Special Notes = }} '''Tsukayama West Kofun''' (塚山西古墳) is a kofun located southwest of Tsukayama Kofun. It is [[Scallop-shaped kofun|scallop-shaped]] and designated as a historic site by Tochigi Prefecture. The mound has a short front section and a rear circular section, oriented to the south-southeast. The dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}: * Total Kofun Length: 74.1 meters (including moat). * Mound Length: 63.1 meters. * Rear Circular Section ** Diameter: 44.5 meters ** Height: 6.7 meters * Front Section ** Length: ~18 meters ** Width: ~22 meters ** Height: ~1.5 meters The mound comprises two or more tiers (upper tiers heavily disturbed){{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. Cylindrical haniwa and Sue pottery (TK208-TK23 styles) were found on the mound's surface{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. A horseshoe-shaped moat surrounds the mound (shallow on the east side due to proximity to Tsukayama Kofun){{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. Burial facilities are unknown due to limited findings; no clay or stone structures have been detected{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. The construction period is estimated to be the late 5th century, following Tsukayama Kofun and preceding Tsukayama South Kofun{{Sfn|Tsukayama Kofun Group (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}. === Tsukayama South Kofun === {{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]] |name = Tsukayama South Kofun |image = [[File:Tsukayama Minami Kofun (Utsunomiya), funkyu-2.jpg|280px]]
Mound (rear circular section in the center, front section in the background) |Alias = |location = [[Tochigi Prefecture|Tochigi]], [[Utsunomiya]] Nishikawada Town Higashihara |Shape = [[Scallop-shaped kofun]] |Size = Mound length: 58 m
Height: 6.8 m (rear section) |Burial Facility = Unknown |burial goods Found = [[Haniwa]], [[Sue pottery]], [[Haji pottery]] |Construction Period = [[5th century]] late |Historic Site Designation = Prefectural Historic Site: "Tsukayama South Kofun" |Special Notes = Excavated artifacts designated as cultural properties of Utsunomiya City }} '''Tsukayama South Kofun''' (塚山南古墳) is a kofun located south of Tsukayama West Kofun. It is [[Scallop-shaped kofun|scallop-shaped]] and designated as a historic site by Tochigi Prefecture. The mound has a short front section and a rear circular section, oriented southward. The dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}: * Total Kofun Length: 70.6 meters (including moat). * Mound Length: 58.0 meters. * Rear Circular Section ** Diameter: 42.1 meters ** Height: 6.8 meters * Front Section ** Length: 13.5 meters ** Height: 4.1 meters The mound is two-tiered{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. Numerous artifacts, including cylindrical haniwa, figurative haniwa (human, horse, deer, and house shapes), large Sue pottery vessels, and Haji pottery, were recovered, though no evidence of surface stones was found{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. A horseshoe-shaped moat surrounds the mound (narrower on the northwest side due to proximity to Tsukayama West Kofun){{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. Burial facilities have not been fully investigated, but depressions and red-painted stones suggest a vertical burial system at the mound's summit, likely plundered{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. Mound (Right: front section; Left-back: rear circular section) | Alternate name = Hyōgo-zuka Kofun | Group = Tsukayama Kofun Cluster | location = Nishikawada-machi 7-chome, {{ill|Utsunomiya City|ja|宇都宮市}}, Tochigi Prefecture | Coordinates = {{Coord|36|30|22.05|N|139|51|39.50|E|region:JP-09_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Tsukayama Kofun}} | Shape = {{ill|Keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} (Kenbishi-style) | Dimensions = Total mound length: 98.3 meters | Burial Facility = Unknown | Artifacts = {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}}, {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器}}, {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器}} | Kofuns = | Construction Era = Mid-5th century | Buried Figure = | Mausoleum = | Historical Site = Tochigi Prefecture-designated Historical Site (Tsukayama Kofun) | Cultural Asset = | Notes = | Map2 = {{location map|Japan Tochigi|label=Tsukayama Kofun|lat_deg=36|lat_min=30|lat_sec=22.05|lon_deg=139|lon_min=51|lon_sec=39.5|mark=前方後円墳-西南西.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=top|width=200|caption=}} }} {{OSM location map | coord = {{Coord|36|30|20|N|139|51|38|E}} | zoom = 17 | float = right | width = 300 | height = 250 | caption = {{center|Distribution map of the Tsukayama Kofun Cluster}} | scalemark = 60 | mark-coord1 = {{Coord|36|30|22.05|N|139|51|39.50|E}} | label1 = Tsukayama Kofun | label-pos1 = top | label-color1 = black | mark1 = 前方後円墳-西南西.svg | mark-size1 = 70 | mark-coord2 = {{Coord|36|30|20.25|N|139|51|36.35|E}} | label2 = Tsukayama West Kofun | label-pos2 = top | label-color2 = black | mark2 = 帆立貝形古墳-南南東.svg | mark-size2 = 60 | mark-coord3 = {{Coord|36|30|17.93|N|139|51|37.23|E}} | label3 = Tsukayama South Kofun | label-pos3 = left | label-color3 = black | mark3 = 帆立貝形古墳-南.svg | mark-size3 = 60 }} '''Tsukayama Kofun''' (塚山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in Nishikawada-machi, {{ill|Utsunomiya City|ja|宇都宮市}}, Tochigi Prefecture. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} and part of the {{ill|Tsukayama Kofun Cluster|ja|塚山古墳群}}. It has been designated as a Tochigi Prefecture-designated historical site. This article also covers the {{ill|Tsukayama Kofun Cluster|ja|塚山古墳群}}, for which Tsukayama Kofun serves as the main mound. [[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]] [[Category:Completion tier 6]][[Category: tier 6]][[Category: tier 6]] [[Category:11]][[sn:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya)]][[Category:11]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya)]][[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[ja:塚山古墳 (宇都宮市)]] == Overview == [[File:100425 Tsukayama Kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|{{center|Aerial view of the Tsukayama Kofun Cluster (2010)}}{{small|Top right: Tsukayama Kofun; Left: Tsukayama West Kofun; Bottom left: Tsukayama South Kofun. {{ill|Aerial photographs of Japan|ja|国土航空写真}}.}}]] Located in southern Tochigi Prefecture, the mound was constructed on a plateau between the {{ill|Tagawa River (Tone River System)|ja|田川 (利根川水系)}} and {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}}. It is the largest keyhole-shaped kofun in the Tsukayama Kofun Cluster, which includes several mounds such as the scallop-shaped Tsukayama West and South Kofun, as well as {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}}-based coffins. The rear circular section has been partially leveled by road construction. In 1989 (Heisei 1), a survey was conducted, followed by four excavation campaigns from 1989 to 1991. The mound has a "Kenbishi-style" keyhole shape with a protruding front section oriented westward. It is constructed in three tiers, with external surfaces featuring {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}}. Cylindrical {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}}, {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器}} (TK216-208 style), and {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器}} have been excavated. The southern neck of the mound features a {{ill|tsukuridashi|ja|造出|1=Platform-style projection}}, and the shield-shaped moat surrounding the mound brings the total length to 119.2 meters. The burial facility remains unexamined, and grave goods are largely unknown. The mound is estimated to date from the mid-5th century, during the middle {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} (or the late 5th century, according to other estimates). It served as a prominent burial site for regional leaders in the southern Utsunomiya area and is considered critical for studying the political dynamics of the {{ill|Shimotsukeno region|ja|下毛野地方}}. The site was designated as a Tochigi Prefecture historical site in 1953 (Shōwa 28). Today, the mound is adorned with {{ill|Dodantsutsuji shrubs|ja|ドウダンツツジ}}, offering a unique landscape that has been developed for preservation. == Ruins History == * [[1953]] (Showa 28), November 10: Tsukayama Kofun was designated as a historic site by Tochigi Prefecture. * [[1966]] (Showa 41): Construction planning for [[National Route 121]] (part of the [[Utsunomiya Ring Road]]) began. The plans were revised to include a tunnel near the kofun group to protect cultural properties. * [[1973]] (Showa 48), April 13: Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun were designated as historic sites by Tochigi Prefecture. * [[1976]] (Showa 51): Excavations of Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama East Kofun were conducted due to road construction (reported by the Tochigi Prefectural Board of Education in [[1979]]). * [[1989]]-[[1991]] (Heisei 1-3): Excavations of Tsukayama Kofun were carried out by the Archaeological Research Society of [[Utsunomiya University]] (findings published in [[1995]]). * [[1991]]-[[1992]] (Heisei 3-4): Excavations of the Tsukayama Kofun Group were conducted during road improvement work by the Utsunomiya City Board of Education (findings published in [[1996]]). * [[1995]]-[[1997]] (Heisei 7-9): Excavations of Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun were carried out for historic site conservation by the Utsunomiya City Board of Education, Utsunomiya University, and [[Utsunomiya Bunsei Junior College]] (findings published in [[2003]]). * [[2005]] (Heisei 17), November 7: Artifacts excavated from Tsukayama South Kofun were designated as tangible cultural properties by Utsunomiya City. [[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kofun in Japan]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]] [[Category:11]][[sn:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya)]][[Category:11]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya)]][[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[ja:塚山古墳群の歴史]] == Mound == The dimensions of the mound are as follows{{Sfn|Tsukayama Kofun Group (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}: * Total Kofun Length: 119.2 meters - The overall length of the kofun, including the surrounding moat. * Mound Length: 98.3 meters * Rear Circular Section Diameter: 55.9 meters * Front Section Width: 59.9 meters File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), funkyu-4.jpg|Mound and surrounding moat. [[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kofun in Japan]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]] [[Category:11]][[sn:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya)]][[Category:11]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya)]][[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[ja:塚山古墳群の墳丘]] == Tsukayama Kofun Group == The '''Tsukayama Kofun Group''' consists of a cluster of kofun (ancient Kofuns) with Tsukayama Kofun as the main mound. Originally composed of over 10 kofun, it currently includes one [[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped kofun]] (Tsukayama Kofun), two [[Scallop-shaped kofun|scallop-shaped kofun]] (Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun), and one round kofun (No. 6 Kofun). Investigations have identified six small round kofun (Nos. 4, 5, 7, 8, and two within the old shooting range) to the north of Tsukayama Kofun. To the west and southwest, from north to south, lie a mid-sized round kofun (No. 6), Tsukayama West Kofun, and Tsukayama South Kofun. Haniwa sarcophagi have also been discovered in the area, with one featuring an engraved depiction of four deer in alternating male and female pairs. The construction period is estimated to span the mid-5th century to the early 6th century during the mid- to late-Kofun period, following the [[Mobara Kofun Group]] and the {{ill|Higashitani Kofun Group|ja|東谷古墳群}}. The kofun group is detailed as follows: {| class="wikitable" style="text-align:center;background:#ffffff;white-space:nowrap;font-size:85%" |+List of Tsukayama Kofun GroupTsukayama Kofun Group Pamphlet.Historic Site Information Board. ! Kofun name ! Shape ! Size ! Artifacts Found ! Construction Period ! Historic Site Designation ! Notes |- |'''No. 1 Kofun
(Tsukayama Kofun)'''||[[Zenpokoenfun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]]||Mound length: 98 m||style="text-align:left"|Cylindrical haniwa, Sue pottery||Mid-5th century||Prefectural Designation||style="text-align:left"|Survey: 1989
Excavation: 1989, 1990, 1991 |- |'''No. 2 Kofun
(Tsukayama West Kofun)'''||[[Scallop-shaped kofun]]||Mound length: 63 m||style="text-align:left"|Cylindrical haniwa, Sue pottery||Late 5th century||Prefectural Designation||style="text-align:left"|Survey: 1976, 1995
Excavation: 1976, 1990, 1995, 1996 |- |'''No. 3 Kofun
(Tsukayama South Kofun)'''||Scallop-shaped kofun||Mound length: 58 m||style="text-align:left"|Cylindrical haniwa, Sue pottery, Haji pottery||Late 5th century||Prefectural Designation||style="text-align:left"|Survey: 1976, 1996
Excavation: 1976, 1996, 1997, 1998
Artifacts designated as cultural properties of Utsunomiya City |- |'''No. 4 Kofun'''||[[Enpun|Round kofun]]||Diameter: 8 m||style="text-align:left"|Pottery|| ||(Destroyed)|| |- |'''No. 5 Kofun'''||Round kofun||Diameter: 7 m||style="text-align:left"|Traces of wooden coffins, cylindrical haniwa, pottery, jewelry|| ||(Destroyed)|| |- |'''No. 6 Kofun'''||Round kofun||Diameter: 20 m||style="text-align:left"|Cylindrical haniwa, pottery|| ||None|| |- |'''No. 7 Kofun'''||Round kofun|| ||style="text-align:left"|Figurative haniwa (birds), pottery|| ||(Destroyed)|| |- |'''No. 8 Kofun'''||Round kofun|| ||style="text-align:left"|Cylindrical haniwa, pottery|| ||(Destroyed)|| |- |Two Kofun within Old Shooting Range||Round kofun|| ||style="text-align:left"|Cylindrical haniwa, figurative haniwa (birds, armor)|| ||(Destroyed)|| |- |Five Haniwa Sarcophagi||Haniwa Sarcophagi|| ||style="text-align:left"|Cylindrical haniwa|| ||(Destroyed)|| |} File:Tsukayama Kofun Group (Utsunomiya)-6, funkyu.jpg|No. 6 Kofun === Tsukayama West Kofun === {{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]] |name = Tsukayama West Kofun |image = [[File:Tsukayama Nishi Kofun (Utsunomiya), funkyu-2.jpg|280px]]
Mound (rear circular section in the center, front section in the background) |Alias = |location = [[Tochigi Prefecture|Tochigi]], [[Utsunomiya]] Nishikawada Town Higashihara |Shape = [[Scallop-shaped kofun]] |Size = Mound length: 63.1 m
Height: 6.7 m (rear section) |Burial Facility = Unknown |burial goods Found = [[Haniwa]], [[Sue pottery]] |Construction Period = [[5th century]] late |Historic Site Designation = Prefectural Historic Site: "Tsukayama West Kofun" |Special Notes = }} '''Tsukayama West Kofun''' (塚山西古墳) is a kofun located southwest of Tsukayama Kofun. It is [[Scallop-shaped kofun|scallop-shaped]] and designated as a historic site by Tochigi Prefecture. The mound has a short front section and a rear circular section, oriented to the south-southeast. The dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}: * Total Kofun Length: 74.1 meters (including moat). * Mound Length: 63.1 meters. * Rear Circular Section ** Diameter: 44.5 meters ** Height: 6.7 meters * Front Section ** Length: ~18 meters ** Width: ~22 meters ** Height: ~1.5 meters The mound comprises two or more tiers (upper tiers heavily disturbed){{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. Cylindrical haniwa and Sue pottery (TK208-TK23 styles) were found on the mound's surface{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. A horseshoe-shaped moat surrounds the mound (shallow on the east side due to proximity to Tsukayama Kofun){{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. Burial facilities are unknown due to limited findings; no clay or stone structures have been detected{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. The construction period is estimated to be the late 5th century, following Tsukayama Kofun and preceding Tsukayama South Kofun{{Sfn|Tsukayama Kofun Group (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}. === Tsukayama South Kofun === {{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]] |name = Tsukayama South Kofun |image = [[File:Tsukayama Minami Kofun (Utsunomiya), funkyu-2.jpg|280px]]
Mound (rear circular section in the center, front section in the background) |Alias = |location = [[Tochigi Prefecture|Tochigi]], [[Utsunomiya]] Nishikawada Town Higashihara |Shape = [[Scallop-shaped kofun]] |Size = Mound length: 58 m
Height: 6.8 m (rear section) |Burial Facility = Unknown |burial goods Found = [[Haniwa]], [[Sue pottery]], [[Haji pottery]] |Construction Period = [[5th century]] late |Historic Site Designation = Prefectural Historic Site: "Tsukayama South Kofun" |Special Notes = Excavated artifacts designated as cultural properties of Utsunomiya City }} '''Tsukayama South Kofun''' (塚山南古墳) is a kofun located south of Tsukayama West Kofun. It is [[Scallop-shaped kofun|scallop-shaped]] and designated as a historic site by Tochigi Prefecture. The mound has a short front section and a rear circular section, oriented southward. The dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}: * Total Kofun Length: 70.6 meters (including moat). * Mound Length: 58.0 meters. * Rear Circular Section ** Diameter: 42.1 meters ** Height: 6.8 meters * Front Section ** Length: 13.5 meters ** Height: 4.1 meters The mound is two-tiered{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. Numerous artifacts, including cylindrical haniwa, figurative haniwa (human, horse, deer, and house shapes), large Sue pottery vessels, and Haji pottery, were recovered, though no evidence of surface stones was found{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. A horseshoe-shaped moat surrounds the mound (narrower on the northwest side due to proximity to Tsukayama West Kofun){{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. Burial facilities have not been fully investigated, but depressions and red-painted stones suggest a vertical burial system at the mound's summit, likely plundered{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. Designated on April 13, 1973 (Showa 48).[http://www.tochigi-edu.ed.jp/center/bunkazai/2341039.htm 塚山西古墳] (Cultural Property Section, Tochigi Prefectural Board of Education).[https://utsunomiya-8story.jp/search_post/%e5%a1%9a%e5%b1%b1%e8%a5%bf%e5%8f%a4%e5%a2%b3/ 塚山西古墳] (Utsunomiya Historical and Cultural Resources Promotion Council). ** {{ill|Tsukayama Minami Kofun|ja|塚山南古墳}} - Designated on April 13, 1973 (Showa 48).[http://www.tochigi-edu.ed.jp/center/bunkazai/2341040.htm 塚山南古墳] (Cultural Property Section, Tochigi Prefectural Board of Education).[https://utsunomiya-8story.jp/search_post/%e5%a1%9a%e5%b1%b1%e5%8d%97%e5%8f%a4%e5%a2%b3/ 塚山南古墳] (Utsunomiya Historical and Cultural Resources Promotion Council). === Utsunomiya City Designated Cultural Properties === * Tangible Cultural Properties ** Artifacts excavated from {{ill|Tsukayama Minami Kofun|ja|塚山南古墳}} (archaeological materials) - Designated on November 7, 2005 (Heisei 17). {{afc comment|1=I hope this is not too annoying but this article is gonna be placed under [[:Category:Pages using infobox ancient site with unknown parameters]] and there is a decent chance these unknown parameters are ones[[Category:marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] I want added to the main template like burial chamber structure and burial goods. Please do not use any bots that just remove the unknown parameters without looking at them. This was added through [[Special:MassEditRegex]] to all pages with the category so apologies if it was just some kind of an error like the image parameter being in Japanese[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 06:00, 27 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]] | name = Tsukayama Kofun | image = [[File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), funkyu-2.jpg|280px]]
Mound (Right: front section; Left-back: rear circular section) | Alternate name = Hyōgo-zuka Kofun | Group = Tsukayama Kofun Cluster | location = Nishikawada-machi 7-chome, {{ill|Utsunomiya City|ja|宇都宮市}}, Tochigi Prefecture | Coordinates = {{Coord|36|30|22.05|N|139|51|39.50|E|region:JP-09_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Tsukayama Kofun}} | Shape = {{ill|Keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} (Kenbishi-style) | Dimensions = Total mound length: 98.3 meters | Burial Facility = Unknown | Artifacts = {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}}, {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}}, {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器}} | Kofuns = | Construction Era = Mid-5th century | Buried Figure = | Mausoleum = | Historical Site = Tochigi Prefecture-designated Historical Site (Tsukayama Kofun) | Cultural Asset = | Notes = | Map2 = {{location map|Japan Tochigi|label=Tsukayama Kofun|lat_deg=36|lat_min=30|lat_sec=22.05|lon_deg=139|lon_min=51|lon_sec=39.5|mark=前方後円墳-西南西.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=top|width=200|caption=}} }} {{OSM location map | coord = {{Coord|36|30|20|N|139|51|38|E}} | zoom = 17 | float = right | width = 300 | height = 250 | caption = {{center|Distribution map of the Tsukayama Kofun Cluster}} | scalemark = 60 | mark-coord1 = {{Coord|36|30|22.05|N|139|51|39.50|E}} | label1 = Tsukayama Kofun | label-pos1 = top | label-color1 = black | mark1 = 前方後円墳-西南西.svg | mark-size1 = 70 | mark-coord2 = {{Coord|36|30|20.25|N|139|51|36.35|E}} | label2 = Tsukayama West Kofun | label-pos2 = top | label-color2 = black | mark2 = 帆立貝形古墳-南南東.svg | mark-size2 = 60 | mark-coord3 = {{Coord|36|30|17.93|N|139|51|37.23|E}} | label3 = Tsukayama South Kofun | label-pos3 = left | label-color3 = black | mark3 = 帆立貝形古墳-南.svg | mark-size3 = 60 }} '''Tsukayama Kofun''' (塚山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in Nishikawada-machi, {{ill|Utsunomiya City|ja|宇都宮市}}, Tochigi Prefecture. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} and part of the {{ill|Tsukayama Kofun Cluster|ja|塚山古墳群}}. It has been designated as a Tochigi Prefecture-designated historical site. This article also covers the {{ill|Tsukayama Kofun Cluster|ja|塚山古墳群}}, for which Tsukayama Kofun serves as the main mound. [[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]] [[Category:Completion tier 6]][[Category: tier 6]][[Category: tier 6]] [[Category:11]][[sn:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya)]][[Category:11]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya)]][[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[ja:塚山古墳 (宇都宮市)]] == Overview == [[File:100425 Tsukayama Kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|{{center|Aerial view of the Tsukayama Kofun Cluster (2010)}}{{small|Top right: Tsukayama Kofun; Left: Tsukayama West Kofun; Bottom left: Tsukayama South Kofun. {{ill|Aerial photographs of Japan|ja|国土航空写真}}.}}]] Located in southern Tochigi Prefecture, the mound was constructed on a plateau between the {{ill|Tagawa River (Tone River System)|ja|田川 (利根川水系)}} and {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}}. It is the largest keyhole-shaped kofun in the Tsukayama Kofun Cluster, which includes several mounds such as the scallop-shaped Tsukayama West and South Kofun, as well as {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}}-based coffins. The rear circular section has been partially leveled by road construction. In 1989 (Heisei 1), a survey was conducted, followed by four excavation campaigns from 1989 to 1991. The mound has a "Kenbishi-style" keyhole shape with a protruding front section oriented westward. It is constructed in three tiers, with external surfaces featuring {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}}. Cylindrical {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}}, {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} (TK216-208 style), and {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器}} have been excavated. The southern neck of the mound features a {{ill|tsukuridashi|ja|造出|1=Platform-style projection}}, and the shield-shaped moat surrounding the mound brings the total length to 119.2 meters. The burial facility remains unexamined, and grave goods are largely unknown. The mound is estimated to date from the mid-5th century, during the middle {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} (or the late 5th century, according to other estimates). It served as a prominent burial site for regional leaders in the southern Utsunomiya area and is considered critical for studying the political dynamics of the {{ill|Shimotsukeno region|ja|下毛野地方}}. The site was designated as a Tochigi Prefecture historical site in 1953 (Shōwa 28). Today, the mound is adorned with {{ill|Dodantsutsuji shrubs|ja|ドウダンツツジ}}, offering a unique landscape that has been developed for preservation. == Ruins History == * [[1953]] (Showa 28), November 10: Tsukayama Kofun was designated as a historic site by Tochigi Prefecture. * [[1966]] (Showa 41): Construction planning for [[National Route 121]] (part of the [[Utsunomiya Ring Road]]) began. The plans were revised to include a tunnel near the kofun group to protect cultural properties. * [[1973]] (Showa 48), April 13: Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun were designated as historic sites by Tochigi Prefecture. * [[1976]] (Showa 51): Excavations of Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama East Kofun were conducted due to road construction (reported by the Tochigi Prefectural Board of Education in [[1979]]). * [[1989]]-[[1991]] (Heisei 1-3): Excavations of Tsukayama Kofun were carried out by the Archaeological Research Society of [[Utsunomiya University]] (findings published in [[1995]]). * [[1991]]-[[1992]] (Heisei 3-4): Excavations of the Tsukayama Kofun Group were conducted during road improvement work by the Utsunomiya City Board of Education (findings published in [[1996]]). * [[1995]]-[[1997]] (Heisei 7-9): Excavations of Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun were carried out for historic site conservation by the Utsunomiya City Board of Education, Utsunomiya University, and [[Utsunomiya Bunsei Junior College]] (findings published in [[2003]]). * [[2005]] (Heisei 17), November 7: Artifacts excavated from Tsukayama South Kofun were designated as tangible cultural properties by Utsunomiya City. [[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kofun in Japan]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]] [[Category:11]][[sn:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya)]][[Category:11]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya)]][[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[ja:塚山古墳群の歴史]] == Mound == The dimensions of the mound are as follows{{Sfn|Tsukayama Kofun Group (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}: * Total Kofun Length: 119.2 meters - The overall length of the kofun, including the surrounding moat. * Mound Length: 98.3 meters * Rear Circular Section Diameter: 55.9 meters * Front Section Width: 59.9 meters File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), funkyu-4.jpg|Mound and surrounding moat. File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), funkyu-3.jpg|Mound
{{small|Rear circular section on the left, front section in the right background.}} File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), funcho.jpg|Summit of the rear circular section. File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), kouenbu.jpg|View from the front section toward the rear circular section. File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), zenpoubu.jpg|View from the rear circular section toward the front section. [[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kofun in Japan]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]] [[Category:11]][[sn:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya)]][[Category:11]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya)]][[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:11]][[Category:kk]][[ja:塚山古墳群の墳丘]] == Tsukayama Kofun Group == The '''Tsukayama Kofun Group''' consists of a cluster of kofun (ancient Kofuns) with Tsukayama Kofun as the main mound. Originally composed of over 10 kofun, it currently includes one [[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped kofun]] (Tsukayama Kofun), two [[Scallop-shaped kofun|scallop-shaped kofun]] (Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun), and one round kofun (No. 6 Kofun). Investigations have identified six small round kofun (Nos. 4, 5, 7, 8, and two within the old shooting range) to the north of Tsukayama Kofun. To the west and southwest, from north to south, lie a mid-sized round kofun (No. 6), Tsukayama West Kofun, and Tsukayama South Kofun. Haniwa sarcophagi have also been discovered in the area, with one featuring an engraved depiction of four deer in alternating male and female pairs. The construction period is estimated to span the mid-5th century to the early 6th century during the mid- to late-Kofun period, following the [[Mobara Kofun Group]] and the {{ill|Higashitani Kofun Group|ja|東谷古墳群}}. The kofun group is detailed as follows: {| class="wikitable" style="text-align:center;background:#ffffff;white-space:nowrap;font-size:85%" |+List of Tsukayama Kofun GroupTsukayama Kofun Group Pamphlet.Historic Site Information Board. ! (Tsukayama West Kofun)'''||[[Scallop-shaped kofun]]||Mound length: 63 m||style="text-align:left"|Cylindrical haniwa, Sue pottery||Late 5th century||Prefectural Designation||style="text-align:left"|Survey: 1976, 1995
