File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), zenpoubu.jpg|View from the rear circular section toward the front section. == Tsukayama Kofun Group == The '''Tsukayama Kofun Group''' consists of a cluster of kofun (ancient Kofuns) with Tsukayama Kofun as the main mound. Originally composed of over 10 kofun, it currently includes one [[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped kofun]] (Tsukayama Kofun), two [[Scallop-shaped kofun|scallop-shaped kofun]] (Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun), and one round kofun (No. 6 Kofun). Investigations have identified six small round kofun (Nos. 4, 5, 7, 8, and two within the old shooting range) to the north of Tsukayama Kofun. To the west and southwest, from north to south, lie a mid-sized round kofun (No. 6), Tsukayama West Kofun, and Tsukayama South Kofun. Haniwa sarcophagi have also been discovered in the area, with one featuring an engraved depiction of four deer in alternating male and female pairs. The construction period is estimated to span the mid-5th century to the early 6th century during the mid- to late-Kofun period, following the [[Mobara Kofun Group]] and the {{ill|Higashitani Kofun Group|ja|東谷古墳群|12=draft|12=draft}}. It is [[Scallop-shaped kofun|scallop-shaped]] and designation1 as a historic site by Tochigi Prefecture. The mound has a short front section and a rear circular section, oriented to the south-southeast. The area are as follows{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}: * Total Kofun Length: 74.1 meters (including moat). * Mound Length: 63.1 meters. * Rear Circular Section ** Diameter: 44.5 meters ** Height: 6.7 meters * Front Section ** Length: ~18 meters ** Width: ~22 meters ** Height: ~1.5 meters The mound comprises two or more tiers (upper tiers heavily disturbed){{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. Cylindrical haniwa and Sue pottery (TK208-TK23 styles) were found on the mound's surface{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. A horseshoe-shaped moat surrounds the mound (shallow on the east side due to proximity to Tsukayama Kofun){{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. burial are unknown due to limited findings; no clay or stone structures have been detected{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. The construction period is estimated to be the late 5th century, following Tsukayama Kofun and preceding Tsukayama South Kofun{{Sfn|Tsukayama Kofun Group (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}. === Tsukayama South Kofun === {{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]] |name = Tsukayama South Kofun |image = [[File:Tsukayama Minami Kofun (Utsunomiya), funkyu-2.jpg|280px]]
Mound (rear circular section in the center, front section in the background) |alternate_name = |location = [[Tochigi Prefecture|Tochigi]], [[Utsunomiya]] Nishikawada Town Higashihara |type = [[Scallop-shaped kofun]] |area = Mound length: 58 m
Height: 6.8 m (rear section) |burial = Unknown |burial goods = [[Haniwa]], [[Sue pottery]], [[Haji pottery]] |built = [[5th century]] late |Historic Site = Prefectural Historic Site: "Tsukayama South Kofun" |notes = excavations designation1 as cultural properties of Utsunomiya City }} '''Tsukayama South Kofun''' (塚山南古墳) is a kofun located south of Tsukayama West Kofun. It is [[Scallop-shaped kofun|scallop-shaped]] and designation1 as a historic site by Tochigi Prefecture. The mound has a short front section and a rear circular section, oriented southward. The area are as follows{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}: * Total Kofun Length: 70.6 meters (including moat). * Mound Length: 58.0 meters. * Rear Circular Section ** Diameter: 42.1 meters ** Height: 6.8 meters * Front Section ** Length: 13.5 meters ** Height: 4.1 meters The mound is two-tiered{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. Numerous burial goods, including cylindrical haniwa, figurative haniwa (human, horse, deer, and house types), large Sue pottery vessels, and Haji pottery, were recovered, though no evidence of surface stones was found{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. A horseshoe-shaped moat surrounds the mound (narrower on the northwest side due to proximity to Tsukayama West Kofun){{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. burial have not been fully investigated, but depressions and red-painted stones suggest a vertical burial system at the mound's summit, likely plundered{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. The construction period is estimated to be the late 5th century to early 6th century, following Tsukayama West Kofun{{Sfn|Tsukayama Kofun Group (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}. == Historic Site == === Tochigi Prefectural Historic Site === * Historic Sites ** {{ill|Tsukayama Kofun|ja|塚山古墳|12=draft|12=draft}} - {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located in Nishikawada-machi, {{ill|Utsunomiya City|ja|宇都宮市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Tochigi Prefecture. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and part of the {{ill|Tsukayama Kofun Cluster|ja|塚山古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. It has been designation1 as a Tochigi Prefecture-designation1 historical site. This article also covers the {{ill|Tsukayama Kofun Cluster|ja|塚山古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, for which Tsukayama Kofun serves as the main mound. == Overview == [[File:100425 Tsukayama Kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|{{center|Aerial view of the Tsukayama Kofun Cluster (2010)}}{{small|Top right: Tsukayama Kofun; Left: Tsukayama West Kofun; Bottom left: Tsukayama South Kofun. {{ill|Aerial photographs of Japan|ja|国土航空写真|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.}}]] Located in southern Tochigi Prefecture, the mound was constructed on a plateau between the {{ill|Tagawa River (Tone River System)|ja|田川 (利根川水系)|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. It is the largest keyhole-shaped kofun in the Tsukayama Kofun Cluster, which includes several mounds such as the scallop-shaped Tsukayama West and South Kofun, as well as {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|qq=draft}}-based coffins. The rear circular section has been partially leveled by road construction. In 1989 (Heisei 1), a survey was conducted, followed by four excavation campaigns from 1989 to 1991. The mound has a "Kenbishi-style" keyhole type with a protruding front section oriented westward. It is constructed in three tiers, with external surfaces featuring {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Cylindrical {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (TK216-208 style), and {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery|qq=draft|qq=draft}} have been excavated. The southern neck of the mound features a {{ill|tsukuridashi|ja|造出|1=Platform-style projection|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and the shield-shaped moat surrounding the mound brings the total length to 119.2 meters. The burial facility remains unexamined, and grave goods are largely unknown. The mound is estimated to date from the mid-5th century, during the middle {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (or the late 5th century, according to other estimates). It served as a prominent burial site for regional leaders in the southern Utsunomiya area and is considered critical for studying the political dynamics of the {{ill|Shimotsukeno region|ja|下毛野地方|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. The site was designation1 as a Tochigi Prefecture historical site in 1953 (Shōwa 28). Today, the mound is adorned with {{ill|Dodantsutsuji shrubs|ja|ドウダンツツジ|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, offering a unique landscape that has been developed for preservation. == Ruins History == * [[1953]] (Showa 28), November 10: Tsukayama Kofun was designation1 as a historic site by Tochigi Prefecture. * [[1966]] (Showa 41): Construction planning for [[National Route 121]] (part of the [[Utsunomiya Ring Road]]) began. The plans were revised to include a tunnel near the kofun group to protect cultural properties. * [[1973]] (Showa 48), April 13: Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun were designation1 as historic sites by Tochigi Prefecture. * [[1976]] (Showa 51): Excavations of Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama East Kofun were conducted due to road construction (reported by the Tochigi Prefectural Board of Education in [[1979]]). * [[1989]]-[[1991]] (Heisei 1-3): Excavations of Tsukayama Kofun were carried out by the Archaeological Research Society of [[Utsunomiya University]] (findings published in [[1995]]). * [[1991]]-[[1992]] (Heisei 3-4): Excavations of the Tsukayama Kofun Group were conducted during road improvement work by the Utsunomiya City Board of Education (findings published in [[1996]]). * [[1995]]-[[1997]] (Heisei 7-9): Excavations of Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun were carried out for historic site conservation by the Utsunomiya City Board of Education, Utsunomiya University, and [[Utsunomiya Bunsei Junior College]] (findings published in [[2003]]). * [[2005]] (Heisei 17), November 7: burial goods excavated from Tsukayama South Kofun were designation1 as tangible cultural properties by Utsunomiya City. == Mound == The area of the mound are as follows{{Sfn|Tsukayama Kofun Group (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}: * Total Kofun Length: 119.2 meters - The overall length of the kofun, including the surrounding moat. * Mound Length: 98.3 meters * Rear Circular Section Diameter: 55.9 meters * Front Section Width: 59.9 meters File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), funkyu-4.jpg|Mound and surrounding moat. File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), zenpoubu.jpg|View from the rear circular section toward the front section. == Tsukayama Kofun Group == The '''Tsukayama Kofun Group''' consists of a cluster of kofun (ancient Kofuns) with Tsukayama Kofun as the main mound. Originally composed of over 10 kofun, it currently includes one [[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped kofun]] (Tsukayama Kofun), two [[Scallop-shaped kofun|scallop-shaped kofun]] (Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun), and one round kofun (No. 6 Kofun). Investigations have identified six small round kofun (Nos. 4, 5, 7, 8, and two within the old shooting range) to the north of Tsukayama Kofun. To the west and southwest, from north to south, lie a mid-sized round kofun (No. 6), Tsukayama West Kofun, and Tsukayama South Kofun. Haniwa sarcophagi have also been discovered in the area, with one featuring an engraved depiction of four deer in alternating male and female pairs. The construction period is estimated to span the mid-5th century to the early 6th century during the mid- to late-Kofun period, following the [[Mobara Kofun Group]] and the {{ill|Higashitani Kofun Group|ja|東谷古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Mound (rear circular section in the center, front section in the background) |alternate_name = |location = [[Tochigi Prefecture|Tochigi]], [[Utsunomiya]] Nishikawada Town Higashihara |type = [[Scallop-shaped kofun]] |area = Mound length: 63.1 m
Height: 6.7 m (rear section) |burial = Unknown |burial goods = [[Haniwa]], [[Sue pottery]] |built = [[5th century]] late |Historic Site = Prefectural Historic Site: "Tsukayama West Kofun" |notes = }} '''Tsukayama West Kofun''' (塚山西古墳) is a kofun located southwest of Tsukayama Kofun. It is [[Scallop-shaped kofun|scallop-shaped]] and designation1 as a historic site by Tochigi Prefecture. The mound has a short front section and a rear circular section, oriented to the south-southeast. The area are as follows{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}: * Total Kofun Length: 74.1 meters (including moat). * Mound Length: 63.1 meters. * Rear Circular Section ** Diameter: 44.5 meters ** Height: 6.7 meters * Front Section ** Length: ~18 meters ** Width: ~22 meters ** Height: ~1.5 meters The mound comprises two or more tiers (upper tiers heavily disturbed){{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. Cylindrical haniwa and Sue pottery (TK208-TK23 styles) were found on the mound's surface{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. A horseshoe-shaped moat surrounds the mound (shallow on the east side due to proximity to Tsukayama Kofun){{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. burial are unknown due to limited findings; no clay or stone structures have been detected{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. The construction period is estimated to be the late 5th century, following Tsukayama Kofun and preceding Tsukayama South Kofun{{Sfn|Tsukayama Kofun Group (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}. === Tsukayama South Kofun === {{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]] |name = Tsukayama South Kofun |image = [[File:Tsukayama Minami Kofun (Utsunomiya), funkyu-2.jpg|280px]]
Mound (rear circular section in the center, front section in the background) |alternate_name = |location = [[Tochigi Prefecture|Tochigi]], [[Utsunomiya]] Nishikawada Town Higashihara |type = [[Scallop-shaped kofun]] |area = Mound length: 58 m
Height: 6.8 m (rear section) |burial = Unknown |burial goods = [[Haniwa]], [[Sue pottery]], [[Haji pottery]] |built = [[5th century]] late |Historic Site = Prefectural Historic Site: "Tsukayama South Kofun" |notes = excavations designation1 as cultural properties of Utsunomiya City }} '''Tsukayama South Kofun''' (塚山南古墳) is a kofun located south of Tsukayama West Kofun. It is [[Scallop-shaped kofun|scallop-shaped]] and designation1 as a historic site by Tochigi Prefecture. The mound has a short front section and a rear circular section, oriented southward. The area are as follows{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}: * Total Kofun Length: 70.6 meters (including moat). * Mound Length: 58.0 meters. * Rear Circular Section ** Diameter: 42.1 meters ** Height: 6.8 meters * Front Section ** Length: 13.5 meters ** Height: 4.1 meters The mound is two-tiered{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. Numerous burial goods, including cylindrical haniwa, figurative haniwa (human, horse, deer, and house types), large Sue pottery vessels, and Haji pottery, were recovered, though no evidence of surface stones was found{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. A horseshoe-shaped moat surrounds the mound (narrower on the northwest side due to proximity to Tsukayama West Kofun){{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. burial have not been fully investigated, but depressions and red-painted stones suggest a vertical burial system at the mound's summit, likely plundered{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. The construction period is estimated to be the late 5th century to early 6th century, following Tsukayama West Kofun{{Sfn|Tsukayama Kofun Group (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}. == Historic Site == === Tochigi Prefectural Historic Site === * Historic Sites ** {{ill|Tsukayama Kofun|ja|塚山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - map | coord = {{Coord|36|30|20|N|139|51|38|E}} | zoom = 17 | float = right | width = 300| height =250 | caption = {{center|塚山古墳群分布図}} | scalemark = 60 | mark-coord1= {{Coord|36|30|22.05|N|139|51|39.50|E}} | label1=塚山古墳 | label-pos1=top | label-color1=black | mark1=前方後円墳-西南西.svg | mark-size1=70 | mark-coord2= {{Coord|36|30|20.25|N|139|51|36.35|E}} | label2=塚山西古墳 | label-pos2=top | label-color2=black | mark2=帆立貝形古墳-南南東.svg | mark-size2=60 | mark-coord3= {{Coord|36|30|17.93|N|139|51|37.23|E}} | label3=塚山南古墳 | label-pos3=left | label-color3=black | mark3=帆立貝形古墳-南.svg | mark-size3=60 }} '''塚山古墳'''（つかやまこふん）は、[[栃木県]][[宇都宮市]]西川田町にある[[古墳]]。形状は[[前方後円墳]]。塚山古墳群を構成する古墳の1つ。栃木県指定史跡に指定されている。 本項目では、塚山古墳を主墳とする'''[[#塚山古墳群|塚山古墳群]]'''についても解説する。 == 概要 == [[File:100425 Tsukayama Kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|{{center|塚山古墳群の空中写真（[[2010年]]）}}{{small|右上に塚山古墳、左に塚山西古墳、左下に塚山南古墳。{{国土航空写真}}。}}]] 栃木県南部、[[田川 (利根川水系)|田川]]・[[姿川]]の中間の台地上に築造された大型前方後円墳である。周辺には[[帆立貝形古墳]]の塚山西古墳・塚山南古墳含む古墳数基・埴輪棺が分布して塚山古墳群を形成し、本古墳はそのうち最大規模になる。現在までに後円部の一部が道路で削平を受けているほか、[[1989年]]（[[平成]]元年）に測量調査が、1989-[[1991年]]（平成元-3年）に4次の発掘調査が実施されている。 墳形は前方部前端が突出する「剣菱型」の前方後円形で、前方部を西方向に向ける。墳丘は3段築成。墳丘外表では[[葺石]]が認められるほか、[[円筒埴輪]]・[[須恵器]]（TK216-208型式）・[[土師器]]が検出されている。墳丘くびれ部南側には[[造出]]を付す。また墳丘周囲には盾形の周濠が巡らされ、周濠を含めた古墳全長は119.2メートルにもおよぶ{{Sfn|塚山古墳群（続古墳）|2002}}。埋葬施設は未調査のため明らかでなく、副葬品も詳らかでない。 築造時期は、[[古墳時代]]中期の[[5世紀]]中葉{{Sfn|塚山古墳群（続古墳）|2002}}（または5世紀後半）頃と推定される。宇都宮南部地域における大型首長墓であり、下毛野地方の政治情勢を考察するうえで重要視される古墳になる{{Sfn|塚山古墳群（続古墳）|2002}}。 古墳域は[[1953年]]（[[昭和]]28年）に栃木県指定史跡に指定された。現在では墳丘上に[[ドウダンツツジ]]が植えられ、独特の景観を呈する古墳として整備されている。 == 遺跡歴 == * [[1953年]]（[[昭和]]28年）11月10日、塚山古墳が栃木県指定史跡に指定。 * [[1966年]]（昭和41年）、[[国道121号]]（[[宇都宮環状道路]]）の建設計画立案。文化財保護のため古墳群付近のトンネル化に計画変更。 * [[1973年]]（昭和48年）4月13日、塚山西古墳・塚山南古墳が栃木県指定史跡に指定。 * [[1976年]]（昭和51年）、道路建設に伴う塚山西古墳・塚山東古墳の発掘調査（栃木県教育委員会、[[1979年]]に報告書刊行）。 * [[1989年|1989]]-[[1991年]]（[[平成]]元-3年）、塚山古墳の発掘調査（[[宇都宮大学]]考古学研究会、[[1995年]]に報告）。 * [[1991年|1991]]-[[1992年]]度（平成3-4年度）、道路改良に伴う塚山古墳群の発掘調査（宇都宮市教育委員会、[[1996年]]に報告書刊行）。 * [[1995年|1995]]-[[1997年]]度（平成7-9年度）、史跡整備に伴う塚山西古墳・塚山南古墳の発掘調査（宇都宮市教育委員会・宇都宮大学・[[宇都宮文星短期大学]]、[[2003年]]に報告書刊行）。 * [[2005年]]（平成17年）11月7日、塚山南古墳出土土器が宇都宮市指定有形文化財に指定。 == 墳丘 == 墳丘の規模は次の通り{{Sfn|塚山古墳群（続古墳）|2002}}。 * 古墳総長：119.2メートル - 周濠を含めた古墳全長。 * 墳丘長：98.3メートル * 後円部 直径：55.9メートル * 前方部 幅：59.9メートル File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), funkyu-4.jpg|墳丘・周濠 File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), funkyu-3.jpg|墳丘
{{small|左に後円部、右奥に前方部。}} File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), funcho.jpg|後円部墳頂 File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), kouenbu.jpg|前方部から後円部を望む File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), zenpoubu.jpg|後円部から前方部を望む == 塚山古墳群 == '''塚山古墳群'''は、塚山古墳を主墳とする古墳群。かつては古墳10基以上で構成され、[[前方後円墳]]1基（塚山古墳）・[[帆立貝形古墳]]2基（塚山西古墳・塚山東古墳）・円墳1基（6号墳）が現存する。 これまでの調査では、塚山古墳の北側に小円墳6基（4・5・7・8号墳、旧射撃場内古墳2基）、西-南西側に北から中円墳（6号墳）・塚山西古墳・塚山南古墳が確認されている。一帯では埴輪棺が検出されており、その1つには線刻画として雌雄交互の鹿4頭が描かれる。営造時期は古墳時代中期-後期の5世紀中葉-[[6世紀]]初頭頃と推定され、茂原古墳群・[[東谷古墳群]]に後続する時期に想定される。 古墳群の内容は次の通り。 {| class="wikitable" style="text-align:center;background:#ffffff;white-space:nowrap;font-size:85%" |+塚山古墳群の一覧塚山古墳群パンフレット。史跡説明板。 !古墳名 !形状 !規模 !出土品 !築造時期 !史跡指定 !備考 |- |'''1号墳
（塚山古墳）'''||[[前方後円墳]]||墳丘長98m||style="text-align:left"|円筒埴輪・須恵器||5世紀中葉||県指定||style="text-align:left"|測量：1989年
発掘：1989・1990・1991年 |- |'''2号墳
（塚山西古墳）'''||[[帆立貝形古墳]]||墳丘長63m||style="text-align:left"|円筒埴輪・須恵器||5世紀後葉||県指定||style="text-align:left"|測量：1976・1995年
発掘：1976・1990・1995・1996年 |- |'''3号墳
（塚山南古墳）'''||帆立貝形古墳||墳丘長58m||style="text-align:left"|円筒埴輪・須恵器・土師器||5世紀末葉||県指定||style="text-align:left"|測量：1976・1996年
発掘：1976・1996・1997・1998年
出土土器は宇都宮市指定有形文化財 |- |'''4号墳'''||[[円墳]]||直径8m||style="text-align:left"|土器|| ||（消滅）|| |- |'''5号墳'''||円墳||直径7m||style="text-align:left"|木棺跡・円筒埴輪・土器・玉類|| ||（消滅）|| |- |'''6号墳'''||円墳||直径20m||style="text-align:left"|円筒埴輪・土器|| ||なし|| |- |'''7号墳'''||円墳|| ||style="text-align:left"|形象埴輪（鳥）・土器|| ||（消滅）|| |- |'''8号墳'''||円墳|| ||style="text-align:left"|円筒埴輪・土器|| ||（消滅）|| |- |旧射撃場内古墳2基||円墳|| ||style="text-align:left"|円筒埴輪・形象埴輪（鳥・短甲）|| ||（消滅）|| |- |埴輪棺5基||埴輪棺|| ||style="text-align:left"|円筒埴輪|| ||（消滅）|| |} File:Tsukayama Kofun Group (Utsunomiya)-6, funkyu.jpg|6号墳 === 塚山西古墳 === {{日本の古墳 |名称 = 塚山西古墳 |画像 = [[File:Tsukayama Nishi Kofun (Utsunomiya), funkyu-2.jpg|280px]]
墳丘（中央に後円部、右奥に前方部） |別名 = |所属 = |所在地 = [[栃木県]][[宇都宮市]]西川田町東原 |位置 = |形状 = [[帆立貝形古墳]] |規模 = 墳丘長63.1m
高さ6.7m（後円部） |埋葬施設 = 不明 |出土品 = [[埴輪]]・[[須恵器]] |陪塚 = |築造時期 = [[5世紀]]後葉 |被葬者 = |陵墓 = |史跡 = 栃木県指定史跡「塚山西古墳」 |有形文化財 = |特記事項 = }} '''塚山西古墳'''（つかやまにしこふん）は、塚山古墳の南西にある古墳。形状は[[帆立貝形古墳]]。栃木県指定史跡に指定されている。 墳形は、前方部が短小な帆立貝形の前方後円形で、前方部を南南東方向に向ける。墳丘の規模は次の通り{{Sfn|塚山西古墳・塚山南古墳|2003}}。 * 古墳総長：74.1メートル - 周濠を含めた古墳全長。 * 墳丘長：63.1メートル * 後円部 ** 直径：44.5メートル ** 高さ：6.7メートル * 前方部 ** 長さ：約18メートル ** 幅：約22メートル ** 高さ：約1.5メートル 墳丘は2段以上の築成（2段目以上は撹乱が著しく不明）{{Sfn|塚山西古墳・塚山南古墳|2003}}。墳丘外表では円筒埴輪・須恵器（TK208-TK23型式）が検出されている{{Sfn|塚山西古墳・塚山南古墳|2003}}。また墳丘周囲には馬蹄形の周濠が巡らされる（東側は塚山古墳の制約のため浅い）{{Sfn|塚山西古墳・塚山南古墳|2003}}。埋葬施設は後円部墳頂に存在するが、一部の検出に留まるため詳らかでない（粘土・石材の検出はなし）{{Sfn|塚山西古墳・塚山南古墳|2003}}。副葬品は詳らかでない。 築造時期は古墳時代中期の5世紀後葉頃と推定され、塚山古墳に後続し塚山南古墳に先行する時期に想定される{{Sfn|塚山古墳群（続古墳）|2002}}。 === 塚山南古墳 === {{日本の古墳 |名称 = 塚山南古墳 |画像 = [[File:Tsukayama Minami Kofun (Utsunomiya), funkyu-2.jpg|280px]]
墳丘（中央に後円部、右奥に前方部） |別名 = |所属 = |所在地 = [[栃木県]][[宇都宮市]]西川田町東原 |位置 = |形状 = [[帆立貝形古墳]] |規模 = 墳丘長58m
高さ6.8m（後円部） |埋葬施設 = 不明 |出土品 = [[埴輪]]・[[須恵器]]・[[土師器]] |陪塚 = |築造時期 = [[5世紀]]末葉 |被葬者 = |陵墓 = |史跡 = 栃木県指定史跡「塚山南古墳」 |有形文化財 = 出土土器（宇都宮市指定文化財） |特記事項 = }} '''塚山南古墳'''（つかやまみなみこふん）は、塚山西古墳の南にある古墳。形状は帆立貝形古墳。栃木県指定史跡に指定されている。 墳形は、前方部が短小な帆立貝形の前方後円形で、前方部を南方向に向ける。墳丘の規模は次の通り{{Sfn|塚山西古墳・塚山南古墳|2003}}。 * 古墳総長：70.6メートル - 周濠を含めた古墳全長。 * 墳丘長：58.0メートル * 後円部 ** 直径：42.1メートル ** 高さ：6.8メートル * 前方部 ** 長さ：13.5メートル ** 高さ：4.1メートル 墳丘は2段築成{{Sfn|塚山西古墳・塚山南古墳|2003}}。墳丘外表では円筒埴輪・形象埴輪（人物形・馬形・鹿形・家形埴輪）のほか、多数の須恵器（大甕・高坏形器台・装飾付脚付壺・二重𤭯：TK208-TK23型式）・[[土師器]]が検出されているが、葺石は認められていない{{Sfn|塚山西古墳・塚山南古墳|2003}}。また墳丘周囲には馬蹄形の周濠が巡らされる（後円部北西側は塚山西古墳の制約のため狭い）{{Sfn|塚山西古墳・塚山南古墳|2003}}。埋葬施設は未調査のため明らかでないが、墳頂に窪みや赤彩の石が存在することから、後円部墳頂における竪穴系施設であるが盗掘を受けていると推測される{{Sfn|塚山西古墳・塚山南古墳|2003}}。副葬品は詳らかでない。 築造時期は古墳時代後期の5世紀末葉{{Sfn|塚山古墳群（続古墳）|2002}}（5世紀末葉-6世紀初頭{{Sfn|塚山西古墳・塚山南古墳|2003}}）頃と推定され、塚山西古墳に後続する時期に想定される{{Sfn|塚山古墳群（続古墳）|2002}}。 == 文化財 == === 栃木県指定文化財 === * 史跡 ** 塚山古墳 - 1953年（昭和28年）11月10日指定[http://www.tochigi-edu.ed.jp/center/bunkazai/2341001.htm 塚山古墳]（栃木県教育委員会事務局文化財課「とちぎの文化財」）。[https://utsunomiya-8story.jp/search_post/%e5%a1%9a%e5%b1%b1%e5%8f%a4%e5%a2%b3/ 塚山古墳]（宇都宮市歴史文化資源活用推進協議会「宇都宮の歴史と文化財」）。。 ** 塚山西古墳 - 1973年（昭和48年）4月13日指定[http://www.tochigi-edu.ed.jp/center/bunkazai/2341039.htm 塚山西古墳]（栃木県教育委員会事務局文化財課「とちぎの文化財」）。[https://utsunomiya-8story.jp/search_post/%e5%a1%9a%e5%b1%b1%e8%a5%bf%e5%8f%a4%e5%a2%b3/ 塚山西古墳]（宇都宮市歴史文化資源活用推進協議会「宇都宮の歴史と文化財」）。。 ** 塚山南古墳 - 1973年（昭和48年）4月13日指定[http://www.tochigi-edu.ed.jp/center/bunkazai/2341040.htm 塚山南古墳]（栃木県教育委員会事務局文化財課「とちぎの文化財」）。[https://utsunomiya-8story.jp/search_post/%e5%a1%9a%e5%b1%b1%e5%8d%97%e5%8f%a4%e5%a2%b3/ 塚山南古墳]（宇都宮市歴史文化資源活用推進協議会「宇都宮の歴史と文化財」）。。 === 宇都宮市指定文化財 === * 有形文化財 ** 塚山南古墳出土土器（考古資料） - 2005年（平成17年）11月7日指定。 == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} == 参考文献 == {{small|（記事執筆に使用した文献）}} * 史跡説明板（塚山古墳群愛護会設置） * {{PDFlink|[https://utsunomiya-8story.jp/wordpress/wp-content/themes/utsunomiya/image/archive/contents10/tsukayama.pdf 塚山古墳群パンフレット]}}（宇都宮市教育委員会） - リンクは宇都宮市歴史文化資源活用推進協議会「宇都宮の歴史と文化財」。 * 地方自治体発行 ** {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=1979|chapter=|title=[https://sitereports.nabunken.go.jp/90128 塚山古墳群（栃木県埋蔵文化財調査報告書 第32集）]|publisher=栃木県教育委員会|isbn=|ref={{Harvid|塚山古墳群|1979}}}} - リンクは奈良文化財研究所「全国遺跡報告総覧」。 ** {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=1996|chapter=|title=[https://sitereports.nabunken.go.jp/71406 塚山古墳群 -道路改良工事に伴う発掘調査-（宇都宮市埋蔵文化財調査報告書 第40集）]|publisher=宇都宮市教育委員会|isbn=|ref={{Harvid|塚山古墳群|1996}}}} - リンクは奈良文化財研究所「全国遺跡報告総覧」。 ** {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=2003|chapter=|title=[https://sitereports.nabunken.go.jp/71393 塚山西古墳・塚山南古墳（宇都宮市埋蔵文化財調査報告書 第48集）]|publisher=宇都宮市教育委員会|isbn=|ref={{Harvid|塚山西古墳・塚山南古墳|2003}}}} - リンクは奈良文化財研究所「全国遺跡報告総覧」。 * 事典類 ** {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=1988|chapter=塚山古墳群|title=[[日本歴史地名大系]] 9 栃木県の地名|publisher=[[平凡社]]|isbn=4582490093|ref={{Harvid|塚山古墳群（平凡社）|1988}}}} ** {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=竹澤謙|year=1989|chapter=塚山古墳群|title=[[日本古墳大辞典]]|publisher=[[東京堂出版]]|isbn=4490102607|ref={{Harvid|塚山古墳群（古墳）|1989}}}} ** {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=橋本澄朗|year=2002|chapter=塚山古墳群|title=[[日本古墳大辞典|続 日本古墳大辞典]]|publisher=[[東京堂出版]]|isbn=4490105991|ref={{Harvid|塚山古墳群（続古墳）|2002}}}} * その他 ** {{Cite book|和書|author=塙静夫|authorlink=塙静夫|title=探訪とちぎの古墳|publisher=[[随想舎]]|year=2000|date=2000-02|isbn=4887480342|ref=harv}} == 関連文献 == {{small|（記事執筆に使用していない関連文献）}} * {{Cite journal|和書|author=石部正志ら|title=塚山古墳外形確認調査報告|date=1995|publisher=宇都宮大学考古学研究会|journal=峰考古|volume=|number=9|pages=|url=|naid=|doi=|ref=}} == 関連項目 == * [[笹塚古墳]] * [[栃木県総合運動公園]] == 外部リンク == {{Commonscat|Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya)}} {{Commonscat|Tsukayama Kofun Group (Utsunomiya)|塚山古墳群}} * [http://www.tochigi-edu.ed.jp/center/bunkazai/2341001.htm 塚山古墳]、[http://www.tochigi-edu.ed.jp/center/bunkazai/2341039.htm 塚山西古墳]、[http://www.tochigi-edu.ed.jp/center/bunkazai/2341040.htm 塚山南古墳] - mark3=帆立貝形古墳-南.svg | mark-size3=60 }} '''塚山古墳'''（つかやまこふん）は、[[栃木県]][[宇都宮市]]西川田町にある[[古墳]]。形状は[[前方後円墳]]。塚山古墳群を構成する古墳の1つ。栃木県指定史跡に指定されている。 本項目では、塚山古墳を主墳とする'''[[#塚山古墳群|塚山古墳群]]'''についても解説する。 == 概要 == [[File:100425 Tsukayama Kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|{{center|塚山古墳群の空中写真（[[2010年]]）}}{{small|右上に塚山古墳、左に塚山西古墳、左下に塚山南古墳。{{国土航空写真}}。}}]] 栃木県南部、[[田川 (利根川水系)|田川]]・[[姿川]]の中間の台地上に築造された大型前方後円墳である。周辺には[[帆立貝形古墳]]の塚山西古墳・塚山南古墳含む古墳数基・埴輪棺が分布して塚山古墳群を形成し、本古墳はそのうち最大規模になる。現在までに後円部の一部が道路で削平を受けているほか、[[1989年]]（[[平成]]元年）に測量調査が、1989-[[1991年]]（平成元-3年）に4次の発掘調査が実施されている。 墳形は前方部前端が突出する「剣菱型」の前方後円形で、前方部を西方向に向ける。墳丘は3段築成。墳丘外表では[[葺石]]が認められるほか、[[円筒埴輪]]・[[須恵器]]（TK216-208型式）・[[土師器]]が検出されている。墳丘くびれ部南側には[[造出]]を付す。また墳丘周囲には盾形の周濠が巡らされ、周濠を含めた古墳全長は119.2メートルにもおよぶ{{Sfn|塚山古墳群（続古墳）|2002}}。埋葬施設は未調査のため明らかでなく、副葬品も詳らかでない。 築造時期は、[[古墳時代]]中期の[[5世紀]]中葉{{Sfn|塚山古墳群（続古墳）|2002}}（または5世紀後半）頃と推定される。宇都宮南部地域における大型首長墓であり、下毛野地方の政治情勢を考察するうえで重要視される古墳になる{{Sfn|塚山古墳群（続古墳）|2002}}。 古墳域は[[1953年]]（[[昭和]]28年）に栃木県指定史跡に指定された。現在では墳丘上に[[ドウダンツツジ]]が植えられ、独特の景観を呈する古墳として整備されている。 == 遺跡歴 == * [[1953年]]（[[昭和]]28年）11月10日、塚山古墳が栃木県指定史跡に指定。 * [[1966年]]（昭和41年）、[[国道121号]]（[[宇都宮環状道路]]）の建設計画立案。文化財保護のため古墳群付近のトンネル化に計画変更。 * [[1973年]]（昭和48年）4月13日、塚山西古墳・塚山南古墳が栃木県指定史跡に指定。 * [[1976年]]（昭和51年）、道路建設に伴う塚山西古墳・塚山東古墳の発掘調査（栃木県教育委員会、[[1979年]]に報告書刊行）。 * [[1989年|1989]]-[[1991年]]（[[平成]]元-3年）、塚山古墳の発掘調査（[[宇都宮大学]]考古学研究会、[[1995年]]に報告）。 * [[1991年|1991]]-[[1992年]]度（平成3-4年度）、道路改良に伴う塚山古墳群の発掘調査（宇都宮市教育委員会、[[1996年]]に報告書刊行）。 * [[1995年|1995]]-[[1997年]]度（平成7-9年度）、史跡整備に伴う塚山西古墳・塚山南古墳の発掘調査（宇都宮市教育委員会・宇都宮大学・[[宇都宮文星短期大学]]、[[2003年]]に報告書刊行）。 * [[2005年]]（平成17年）11月7日、塚山南古墳出土土器が宇都宮市指定有形文化財に指定。 == 墳丘 == 墳丘の規模は次の通り{{Sfn|塚山古墳群（続古墳）|2002}}。 * 古墳総長：119.2メートル - 周濠を含めた古墳全長。 * 墳丘長：98.3メートル * 後円部 直径：55.9メートル * 前方部 幅：59.9メートル File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), funkyu-4.jpg|墳丘・周濠 File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), funkyu-3.jpg|墳丘
{{small|左に後円部、右奥に前方部。}} File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), funcho.jpg|後円部墳頂 File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), kouenbu.jpg|前方部から後円部を望む File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), zenpoubu.jpg|後円部から前方部を望む == 塚山古墳群 == '''塚山古墳群'''は、塚山古墳を主墳とする古墳群。かつては古墳10基以上で構成され、[[前方後円墳]]1基（塚山古墳）・[[帆立貝形古墳]]2基（塚山西古墳・塚山東古墳）・円墳1基（6号墳）が現存する。 これまでの調査では、塚山古墳の北側に小円墳6基（4・5・7・8号墳、旧射撃場内古墳2基）、西-南西側に北から中円墳（6号墳）・塚山西古墳・塚山南古墳が確認されている。一帯では埴輪棺が検出されており、その1つには線刻画として雌雄交互の鹿4頭が描かれる。営造時期は古墳時代中期-後期の5世紀中葉-[[6世紀]]初頭頃と推定され、茂原古墳群・[[東谷古墳群]]に後続する時期に想定される。 古墳群の内容は次の通り。 {| class="wikitable" style="text-align:center;background:#ffffff;white-space:nowrap;font-size:85%" |+塚山古墳群の一覧塚山古墳群パンフレット。史跡説明板。 !古墳名 !形状 !規模 !出土品 !築造時期 !史跡指定 !備考 |- |'''1号墳

墳丘（中央に後円部、右奥に前方部） |別名 = |所属 = |所在地 = [[栃木県]][[宇都宮市]]西川田町東原 |位置 = |形状 = [[帆立貝形古墳]] |規模 = 墳丘長63.1m
高さ6.7m（後円部） |埋葬施設 = 不明 |出土品 = [[埴輪]]・[[須恵器]] |陪塚 = |築造時期 = [[5世紀]]後葉 |被葬者 = |陵墓 = |史跡 = 栃木県指定史跡「塚山西古墳」 |有形文化財 = |特記事項 = }} '''塚山西古墳'''（つかやまにしこふん）は、塚山古墳の南西にある古墳。形状は[[帆立貝形古墳]]。栃木県指定史跡に指定されている。 墳形は、前方部が短小な帆立貝形の前方後円形で、前方部を南南東方向に向ける。墳丘の規模は次の通り{{Sfn|塚山西古墳・塚山南古墳|2003}}。 * 古墳総長：74.1メートル - 周濠を含めた古墳全長。 * 墳丘長：63.1メートル * 後円部 ** 直径：44.5メートル ** 高さ：6.7メートル * 前方部 ** 長さ：約18メートル ** 幅：約22メートル ** 高さ：約1.5メートル 墳丘は2段以上の築成（2段目以上は撹乱が著しく不明）{{Sfn|塚山西古墳・塚山南古墳|2003}}。墳丘外表では円筒埴輪・須恵器（TK208-TK23型式）が検出されている{{Sfn|塚山西古墳・塚山南古墳|2003}}。また墳丘周囲には馬蹄形の周濠が巡らされる（東側は塚山古墳の制約のため浅い）{{Sfn|塚山西古墳・塚山南古墳|2003}}。埋葬施設は後円部墳頂に存在するが、一部の検出に留まるため詳らかでない（粘土・石材の検出はなし）{{Sfn|塚山西古墳・塚山南古墳|2003}}。副葬品は詳らかでない。 築造時期は古墳時代中期の5世紀後葉頃と推定され、塚山古墳に後続し塚山南古墳に先行する時期に想定される{{Sfn|塚山古墳群（続古墳）|2002}}。 === 塚山南古墳 === {{日本の古墳 |名称 = 塚山南古墳 |画像 = [[File:Tsukayama Minami Kofun (Utsunomiya), funkyu-2.jpg|280px]]
墳丘（中央に後円部、右奥に前方部） |別名 = |所属 = |所在地 = [[栃木県]][[宇都宮市]]西川田町東原 |位置 = |形状 = [[帆立貝形古墳]] |規模 = 墳丘長58m
高さ6.8m（後円部） |埋葬施設 = 不明 |出土品 = [[埴輪]]・[[須恵器]]・[[土師器]] |陪塚 = |築造時期 = [[5世紀]]末葉 |被葬者 = |陵墓 = |史跡 = 栃木県指定史跡「塚山南古墳」 |有形文化財 = 出土土器（宇都宮市指定文化財） |特記事項 = }} '''塚山南古墳'''（つかやまみなみこふん）は、塚山西古墳の南にある古墳。形状は帆立貝形古墳。栃木県指定史跡に指定されている。 墳形は、前方部が短小な帆立貝形の前方後円形で、前方部を南方向に向ける。墳丘の規模は次の通り{{Sfn|塚山西古墳・塚山南古墳|2003}}。 * 古墳総長：70.6メートル - 周濠を含めた古墳全長。 * 墳丘長：58.0メートル * 後円部 ** 直径：42.1メートル ** 高さ：6.8メートル * 前方部 ** 長さ：13.5メートル ** 高さ：4.1メートル 墳丘は2段築成{{Sfn|塚山西古墳・塚山南古墳|2003}}。墳丘外表では円筒埴輪・形象埴輪（人物形・馬形・鹿形・家形埴輪）のほか、多数の須恵器（大甕・高坏形器台・装飾付脚付壺・二重𤭯：TK208-TK23型式）・[[土師器]]が検出されているが、葺石は認められていない{{Sfn|塚山西古墳・塚山南古墳|2003}}。また墳丘周囲には馬蹄形の周濠が巡らされる（後円部北西側は塚山西古墳の制約のため狭い）{{Sfn|塚山西古墳・塚山南古墳|2003}}。埋葬施設は未調査のため明らかでないが、墳頂に窪みや赤彩の石が存在することから、後円部墳頂における竪穴系施設であるが盗掘を受けていると推測される{{Sfn|塚山西古墳・塚山南古墳|2003}}。副葬品は詳らかでない。 築造時期は古墳時代後期の5世紀末葉{{Sfn|塚山古墳群（続古墳）|2002}}（5世紀末葉-6世紀初頭{{Sfn|塚山西古墳・塚山南古墳|2003}}）頃と推定され、塚山西古墳に後続する時期に想定される{{Sfn|塚山古墳群（続古墳）|2002}}。 == 文化財 == === 栃木県指定文化財 === * 史跡 ** 塚山古墳 - {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located in Nishikawada-machi, {{ill|Utsunomiya City|ja|宇都宮市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Tochigi Prefecture. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and part of the {{ill|Tsukayama Kofun Cluster|ja|塚山古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. It has been designation1 as a Tochigi Prefecture-designation1 historical site. This article also covers the {{ill|Tsukayama Kofun Cluster|ja|塚山古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, for which Tsukayama Kofun serves as the main mound. == Overview == [[File:100425 Tsukayama Kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|{{center|Aerial view of the Tsukayama Kofun Cluster (2010)}}{{small|Top right: Tsukayama Kofun; Left: Tsukayama West Kofun; Bottom left: Tsukayama South Kofun. {{ill|Aerial photographs of Japan|ja|国土航空写真|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.}}]] Located in southern Tochigi Prefecture, the mound was constructed on a plateau between the {{ill|Tagawa River (Tone River System)|ja|田川 (利根川水系)|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. It is the largest keyhole-shaped kofun in the Tsukayama Kofun Cluster, which includes several mounds such as the scallop-shaped Tsukayama West and South Kofun, as well as {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|qq=draft}}-based coffins. The rear circular section has been partially leveled by road construction. In 1989 (Heisei 1), a survey was conducted, followed by four excavation campaigns from 1989 to 1991. The mound has a "Kenbishi-style" keyhole type with a protruding front section oriented westward. It is constructed in three tiers, with external surfaces featuring {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Cylindrical {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (TK216-208 style), and {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery|qq=draft|qq=draft}} have been excavated. The southern neck of the mound features a {{ill|tsukuridashi|ja|造出|1=Platform-style projection|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and the shield-shaped moat surrounding the mound brings the total length to 119.2 meters. The burial facility remains unexamined, and grave goods are largely unknown. The mound is estimated to date from the mid-5th century, during the middle {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (or the late 5th century, according to other estimates). It served as a prominent burial site for regional leaders in the southern Utsunomiya area and is considered critical for studying the political dynamics of the {{ill|Shimotsukeno region|ja|下毛野地方|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. The site was designation1 as a Tochigi Prefecture historical site in 1953 (Shōwa 28). Today, the mound is adorned with {{ill|Dodantsutsuji shrubs|ja|ドウダンツツジ|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, offering a unique landscape that has been developed for preservation. == Ruins History == * [[1953]] (Showa 28), November 10: Tsukayama Kofun was designation1 as a historic site by Tochigi Prefecture. * [[1966]] (Showa 41): Construction planning for [[National Route 121]] (part of the [[Utsunomiya Ring Road]]) began. The plans were revised to include a tunnel near the kofun group to protect cultural properties. * [[1973]] (Showa 48), April 13: Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun were designation1 as historic sites by Tochigi Prefecture. * [[1976]] (Showa 51): Excavations of Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama East Kofun were conducted due to road construction (reported by the Tochigi Prefectural Board of Education in [[1979]]). * [[1989]]-[[1991]] (Heisei 1-3): Excavations of Tsukayama Kofun were carried out by the Archaeological Research Society of [[Utsunomiya University]] (findings published in [[1995]]). * [[1991]]-[[1992]] (Heisei 3-4): Excavations of the Tsukayama Kofun Group were conducted during road improvement work by the Utsunomiya City Board of Education (findings published in [[1996]]). * [[1995]]-[[1997]] (Heisei 7-9): Excavations of Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun were carried out for historic site conservation by the Utsunomiya City Board of Education, Utsunomiya University, and [[Utsunomiya Bunsei Junior College]] (findings published in [[2003]]). * [[2005]] (Heisei 17), November 7: burial goods excavated from Tsukayama South Kofun were designation1 as tangible cultural properties by Utsunomiya City. == Mound == The area of the mound are as follows{{Sfn|Tsukayama Kofun Group (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}: * Total Kofun Length: 119.2 meters - The overall length of the kofun, including the surrounding moat. * Mound Length: 98.3 meters * Rear Circular Section Diameter: 55.9 meters * Front Section Width: 59.9 meters File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), funkyu-4.jpg|Mound and surrounding moat. File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), zenpoubu.jpg|View from the rear circular section toward the front section. == Tsukayama Kofun Group == The '''Tsukayama Kofun Group''' consists of a cluster of kofun (ancient Kofuns) with Tsukayama Kofun as the main mound. Originally composed of over 10 kofun, it currently includes one [[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped kofun]] (Tsukayama Kofun), two [[Scallop-shaped kofun|scallop-shaped kofun]] (Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun), and one round kofun (No. 6 Kofun). Investigations have identified six small round kofun (Nos. 4, 5, 7, 8, and two within the old shooting range) to the north of Tsukayama Kofun. To the west and southwest, from north to south, lie a mid-sized round kofun (No. 6), Tsukayama West Kofun, and Tsukayama South Kofun. Haniwa sarcophagi have also been discovered in the area, with one featuring an engraved depiction of four deer in alternating male and female pairs. The construction period is estimated to span the mid-5th century to the early 6th century during the mid- to late-Kofun period, following the [[Mobara Kofun Group]] and the {{ill|Higashitani Kofun Group|ja|東谷古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Mound (rear circular section in the center, front section in the background) |alternate_name = |location = [[Tochigi Prefecture|Tochigi]], [[Utsunomiya]] Nishikawada Town Higashihara |type = [[Scallop-shaped kofun]] |area = Mound length: 63.1 m
Height: 6.7 m (rear section) |burial = Unknown |burial goods = [[Haniwa]], [[Sue pottery]] |built = [[5th century]] late |Historic Site = Prefectural Historic Site: "Tsukayama West Kofun" |notes = }} '''Tsukayama West Kofun''' (塚山西古墳) is a kofun located southwest of Tsukayama Kofun. It is [[Scallop-shaped kofun|scallop-shaped]] and designation1 as a historic site by Tochigi Prefecture. The mound has a short front section and a rear circular section, oriented to the south-southeast. The area are as follows{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}: * Total Kofun Length: 74.1 meters (including moat). * Mound Length: 63.1 meters. * Rear Circular Section ** Diameter: 44.5 meters ** Height: 6.7 meters * Front Section ** Length: ~18 meters ** Width: ~22 meters ** Height: ~1.5 meters The mound comprises two or more tiers (upper tiers heavily disturbed){{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. Cylindrical haniwa and Sue pottery (TK208-TK23 styles) were found on the mound's surface{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. A horseshoe-shaped moat surrounds the mound (shallow on the east side due to proximity to Tsukayama Kofun){{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. burial are unknown due to limited findings; no clay or stone structures have been detected{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. The construction period is estimated to be the late 5th century, following Tsukayama Kofun and preceding Tsukayama South Kofun{{Sfn|Tsukayama Kofun Group (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}. === Tsukayama South Kofun === {{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]] |name = Tsukayama South Kofun |image = [[File:Tsukayama Minami Kofun (Utsunomiya), funkyu-2.jpg|280px]]

Height: 6.8 m (rear section) |burial = Unknown |burial goods = [[Haniwa]], [[Sue pottery]], [[Haji pottery]] |built = [[5th century]] late |Historic Site = Prefectural Historic Site: "Tsukayama South Kofun" |notes = excavations designation1 as cultural properties of Utsunomiya City }} '''Tsukayama South Kofun''' (塚山南古墳) is a kofun located south of Tsukayama West Kofun. It is [[Scallop-shaped kofun|scallop-shaped]] and designation1 as a historic site by Tochigi Prefecture. The mound has a short front section and a rear circular section, oriented southward. The area are as follows{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}: * Total Kofun Length: 70.6 meters (including moat). * Mound Length: 58.0 meters. * Rear Circular Section ** Diameter: 42.1 meters ** Height: 6.8 meters * Front Section ** Length: 13.5 meters ** Height: 4.1 meters The mound is two-tiered{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. Numerous burial goods, including cylindrical haniwa, figurative haniwa (human, horse, deer, and house types), large Sue pottery vessels, and Haji pottery, were recovered, though no evidence of surface stones was found{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. A horseshoe-shaped moat surrounds the mound (narrower on the northwest side due to proximity to Tsukayama West Kofun){{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. burial have not been fully investigated, but depressions and red-painted stones suggest a vertical burial system at the mound's summit, likely plundered{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. The construction period is estimated to be the late 5th century to early 6th century, following Tsukayama West Kofun{{Sfn|Tsukayama Kofun Group (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}. == Historic Site == === Tochigi Prefectural Historic Site === * Historic Sites ** {{ill|Tsukayama Kofun|ja|塚山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located in Nishikawada-machi, {{ill|Utsunomiya City|ja|宇都宮市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Tochigi Prefecture. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and part of the {{ill|Tsukayama Kofun Cluster|ja|塚山古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. It has been designation1 as a Tochigi Prefecture-designation1 historical site. This article also covers the {{ill|Tsukayama Kofun Cluster|ja|塚山古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, for which Tsukayama Kofun serves as the main mound. == Overview == [[File:100425 Tsukayama Kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|{{center|Aerial view of the Tsukayama Kofun Cluster (2010)}}{{small|Top right: Tsukayama Kofun; Left: Tsukayama West Kofun; Bottom left: Tsukayama South Kofun. {{ill|Aerial photographs of Japan|ja|国土航空写真|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.}}]] Located in southern Tochigi Prefecture, the mound was constructed on a plateau between the {{ill|Tagawa River (Tone River System)|ja|田川 (利根川水系)|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. It is the largest keyhole-shaped kofun in the Tsukayama Kofun Cluster, which includes several mounds such as the scallop-shaped Tsukayama West and South Kofun, as well as {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|qq=draft}}-based coffins. The rear circular section has been partially leveled by road construction. In 1989 (Heisei 1), a survey was conducted, followed by four excavation campaigns from 1989 to 1991. The mound has a "Kenbishi-style" keyhole type with a protruding front section oriented westward. It is constructed in three tiers, with external surfaces featuring {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Cylindrical {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (TK216-208 style), and {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery|qq=draft|qq=draft}} have been excavated. The southern neck of the mound features a {{ill|tsukuridashi|ja|造出|1=Platform-style projection|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and the shield-shaped moat surrounding the mound brings the total length to 119.2 meters. The burial facility remains unexamined, and grave goods are largely unknown. The mound is estimated to date from the mid-5th century, during the middle {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (or the late 5th century, according to other estimates). It served as a prominent burial site for regional leaders in the southern Utsunomiya area and is considered critical for studying the political dynamics of the {{ill|Shimotsukeno region|ja|下毛野地方|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. The site was designation1 as a Tochigi Prefecture historical site in 1953 (Shōwa 28). Today, the mound is adorned with {{ill|Dodantsutsuji shrubs|ja|ドウダンツツジ|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, offering a unique landscape that has been developed for preservation. == Ruins History == * [[1953]] (Showa 28), November 10: Tsukayama Kofun was designation1 as a historic site by Tochigi Prefecture. * [[1966]] (Showa 41): Construction planning for [[National Route 121]] (part of the [[Utsunomiya Ring Road]]) began. The plans were revised to include a tunnel near the kofun group to protect cultural properties. * [[1973]] (Showa 48), April 13: Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun were designation1 as historic sites by Tochigi Prefecture. * [[1976]] (Showa 51): Excavations of Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama East Kofun were conducted due to road construction (reported by the Tochigi Prefectural Board of Education in [[1979]]). * [[1989]]-[[1991]] (Heisei 1-3): Excavations of Tsukayama Kofun were carried out by the Archaeological Research Society of [[Utsunomiya University]] (findings published in [[1995]]). * [[1991]]-[[1992]] (Heisei 3-4): Excavations of the Tsukayama Kofun Group were conducted during road improvement work by the Utsunomiya City Board of Education (findings published in [[1996]]). * [[1995]]-[[1997]] (Heisei 7-9): Excavations of Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun were carried out for historic site conservation by the Utsunomiya City Board of Education, Utsunomiya University, and [[Utsunomiya Bunsei Junior College]] (findings published in [[2003]]). * [[2005]] (Heisei 17), November 7: burial goods excavated from Tsukayama South Kofun were designation1 as tangible cultural properties by Utsunomiya City. == Mound == The area of the mound are as follows{{Sfn|Tsukayama Kofun Group (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}: * Total Kofun Length: 119.2 meters - The overall length of the kofun, including the surrounding moat. * Mound Length: 98.3 meters * Rear Circular Section Diameter: 55.9 meters * Front Section Width: 59.9 meters File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), funkyu-4.jpg|Mound and surrounding moat. File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), zenpoubu.jpg|View from the rear circular section toward the front section. == Tsukayama Kofun Group == The '''Tsukayama Kofun Group''' consists of a cluster of kofun (ancient Kofuns) with Tsukayama Kofun as the main mound. Originally composed of over 10 kofun, it currently includes one [[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped kofun]] (Tsukayama Kofun), two [[Scallop-shaped kofun|scallop-shaped kofun]] (Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun), and one round kofun (No. 6 Kofun). Investigations have identified six small round kofun (Nos. 4, 5, 7, 8, and two within the old shooting range) to the north of Tsukayama Kofun. To the west and southwest, from north to south, lie a mid-sized round kofun (No. 6), Tsukayama West Kofun, and Tsukayama South Kofun. Haniwa sarcophagi have also been discovered in the area, with one featuring an engraved depiction of four deer in alternating male and female pairs. The construction period is estimated to span the mid-5th century to the early 6th century during the mid- to late-Kofun period, following the [[Mobara Kofun Group]] and the {{ill|Higashitani Kofun Group|ja|東谷古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Mound (rear circular section in the center, front section in the background) |alternate_name = |location = [[Tochigi Prefecture|Tochigi]], [[Utsunomiya]] Nishikawada Town Higashihara |type = [[Scallop-shaped kofun]] |area = Mound length: 63.1 m
Height: 6.7 m (rear section) |burial = Unknown |burial goods = [[Haniwa]], [[Sue pottery]] |built = [[5th century]] late |Historic Site = Prefectural Historic Site: "Tsukayama West Kofun" |notes = }} '''Tsukayama West Kofun''' (塚山西古墳) is a kofun located southwest of Tsukayama Kofun. It is [[Scallop-shaped kofun|scallop-shaped]] and designation1 as a historic site by Tochigi Prefecture. The mound has a short front section and a rear circular section, oriented to the south-southeast. The area are as follows{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}: * Total Kofun Length: 74.1 meters (including moat). * Mound Length: 63.1 meters. * Rear Circular Section ** Diameter: 44.5 meters ** Height: 6.7 meters * Front Section ** Length: ~18 meters ** Width: ~22 meters ** Height: ~1.5 meters The mound comprises two or more tiers (upper tiers heavily disturbed){{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. Cylindrical haniwa and Sue pottery (TK208-TK23 styles) were found on the mound's surface{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. A horseshoe-shaped moat surrounds the mound (shallow on the east side due to proximity to Tsukayama Kofun){{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. burial are unknown due to limited findings; no clay or stone structures have been detected{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. The construction period is estimated to be the late 5th century, following Tsukayama Kofun and preceding Tsukayama South Kofun{{Sfn|Tsukayama Kofun Group (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}. === Tsukayama South Kofun === {{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]] |name = Tsukayama South Kofun |image = [[File:Tsukayama Minami Kofun (Utsunomiya), funkyu-2.jpg|280px]]

Height: 6.8 m (rear section) |burial = Unknown |burial goods = [[Haniwa]], [[Sue pottery]], [[Haji pottery]] |built = [[5th century]] late |Historic Site = Prefectural Historic Site: "Tsukayama South Kofun" |notes = excavations designation1 as cultural properties of Utsunomiya City }} '''Tsukayama South Kofun''' (塚山南古墳) is a kofun located south of Tsukayama West Kofun. It is [[Scallop-shaped kofun|scallop-shaped]] and designation1 as a historic site by Tochigi Prefecture. The mound has a short front section and a rear circular section, oriented southward. The area are as follows{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}: * Total Kofun Length: 70.6 meters (including moat). * Mound Length: 58.0 meters. * Rear Circular Section ** Diameter: 42.1 meters ** Height: 6.8 meters * Front Section ** Length: 13.5 meters ** Height: 4.1 meters The mound is two-tiered{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. Numerous burial goods, including cylindrical haniwa, figurative haniwa (human, horse, deer, and house types), large Sue pottery vessels, and Haji pottery, were recovered, though no evidence of surface stones was found{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. A horseshoe-shaped moat surrounds the mound (narrower on the northwest side due to proximity to Tsukayama West Kofun){{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. burial have not been fully investigated, but depressions and red-painted stones suggest a vertical burial system at the mound's summit, likely plundered{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. The construction period is estimated to be the late 5th century to early 6th century, following Tsukayama West Kofun{{Sfn|Tsukayama Kofun Group (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}. == Historic Site == === Tochigi Prefectural Historic Site === * Historic Sites ** {{ill|Tsukayama Kofun|ja|塚山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located in Nishikawada-machi, {{ill|Utsunomiya City|ja|宇都宮市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Tochigi Prefecture. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and part of the {{ill|Tsukayama Kofun Cluster|ja|塚山古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. It has been designation1 as a Tochigi Prefecture-designation1 historical site. This article also covers the {{ill|Tsukayama Kofun Cluster|ja|塚山古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, for which Tsukayama Kofun serves as the main mound. == Overview == [[File:100425 Tsukayama Kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|{{center|Aerial view of the Tsukayama Kofun Cluster (2010)}}{{small|Top right: Tsukayama Kofun; Left: Tsukayama West Kofun; Bottom left: Tsukayama South Kofun. {{ill|Aerial photographs of Japan|ja|国土航空写真|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.}}]] Located in southern Tochigi Prefecture, the mound was constructed on a plateau between the {{ill|Tagawa River (Tone River System)|ja|田川 (利根川水系)|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. It is the largest keyhole-shaped kofun in the Tsukayama Kofun Cluster, which includes several mounds such as the scallop-shaped Tsukayama West and South Kofun, as well as {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|qq=draft}}-based coffins. The rear circular section has been partially leveled by road construction. In 1989 (Heisei 1), a survey was conducted, followed by four excavation campaigns from 1989 to 1991. The mound has a "Kenbishi-style" keyhole type with a protruding front section oriented westward. It is constructed in three tiers, with external surfaces featuring {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Cylindrical {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (TK216-208 style), and {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery|qq=draft|qq=draft}} have been excavated. The southern neck of the mound features a {{ill|tsukuridashi|ja|造出|1=Platform-style projection|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and the shield-shaped moat surrounding the mound brings the total length to 119.2 meters. The burial facility remains unexamined, and grave goods are largely unknown. The mound is estimated to date from the mid-5th century, during the middle {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (or the late 5th century, according to other estimates). It served as a prominent burial site for regional leaders in the southern Utsunomiya area and is considered critical for studying the political dynamics of the {{ill|Shimotsukeno region|ja|下毛野地方|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. The site was designation1 as a Tochigi Prefecture historical site in 1953 (Shōwa 28). Today, the mound is adorned with {{ill|Dodantsutsuji shrubs|ja|ドウダンツツジ|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, offering a unique landscape that has been developed for preservation. == Ruins History == * [[1953]] (Showa 28), November 10: Tsukayama Kofun was designation1 as a historic site by Tochigi Prefecture. * [[1966]] (Showa 41): Construction planning for [[National Route 121]] (part of the [[Utsunomiya Ring Road]]) began. The plans were revised to include a tunnel near the kofun group to protect cultural properties. * [[1973]] (Showa 48), April 13: Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun were designation1 as historic sites by Tochigi Prefecture. * [[1976]] (Showa 51): Excavations of Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama East Kofun were conducted due to road construction (reported by the Tochigi Prefectural Board of Education in [[1979]]). * [[1989]]-[[1991]] (Heisei 1-3): Excavations of Tsukayama Kofun were carried out by the Archaeological Research Society of [[Utsunomiya University]] (findings published in [[1995]]). * [[1991]]-[[1992]] (Heisei 3-4): Excavations of the Tsukayama Kofun Group were conducted during road improvement work by the Utsunomiya City Board of Education (findings published in [[1996]]). * [[1995]]-[[1997]] (Heisei 7-9): Excavations of Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun were carried out for historic site conservation by the Utsunomiya City Board of Education, Utsunomiya University, and [[Utsunomiya Bunsei Junior College]] (findings published in [[2003]]). * [[2005]] (Heisei 17), November 7: burial goods excavated from Tsukayama South Kofun were designation1 as tangible cultural properties by Utsunomiya City. == Mound == The area of the mound are as follows{{Sfn|Tsukayama Kofun Group (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}: * Total Kofun Length: 119.2 meters - The overall length of the kofun, including the surrounding moat. * Mound Length: 98.3 meters * Rear Circular Section Diameter: 55.9 meters * Front Section Width: 59.9 meters File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), funkyu-4.jpg|Mound and surrounding moat. File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), zenpoubu.jpg|View from the rear circular section toward the front section. == Tsukayama Kofun Group == The '''Tsukayama Kofun Group''' consists of a cluster of kofun (ancient Kofuns) with Tsukayama Kofun as the main mound. Originally composed of over 10 kofun, it currently includes one [[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped kofun]] (Tsukayama Kofun), two [[Scallop-shaped kofun|scallop-shaped kofun]] (Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun), and one round kofun (No. 6 Kofun). Investigations have identified six small round kofun (Nos. 4, 5, 7, 8, and two within the old shooting range) to the north of Tsukayama Kofun. To the west and southwest, from north to south, lie a mid-sized round kofun (No. 6), Tsukayama West Kofun, and Tsukayama South Kofun. Haniwa sarcophagi have also been discovered in the area, with one featuring an engraved depiction of four deer in alternating male and female pairs. The construction period is estimated to span the mid-5th century to the early 6th century during the mid- to late-Kofun period, following the [[Mobara Kofun Group]] and the {{ill|Higashitani Kofun Group|ja|東谷古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Height: 6.7 m (rear section) |burial = Unknown |burial goods = [[Haniwa]], [[Sue pottery]] |built = [[5th century]] late |Historic Site = Prefectural Historic Site: "Tsukayama West Kofun" |notes = }} '''Tsukayama West Kofun''' (塚山西古墳) is a kofun located southwest of Tsukayama Kofun. It is [[Scallop-shaped kofun|scallop-shaped]] and designation1 as a historic site by Tochigi Prefecture. The mound has a short front section and a rear circular section, oriented to the south-southeast. The area are as follows{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}: * Total Kofun Length: 74.1 meters (including moat). * Mound Length: 63.1 meters. * Rear Circular Section ** Diameter: 44.5 meters ** Height: 6.7 meters * Front Section ** Length: ~18 meters ** Width: ~22 meters ** Height: ~1.5 meters The mound comprises two or more tiers (upper tiers heavily disturbed){{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. Cylindrical haniwa and Sue pottery (TK208-TK23 styles) were found on the mound's surface{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. A horseshoe-shaped moat surrounds the mound (shallow on the east side due to proximity to Tsukayama Kofun){{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. burial are unknown due to limited findings; no clay or stone structures have been detected{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. The construction period is estimated to be the late 5th century, following Tsukayama Kofun and preceding Tsukayama South Kofun{{Sfn|Tsukayama Kofun Group (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}. === Tsukayama South Kofun === {{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]] |name = Tsukayama South Kofun |image = [[File:Tsukayama Minami Kofun (Utsunomiya), funkyu-2.jpg|280px]]

It is [[Scallop-shaped kofun|scallop-shaped]] and designation1 as a historic site by Tochigi Prefecture. The mound has a short front section and a rear circular section, oriented southward. The area are as follows{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}: * Total Kofun Length: 70.6 meters (including moat). * Mound Length: 58.0 meters. * Rear Circular Section ** Diameter: 42.1 meters ** Height: 6.8 meters * Front Section ** Length: 13.5 meters ** Height: 4.1 meters The mound is two-tiered{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. Numerous burial goods, including cylindrical haniwa, figurative haniwa (human, horse, deer, and house types), large Sue pottery vessels, and Haji pottery, were recovered, though no evidence of surface stones was found{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. A horseshoe-shaped moat surrounds the mound (narrower on the northwest side due to proximity to Tsukayama West Kofun){{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. burial have not been fully investigated, but depressions and red-painted stones suggest a vertical burial system at the mound's summit, likely plundered{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. The construction period is estimated to be the late 5th century to early 6th century, following Tsukayama West Kofun{{Sfn|Tsukayama Kofun Group (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}. == Historic Site == === Tochigi Prefectural Historic Site === * Historic Sites ** {{ill|Tsukayama Kofun|ja|塚山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located in Nishikawada-machi, {{ill|Utsunomiya City|ja|宇都宮市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Tochigi Prefecture. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and part of the {{ill|Tsukayama Kofun Cluster|ja|塚山古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. It has been designation1 as a Tochigi Prefecture-designation1 historical site. This article also covers the {{ill|Tsukayama Kofun Cluster|ja|塚山古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, for which Tsukayama Kofun serves as the main mound. == Overview == [[File:100425 Tsukayama Kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|{{center|Aerial view of the Tsukayama Kofun Cluster (2010)}}{{small|Top right: Tsukayama Kofun; Left: Tsukayama West Kofun; Bottom left: Tsukayama South Kofun. {{ill|Aerial photographs of Japan|ja|国土航空写真|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.}}]] Located in southern Tochigi Prefecture, the mound was constructed on a plateau between the {{ill|Tagawa River (Tone River System)|ja|田川 (利根川水系)|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. It is the largest keyhole-shaped kofun in the Tsukayama Kofun Cluster, which includes several mounds such as the scallop-shaped Tsukayama West and South Kofun, as well as {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|qq=draft}}-based coffins. The rear circular section has been partially leveled by road construction. In 1989 (Heisei 1), a survey was conducted, followed by four excavation campaigns from 1989 to 1991. The mound has a "Kenbishi-style" keyhole type with a protruding front section oriented westward. It is constructed in three tiers, with external surfaces featuring {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Cylindrical {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (TK216-208 style), and {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery|qq=draft|qq=draft}} have been excavated. The southern neck of the mound features a {{ill|tsukuridashi|ja|造出|1=Platform-style projection|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and the shield-shaped moat surrounding the mound brings the total length to 119.2 meters. The burial facility remains unexamined, and grave goods are largely unknown. The mound is estimated to date from the mid-5th century, during the middle {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (or the late 5th century, according to other estimates). It served as a prominent burial site for regional leaders in the southern Utsunomiya area and is considered critical for studying the political dynamics of the {{ill|Shimotsukeno region|ja|下毛野地方|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. The site was designation1 as a Tochigi Prefecture historical site in 1953 (Shōwa 28). Today, the mound is adorned with {{ill|Dodantsutsuji shrubs|ja|ドウダンツツジ|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, offering a unique landscape that has been developed for preservation. == Ruins History == * [[1953]] (Showa 28), November 10: Tsukayama Kofun was designation1 as a historic site by Tochigi Prefecture. * [[1966]] (Showa 41): Construction planning for [[National Route 121]] (part of the [[Utsunomiya Ring Road]]) began. The plans were revised to include a tunnel near the kofun group to protect cultural properties. * [[1973]] (Showa 48), April 13: Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun were designation1 as historic sites by Tochigi Prefecture. * [[1976]] (Showa 51): Excavations of Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama East Kofun were conducted due to road construction (reported by the Tochigi Prefectural Board of Education in [[1979]]). * [[1989]]-[[1991]] (Heisei 1-3): Excavations of Tsukayama Kofun were carried out by the Archaeological Research Society of [[Utsunomiya University]] (findings published in [[1995]]). * [[1991]]-[[1992]] (Heisei 3-4): Excavations of the Tsukayama Kofun Group were conducted during road improvement work by the Utsunomiya City Board of Education (findings published in [[1996]]). * [[1995]]-[[1997]] (Heisei 7-9): Excavations of Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun were carried out for historic site conservation by the Utsunomiya City Board of Education, Utsunomiya University, and [[Utsunomiya Bunsei Junior College]] (findings published in [[2003]]). * [[2005]] (Heisei 17), November 7: burial goods excavated from Tsukayama South Kofun were designation1 as tangible cultural properties by Utsunomiya City. == Mound == The area of the mound are as follows{{Sfn|Tsukayama Kofun Group (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}: * Total Kofun Length: 119.2 meters - The overall length of the kofun, including the surrounding moat. * Mound Length: 98.3 meters * Rear Circular Section Diameter: 55.9 meters * Front Section Width: 59.9 meters File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), funkyu-4.jpg|Mound and surrounding moat. File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), zenpoubu.jpg|View from the rear circular section toward the front section. == Tsukayama Kofun Group == The '''Tsukayama Kofun Group''' consists of a cluster of kofun (ancient Kofuns) with Tsukayama Kofun as the main mound. Originally composed of over 10 kofun, it currently includes one [[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped kofun]] (Tsukayama Kofun), two [[Scallop-shaped kofun|scallop-shaped kofun]] (Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun), and one round kofun (No. 6 Kofun). Investigations have identified six small round kofun (Nos. 4, 5, 7, 8, and two within the old shooting range) to the north of Tsukayama Kofun. To the west and southwest, from north to south, lie a mid-sized round kofun (No. 6), Tsukayama West Kofun, and Tsukayama South Kofun. Haniwa sarcophagi have also been discovered in the area, with one featuring an engraved depiction of four deer in alternating male and female pairs. The construction period is estimated to span the mid-5th century to the early 6th century during the mid- to late-Kofun period, following the [[Mobara Kofun Group]] and the {{ill|Higashitani Kofun Group|ja|東谷古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Height: 6.7 m (rear section) |burial = Unknown |burial goods = [[Haniwa]], [[Sue pottery]] |built = [[5th century]] late |Historic Site = Prefectural Historic Site: "Tsukayama West Kofun" |notes = }} '''Tsukayama West Kofun''' (塚山西古墳) is a kofun located southwest of Tsukayama Kofun. It is [[Scallop-shaped kofun|scallop-shaped]] and designation1 as a historic site by Tochigi Prefecture. The mound has a short front section and a rear circular section, oriented to the south-southeast. The area are as follows{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}: * Total Kofun Length: 74.1 meters (including moat). * Mound Length: 63.1 meters. * Rear Circular Section ** Diameter: 44.5 meters ** Height: 6.7 meters * Front Section ** Length: ~18 meters ** Width: ~22 meters ** Height: ~1.5 meters The mound comprises two or more tiers (upper tiers heavily disturbed){{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. Cylindrical haniwa and Sue pottery (TK208-TK23 styles) were found on the mound's surface{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. A horseshoe-shaped moat surrounds the mound (shallow on the east side due to proximity to Tsukayama Kofun){{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. burial are unknown due to limited findings; no clay or stone structures have been detected{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. The construction period is estimated to be the late 5th century, following Tsukayama Kofun and preceding Tsukayama South Kofun{{Sfn|Tsukayama Kofun Group (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}. === Tsukayama South Kofun === {{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]] |name = Tsukayama South Kofun |image = [[File:Tsukayama Minami Kofun (Utsunomiya), funkyu-2.jpg|280px]]
Mound (rear circular section in the center, front section in the background) |alternate_name = |location = [[Tochigi Prefecture|Tochigi]], [[Utsunomiya]] Nishikawada Town Higashihara |type = [[Scallop-shaped kofun]] |area = Mound length: 58 m
Height: 6.8 m (rear section) |burial = Unknown |burial goods = [[Haniwa]], [[Sue pottery]], [[Haji pottery]] |built = [[5th century]] late |Historic Site = Prefectural Historic Site: "Tsukayama South Kofun" |notes = excavations designation1 as cultural properties of Utsunomiya City }} '''Tsukayama South Kofun''' (塚山南古墳) is a kofun located south of Tsukayama West Kofun. It is [[Scallop-shaped kofun|scallop-shaped]] and designation1 as a historic site by Tochigi Prefecture. The mound has a short front section and a rear circular section, oriented southward. The area are as follows{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}: * Total Kofun Length: 70.6 meters (including moat). * Mound Length: 58.0 meters. * Rear Circular Section ** Diameter: 42.1 meters ** Height: 6.8 meters * Front Section ** Length: 13.5 meters ** Height: 4.1 meters The mound is two-tiered{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. Numerous burial goods, including cylindrical haniwa, figurative haniwa (human, horse, deer, and house types), large Sue pottery vessels, and Haji pottery, were recovered, though no evidence of surface stones was found{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. A horseshoe-shaped moat surrounds the mound (narrower on the northwest side due to proximity to Tsukayama West Kofun){{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. burial have not been fully investigated, but depressions and red-painted stones suggest a vertical burial system at the mound's summit, likely plundered{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. The construction period is estimated to be the late 5th century to early 6th century, following Tsukayama West Kofun{{Sfn|Tsukayama Kofun Group (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}. == Historic Site == === Tochigi Prefectural Historic Site === * Historic Sites ** {{ill|Tsukayama Kofun|ja|塚山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located in Nishikawada-machi, {{ill|Utsunomiya City|ja|宇都宮市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Tochigi Prefecture. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and part of the {{ill|Tsukayama Kofun Cluster|ja|塚山古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. It has been designation1 as a Tochigi Prefecture-designation1 historical site. This article also covers the {{ill|Tsukayama Kofun Cluster|ja|塚山古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, for which Tsukayama Kofun serves as the main mound. == Overview == [[File:100425 Tsukayama Kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|{{center|Aerial view of the Tsukayama Kofun Cluster (2010)}}{{small|Top right: Tsukayama Kofun; Left: Tsukayama West Kofun; Bottom left: Tsukayama South Kofun. {{ill|Aerial photographs of Japan|ja|国土航空写真|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.}}]] Located in southern Tochigi Prefecture, the mound was constructed on a plateau between the {{ill|Tagawa River (Tone River System)|ja|田川 (利根川水系)|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. It is the largest keyhole-shaped kofun in the Tsukayama Kofun Cluster, which includes several mounds such as the scallop-shaped Tsukayama West and South Kofun, as well as {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|qq=draft}}-based coffins. The rear circular section has been partially leveled by road construction. In 1989 (Heisei 1), a survey was conducted, followed by four excavation campaigns from 1989 to 1991. The mound has a "Kenbishi-style" keyhole type with a protruding front section oriented westward. It is constructed in three tiers, with external surfaces featuring {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Cylindrical {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (TK216-208 style), and {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery|qq=draft|qq=draft}} have been excavated. The southern neck of the mound features a {{ill|tsukuridashi|ja|造出|1=Platform-style projection|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and the shield-shaped moat surrounding the mound brings the total length to 119.2 meters. The burial facility remains unexamined, and grave goods are largely unknown. The mound is estimated to date from the mid-5th century, during the middle {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (or the late 5th century, according to other estimates). It served as a prominent burial site for regional leaders in the southern Utsunomiya area and is considered critical for studying the political dynamics of the {{ill|Shimotsukeno region|ja|下毛野地方|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. The site was designation1 as a Tochigi Prefecture historical site in 1953 (Shōwa 28). Today, the mound is adorned with {{ill|Dodantsutsuji shrubs|ja|ドウダンツツジ|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, offering a unique landscape that has been developed for preservation. == Ruins History == * [[1953]] (Showa 28), November 10: Tsukayama Kofun was designation1 as a historic site by Tochigi Prefecture. * [[1966]] (Showa 41): Construction planning for [[National Route 121]] (part of the [[Utsunomiya Ring Road]]) began. The plans were revised to include a tunnel near the kofun group to protect cultural properties. * [[1973]] (Showa 48), April 13: Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun were designation1 as historic sites by Tochigi Prefecture. * [[1976]] (Showa 51): Excavations of Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama East Kofun were conducted due to road construction (reported by the Tochigi Prefectural Board of Education in [[1979]]). * [[1989]]-[[1991]] (Heisei 1-3): Excavations of Tsukayama Kofun were carried out by the Archaeological Research Society of [[Utsunomiya University]] (findings published in [[1995]]). * [[1991]]-[[1992]] (Heisei 3-4): Excavations of the Tsukayama Kofun Group were conducted during road improvement work by the Utsunomiya City Board of Education (findings published in [[1996]]). * [[1995]]-[[1997]] (Heisei 7-9): Excavations of Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun were carried out for historic site conservation by the Utsunomiya City Board of Education, Utsunomiya University, and [[Utsunomiya Bunsei Junior College]] (findings published in [[2003]]). * [[2005]] (Heisei 17), November 7: burial goods excavated from Tsukayama South Kofun were designation1 as tangible cultural properties by Utsunomiya City. == Mound == The area of the mound are as follows{{Sfn|Tsukayama Kofun Group (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}: * Total Kofun Length: 119.2 meters - The overall length of the kofun, including the surrounding moat. * Mound Length: 98.3 meters * Rear Circular Section Diameter: 55.9 meters * Front Section Width: 59.9 meters File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), funkyu-4.jpg|Mound and surrounding moat. File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), zenpoubu.jpg|View from the rear circular section toward the front section. == Tsukayama Kofun Group == The '''Tsukayama Kofun Group''' consists of a cluster of kofun (ancient Kofuns) with Tsukayama Kofun as the main mound. Originally composed of over 10 kofun, it currently includes one [[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped kofun]] (Tsukayama Kofun), two [[Scallop-shaped kofun|scallop-shaped kofun]] (Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun), and one round kofun (No. 6 Kofun). Investigations have identified six small round kofun (Nos. 4, 5, 7, 8, and two within the old shooting range) to the north of Tsukayama Kofun. To the west and southwest, from north to south, lie a mid-sized round kofun (No. 6), Tsukayama West Kofun, and Tsukayama South Kofun. Haniwa sarcophagi have also been discovered in the area, with one featuring an engraved depiction of four deer in alternating male and female pairs. The construction period is estimated to span the mid-5th century to the early 6th century during the mid- to late-Kofun period, following the [[Mobara Kofun Group]] and the {{ill|Higashitani Kofun Group|ja|東谷古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. It is [[Scallop-shaped kofun|scallop-shaped]] and designation1 as a historic site by Tochigi Prefecture. The mound has a short front section and a rear circular section, oriented to the south-southeast. The area are as follows{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}: * Total Kofun Length: 74.1 meters (including moat). * Mound Length: 63.1 meters. * Rear Circular Section ** Diameter: 44.5 meters ** Height: 6.7 meters * Front Section ** Length: ~18 meters ** Width: ~22 meters ** Height: ~1.5 meters The mound comprises two or more tiers (upper tiers heavily disturbed){{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. Cylindrical haniwa and Sue pottery (TK208-TK23 styles) were found on the mound's surface{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. A horseshoe-shaped moat surrounds the mound (shallow on the east side due to proximity to Tsukayama Kofun){{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. burial are unknown due to limited findings; no clay or stone structures have been detected{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. The construction period is estimated to be the late 5th century, following Tsukayama Kofun and preceding Tsukayama South Kofun{{Sfn|Tsukayama Kofun Group (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}. === Tsukayama South Kofun === {{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]] |name = Tsukayama South Kofun |image = [[File:Tsukayama Minami Kofun (Utsunomiya), funkyu-2.jpg|280px]]

Height: 6.8 m (rear section) |burial = Unknown |burial goods = [[Haniwa]], [[Sue pottery]], [[Haji pottery]] |built = [[5th century]] late |Historic Site = Prefectural Historic Site: "Tsukayama South Kofun" |notes = excavations designation1 as cultural properties of Utsunomiya City }} '''Tsukayama South Kofun''' (塚山南古墳) is a kofun located south of Tsukayama West Kofun. It is [[Scallop-shaped kofun|scallop-shaped]] and designation1 as a historic site by Tochigi Prefecture. The mound has a short front section and a rear circular section, oriented southward. The area are as follows{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}: * Total Kofun Length: 70.6 meters (including moat). * Mound Length: 58.0 meters. * Rear Circular Section ** Diameter: 42.1 meters ** Height: 6.8 meters * Front Section ** Length: 13.5 meters ** Height: 4.1 meters The mound is two-tiered{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. Numerous burial goods, including cylindrical haniwa, figurative haniwa (human, horse, deer, and house types), large Sue pottery vessels, and Haji pottery, were recovered, though no evidence of surface stones was found{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. A horseshoe-shaped moat surrounds the mound (narrower on the northwest side due to proximity to Tsukayama West Kofun){{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. burial have not been fully investigated, but depressions and red-painted stones suggest a vertical burial system at the mound's summit, likely plundered{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. The construction period is estimated to be the late 5th century to early 6th century, following Tsukayama West Kofun{{Sfn|Tsukayama Kofun Group (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}. == Historic Site == === Tochigi Prefectural Historic Site === * Historic Sites ** {{ill|Tsukayama Kofun|ja|塚山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} -
