{{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located in Nishikawada-machi, {{ill|Utsunomiya City|ja|宇都宮市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Tochigi Prefecture. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and part of the {{ill|Tsukayama Kofun Cluster|ja|塚山古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. It has been designation1 as a Tochigi Prefecture-designation1 historical site. This article also covers the {{ill|Tsukayama Kofun Cluster|ja|塚山古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, for which Tsukayama Kofun serves as the main mound. == Overview == [[File:100425 Tsukayama Kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|{{center|Aerial view of the Tsukayama Kofun Cluster (2010)}}{{small|Top right: Tsukayama Kofun; Left: Tsukayama West Kofun; Bottom left: Tsukayama South Kofun. {{ill|Aerial photographs of Japan|ja|国土航空写真|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.}}]] Located in southern Tochigi Prefecture, the mound was constructed on a plateau between the {{ill|Tagawa River (Tone River System)|ja|田川 (利根川水系)|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. It is the largest keyhole-shaped kofun in the Tsukayama Kofun Cluster, which includes several mounds such as the scallop-shaped Tsukayama West and South Kofun, as well as {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|qq=draft}}-based coffins. The rear circular section has been partially leveled by road construction. In 1989 (Heisei 1), a survey was conducted, followed by four excavation campaigns from 1989 to 1991. The mound has a "Kenbishi-style" keyhole type with a protruding front section oriented westward. It is constructed in three tiers, with external surfaces featuring {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Cylindrical {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (TK216-208 style), and {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery|qq=draft|qq=draft}} have been excavated. The southern neck of the mound features a {{ill|tsukuridashi|ja|造出|1=Platform-style projection|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and the shield-shaped moat surrounding the mound brings the total length to 119.2 meters. The burial facility remains unexamined, and grave goods are largely unknown. The mound is estimated to date from the mid-5th century, during the middle {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (or the late 5th century, according to other estimates). It served as a prominent burial site for regional leaders in the southern Utsunomiya area and is considered critical for studying the political dynamics of the {{ill|Shimotsukeno region|ja|下毛野地方|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. The site was designation1 as a Tochigi Prefecture historical site in 1953 (Shōwa 28). Today, the mound is adorned with {{ill|Dodantsutsuji shrubs|ja|ドウダンツツジ|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, offering a unique landscape that has been developed for preservation. == Ruins History == * [[1953]] (Showa 28), November 10: Tsukayama Kofun was designation1 as a historic site by Tochigi Prefecture. * [[1966]] (Showa 41): Construction planning for [[National Route 121]] (part of the [[Utsunomiya Ring Road]]) began. The plans were revised to include a tunnel near the kofun group to protect cultural properties. * [[1973]] (Showa 48), April 13: Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun were designation1 as historic sites by Tochigi Prefecture. * [[1976]] (Showa 51): Excavations of Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama East Kofun were conducted due to road construction (reported by the Tochigi Prefectural Board of Education in [[1979]]). * [[1989]]-[[1991]] (Heisei 1-3): Excavations of Tsukayama Kofun were carried out by the Archaeological Research Society of [[Utsunomiya University]] (findings published in [[1995]]). * [[1991]]-[[1992]] (Heisei 3-4): Excavations of the Tsukayama Kofun Group were conducted during road improvement work by the Utsunomiya City Board of Education (findings published in [[1996]]). * [[1995]]-[[1997]] (Heisei 7-9): Excavations of Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun were carried out for historic site conservation by the Utsunomiya City Board of Education, Utsunomiya University, and [[Utsunomiya Bunsei Junior College]] (findings published in [[2003]]). * [[2005]] (Heisei 17), November 7: burial goods excavated from Tsukayama South Kofun were designation1 as tangible cultural properties by Utsunomiya City. == Mound == The area of the mound are as follows{{Sfn|Tsukayama Kofun Group (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}: * Total Kofun Length: 119.2 meters - The overall length of the kofun, including the surrounding moat. * Mound Length: 98.3 meters * Rear Circular Section Diameter: 55.9 meters * Front Section Width: 59.9 meters File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), funkyu-4.jpg|Mound and surrounding moat. File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), zenpoubu.jpg|View from the rear circular section toward the front section. == Tsukayama Kofun Group == The '''Tsukayama Kofun Group''' consists of a cluster of kofun (ancient Kofuns) with Tsukayama Kofun as the main mound. Originally composed of over 10 kofun, it currently includes one [[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped kofun]] (Tsukayama Kofun), two [[Scallop-shaped kofun|scallop-shaped kofun]] (Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun), and one round kofun (No. 6 Kofun). Investigations have identified six small round kofun (Nos. 4, 5, 7, 8, and two within the old shooting range) to the north of Tsukayama Kofun. To the west and southwest, from north to south, lie a mid-sized round kofun (No. 6), Tsukayama West Kofun, and Tsukayama South Kofun. Haniwa sarcophagi have also been discovered in the area, with one featuring an engraved depiction of four deer in alternating male and female pairs. The construction period is estimated to span the mid-5th century to the early 6th century during the mid- to late-Kofun period, following the [[Mobara Kofun Group]] and the {{ill|Higashitani Kofun Group|ja|東谷古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Mound (rear circular section in the center, front section in the background) |alternate_name = |location = [[Tochigi Prefecture|Tochigi]], [[Utsunomiya]] Nishikawada Town Higashihara |type = [[Scallop-shaped kofun]] |area = Mound length: 63.1 m
Height: 6.7 m (rear section) |burial = Unknown |burial goods = [[Haniwa]], [[Sue pottery]] |built = [[5th century]] late |Historic Site = Prefectural Historic Site: "Tsukayama West Kofun" |notes = }} '''Tsukayama West Kofun''' (塚山西古墳) is a kofun located southwest of Tsukayama Kofun. It is [[Scallop-shaped kofun|scallop-shaped]] and designation1 as a historic site by Tochigi Prefecture. The mound has a short front section and a rear circular section, oriented to the south-southeast. The area are as follows{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}: * Total Kofun Length: 74.1 meters (including moat). * Mound Length: 63.1 meters. * Rear Circular Section ** Diameter: 44.5 meters ** Height: 6.7 meters * Front Section ** Length: ~18 meters ** Width: ~22 meters ** Height: ~1.5 meters The mound comprises two or more tiers (upper tiers heavily disturbed){{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. Cylindrical haniwa and Sue pottery (TK208-TK23 styles) were found on the mound's surface{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. A horseshoe-shaped moat surrounds the mound (shallow on the east side due to proximity to Tsukayama Kofun){{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. burial are unknown due to limited findings; no clay or stone structures have been detected{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. The construction period is estimated to be the late 5th century, following Tsukayama Kofun and preceding Tsukayama South Kofun{{Sfn|Tsukayama Kofun Group (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}. === Tsukayama South Kofun === {{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]] |name = Tsukayama South Kofun |image = [[File:Tsukayama Minami Kofun (Utsunomiya), funkyu-2.jpg|280px]]
Mound (rear circular section in the center, front section in the background) |alternate_name = |location = [[Tochigi Prefecture|Tochigi]], [[Utsunomiya]] Nishikawada Town Higashihara |type = [[Scallop-shaped kofun]] |area = Mound length: 58 m
Height: 6.8 m (rear section) |burial = Unknown |burial goods = [[Haniwa]], [[Sue pottery]], [[Haji pottery]] |built = [[5th century]] late |Historic Site = Prefectural Historic Site: "Tsukayama South Kofun" |notes = excavations designation1 as cultural properties of Utsunomiya City }} '''Tsukayama South Kofun''' (塚山南古墳) is a kofun located south of Tsukayama West Kofun. It is [[Scallop-shaped kofun|scallop-shaped]] and designation1 as a historic site by Tochigi Prefecture. The mound has a short front section and a rear circular section, oriented southward. The area are as follows{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}: * Total Kofun Length: 70.6 meters (including moat). * Mound Length: 58.0 meters. * Rear Circular Section ** Diameter: 42.1 meters ** Height: 6.8 meters * Front Section ** Length: 13.5 meters ** Height: 4.1 meters The mound is two-tiered{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. Numerous burial goods, including cylindrical haniwa, figurative haniwa (human, horse, deer, and house types), large Sue pottery vessels, and Haji pottery, were recovered, though no evidence of surface stones was found{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. A horseshoe-shaped moat surrounds the mound (narrower on the northwest side due to proximity to Tsukayama West Kofun){{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. burial have not been fully investigated, but depressions and red-painted stones suggest a vertical burial system at the mound's summit, likely plundered{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. The construction period is estimated to be the late 5th century to early 6th century, following Tsukayama West Kofun{{Sfn|Tsukayama Kofun Group (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}. == Historic Site == === Tochigi Prefectural Historic Site === * Historic Sites ** {{ill|Tsukayama Kofun|ja|塚山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - Designated on November 10, 1953 (Showa 28).[http://www.tochigi-edu.ed.jp/center/bunkazai/2341001.htm 塚山古墳] (Cultural Property Section, Tochigi Prefectural Board of Education).[https://utsunomiya-8story.jp/search_post/%e5%a1%9a%e5%b1%b1%e5%8f%a4%e5%a2%b3/ 塚山古墳] (Utsunomiya Historical and Cultural Resources Promotion Council). ** {{ill|Tsukayama Nishi Kofun|ja|塚山西古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - {{Coord|36|30|20.25|N|139|51|36.35|E}} | label2 = Tsukayama West Kofun | label-pos2 = top | label-color2 = black | mark2 = 帆立貝形古墳-南南東.svg | mark-size2 = 60 | mark-coord3 = {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun|qq=}} located in Nishikawada-machi, {{ill|Utsunomiya City|ja|宇都宮市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Utsunomiya City|qq=}}, Tochigi Prefecture. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/keyhole-shaped kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoenfun|qq=}} and part of the {{ill|Tsukayama Kofun Cluster|ja|塚山古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukayama Kofun Cluster|qq=}}. It has been designation1 as a Tochigi Prefecture-designation1 historical site. This article also covers the {{ill|Tsukayama Kofun Cluster|ja|塚山古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukayama Kofun Cluster|qq=}}, for which Tsukayama Kofun serves as the main mound. == Overview == [[File:100425 Tsukayama Kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|{{center|Aerial view of the Tsukayama Kofun Cluster (2010)}}{{small|Top right: Tsukayama Kofun; Left: Tsukayama West Kofun; Bottom left: Tsukayama South Kofun. {{ill|Aerial photographs of Japan|ja|国土航空写真|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aerial photographs of Japan|qq=}}.}}]] Located in southern Tochigi Prefecture, the mound was constructed on a plateau between the {{ill|Tagawa River (Tone River System)|ja|田川 (利根川水系)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tagawa River (Tone River System)|qq=}} and {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugata River|qq=}}. It is the largest keyhole-shaped kofun in the Tsukayama Kofun Cluster, which includes several mounds such as the scallop-shaped Tsukayama West and South Kofun, as well as {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/haniwa|qq=}}-based coffins. The rear circular section has been partially leveled by road construction. In 1989 (Heisei 1), a survey was conducted, followed by four excavation campaigns from 1989 to 1991. The mound has a "Kenbishi-style" keyhole type with a protruding front section oriented westward. It is constructed in three tiers, with external surfaces featuring {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/fukiishi|qq=}}. Cylindrical {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/haniwa|qq=}}, {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sue pottery|13=User:Immanuelle/Sue pottery|qq=}} (TK216-208 style), and {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Haji pottery|13=User:Immanuelle/Haji pottery|qq=}} have been excavated. The southern neck of the mound features a {{ill|tsukuridashi|ja|造出|1=Platform-style projection|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/tsukuridashi|13=User:Immanuelle/Platform-style projection|qq=}}, and the shield-shaped moat surrounding the mound brings the total length to 119.2 meters. The burial facility remains unexamined, and grave goods are largely unknown. The mound is estimated to date from the mid-5th century, during the middle {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun period|qq=}} (or the late 5th century, according to other estimates). It served as a prominent burial site for regional leaders in the southern Utsunomiya area and is considered critical for studying the political dynamics of the {{ill|Shimotsukeno region|ja|下毛野地方|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimotsukeno region|qq=}}. The site was designation1 as a Tochigi Prefecture historical site in 1953 (Shōwa 28). Today, the mound is adorned with {{ill|Dodantsutsuji shrubs|ja|ドウダンツツジ|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dodantsutsuji shrubs|qq=}}, offering a unique landscape that has been developed for preservation. == Ruins History == * [[1953]] (Showa 28), November 10: Tsukayama Kofun was designation1 as a historic site by Tochigi Prefecture. * [[1966]] (Showa 41): Construction planning for [[National Route 121]] (part of the [[Utsunomiya Ring Road]]) began. The plans were revised to include a tunnel near the kofun group to protect cultural properties. * [[1973]] (Showa 48), April 13: Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun were designation1 as historic sites by Tochigi Prefecture. * [[1976]] (Showa 51): Excavations of Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama East Kofun were conducted due to road construction (reported by the Tochigi Prefectural Board of Education in [[1979]]). * [[1989]]-[[1991]] (Heisei 1-3): Excavations of Tsukayama Kofun were carried out by the Archaeological Research Society of [[Utsunomiya University]] (findings published in [[1995]]). * [[1991]]-[[1992]] (Heisei 3-4): Excavations of the Tsukayama Kofun Group were conducted during road improvement work by the Utsunomiya City Board of Education (findings published in [[1996]]). * [[1995]]-[[1997]] (Heisei 7-9): Excavations of Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun were carried out for historic site conservation by the Utsunomiya City Board of Education, Utsunomiya University, and [[Utsunomiya Bunsei Junior College]] (findings published in [[2003]]). * [[2005]] (Heisei 17), November 7: burial goods excavated from Tsukayama South Kofun were designation1 as tangible cultural properties by Utsunomiya City. == Mound == The area of the mound are as follows{{Sfn|Tsukayama Kofun Group (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}: * Total Kofun Length: 119.2 meters - The overall length of the kofun, including the surrounding moat. * Mound Length: 98.3 meters * Rear Circular Section Diameter: 55.9 meters * Front Section Width: 59.9 meters File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), funkyu-4.jpg|Mound and surrounding moat. File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), funkyu-3.jpg|Mound
{{small|Rear circular section on the left, front section in the right background.}} File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), funcho.jpg|Summit of the rear circular section. File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), kouenbu.jpg|View from the front section toward the rear circular section. File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), zenpoubu.jpg|View from the rear circular section toward the front section. == Tsukayama Kofun Group == The '''Tsukayama Kofun Group''' consists of a cluster of kofun (ancient Kofuns) with Tsukayama Kofun as the main mound. Originally composed of over 10 kofun, it currently includes one [[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped kofun]] (Tsukayama Kofun), two [[Scallop-shaped kofun|scallop-shaped kofun]] (Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun), and one round kofun (No. 6 Kofun). Investigations have identified six small round kofun (Nos. 4, 5, 7, 8, and two within the old shooting range) to the north of Tsukayama Kofun. To the west and southwest, from north to south, lie a mid-sized round kofun (No. 6), Tsukayama West Kofun, and Tsukayama South Kofun. Haniwa sarcophagi have also been discovered in the area, with one featuring an engraved depiction of four deer in alternating male and female pairs. The construction period is estimated to span the mid-5th century to the early 6th century during the mid- to late-Kofun period, following the [[Mobara Kofun Group]] and the {{ill|Higashitani Kofun Group|ja|東谷古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Higashitani Kofun Group|qq=}}. The kofun group is detailed as follows: {| class="wikitable" style="text-align:center;background:#ffffff;white-space:nowrap;font-size:85%" |+List of Tsukayama Kofun GroupTsukayama Kofun Group Pamphlet.Historic Site Information Board. ! Mound (rear circular section in the center, front section in the background) |alternate_name = |location = [[Tochigi Prefecture|Tochigi]], [[Utsunomiya]] Nishikawada Town Higashihara |type = [[Scallop-shaped kofun]] |area = Mound length: 63.1 m
Height: 6.7 m (rear section) |burial = Unknown |burial goods = [[Haniwa]], [[Sue pottery]] |built = [[5th century]] late |Historic Site = Prefectural Historic Site: "Tsukayama West Kofun" |notes = }} '''Tsukayama West Kofun''' (塚山西古墳) is a kofun located southwest of Tsukayama Kofun. It is [[Scallop-shaped kofun|scallop-shaped]] and designation1 as a historic site by Tochigi Prefecture. The mound has a short front section and a rear circular section, oriented to the south-southeast. The area are as follows{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}: * Total Kofun Length: 74.1 meters (including moat). * Mound Length: 63.1 meters. * Rear Circular Section ** Diameter: 44.5 meters ** Height: 6.7 meters * Front Section ** Length: ~18 meters ** Width: ~22 meters ** Height: ~1.5 meters The mound comprises two or more tiers (upper tiers heavily disturbed){{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. Cylindrical haniwa and Sue pottery (TK208-TK23 styles) were found on the mound's surface{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. A horseshoe-shaped moat surrounds the mound (shallow on the east side due to proximity to Tsukayama Kofun){{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. burial are unknown due to limited findings; no clay or stone structures have been detected{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. The construction period is estimated to be the late 5th century, following Tsukayama Kofun and preceding Tsukayama South Kofun{{Sfn|Tsukayama Kofun Group (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}. === Tsukayama South Kofun === {{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]] |name = Tsukayama South Kofun |image = [[File:Tsukayama Minami Kofun (Utsunomiya), funkyu-2.jpg|280px]]
Mound (rear circular section in the center, front section in the background) |alternate_name = |location = [[Tochigi Prefecture|Tochigi]], [[Utsunomiya]] Nishikawada Town Higashihara |type = [[Scallop-shaped kofun]] |area = Mound length: 58 m
Height: 6.8 m (rear section) |burial = Unknown |burial goods = [[Haniwa]], [[Sue pottery]], [[Haji pottery]] |built = [[5th century]] late |Historic Site = Prefectural Historic Site: "Tsukayama South Kofun" |notes = excavations designation1 as cultural properties of Utsunomiya City }} '''Tsukayama South Kofun''' (塚山南古墳) is a kofun located south of Tsukayama West Kofun. It is [[Scallop-shaped kofun|scallop-shaped]] and designation1 as a historic site by Tochigi Prefecture. The mound has a short front section and a rear circular section, oriented southward. The area are as follows{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}: * Total Kofun Length: 70.6 meters (including moat). * Mound Length: 58.0 meters. * Rear Circular Section ** Diameter: 42.1 meters ** Height: 6.8 meters * Front Section ** Length: 13.5 meters ** Height: 4.1 meters The mound is two-tiered{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. Numerous burial goods, including cylindrical haniwa, figurative haniwa (human, horse, deer, and house types), large Sue pottery vessels, and Haji pottery, were recovered, though no evidence of surface stones was found{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. A horseshoe-shaped moat surrounds the mound (narrower on the northwest side due to proximity to Tsukayama West Kofun){{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. burial have not been fully investigated, but depressions and red-painted stones suggest a vertical burial system at the mound's summit, likely plundered{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. The construction period is estimated to be the late 5th century to early 6th century, following Tsukayama West Kofun{{Sfn|Tsukayama Kofun Group (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}. == Historic Site == === Tochigi {{Coord|36|30|17.93|N|139|51|37.23|E}} | label3 = Tsukayama South Kofun | label-pos3 = left | label-color3 = black | mark3 = 帆立貝形古墳-南.svg | mark-size3 = 60 }} '''Tsukayama Kofun''' (塚山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun|qq=}} located in Nishikawada-machi, {{ill|Utsunomiya City|ja|宇都宮市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Utsunomiya City|qq=}}, Tochigi Prefecture. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/keyhole-shaped kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoenfun|qq=}} and part of the {{ill|Tsukayama Kofun Cluster|ja|塚山古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukayama Kofun Cluster|qq=}}. It has been designation1 as a Tochigi Prefecture-designation1 historical site. This article also covers the {{ill|Tsukayama Kofun Cluster|ja|塚山古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukayama Kofun Cluster|qq=}}, for which Tsukayama Kofun serves as the main mound. == Overview == [[File:100425 Tsukayama Kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|{{center|Aerial view of the Tsukayama Kofun Cluster (2010)}}{{small|Top right: Tsukayama Kofun; Left: Tsukayama West Kofun; Bottom left: Tsukayama South Kofun. {{ill|Aerial photographs of Japan|ja|国土航空写真|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aerial photographs of Japan|qq=}}.}}]] Located in southern Tochigi Prefecture, the mound was constructed on a plateau between the {{ill|Tagawa River (Tone River System)|ja|田川 (利根川水系)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tagawa River (Tone River System)|qq=}} and {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugata River|qq=}}. It is the largest keyhole-shaped kofun in the Tsukayama Kofun Cluster, which includes several mounds such as the scallop-shaped Tsukayama West and South Kofun, as well as {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/haniwa|qq=}}-based coffins. The rear circular section has been partially leveled by road construction. In 1989 (Heisei 1), a survey was conducted, followed by four excavation campaigns from 1989 to 1991. The mound has a "Kenbishi-style" keyhole type with a protruding front section oriented westward. It is constructed in three tiers, with external surfaces featuring {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/fukiishi|qq=}}. Cylindrical {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/haniwa|qq=}}, {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sue pottery|13=User:Immanuelle/Sue pottery|qq=}} (TK216-208 style), and {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Haji pottery|13=User:Immanuelle/Haji pottery|qq=}} have been excavated. The southern neck of the mound features a {{ill|tsukuridashi|ja|造出|1=Platform-style projection|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/tsukuridashi|13=User:Immanuelle/Platform-style projection|qq=}}, and the shield-shaped moat surrounding the mound brings the total length to 119.2 meters. The burial facility remains unexamined, and grave goods are largely unknown. The mound is estimated to date from the mid-5th century, during the middle {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun period|qq=}} (or the late 5th century, according to other estimates). It served as a prominent burial site for regional leaders in the southern Utsunomiya area and is considered critical for studying the political dynamics of the {{ill|Shimotsukeno region|ja|下毛野地方|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimotsukeno region|qq=}}. The site was designation1 as a Tochigi Prefecture historical site in 1953 (Shōwa 28). Today, the mound is adorned with {{ill|Dodantsutsuji shrubs|ja|ドウダンツツジ|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dodantsutsuji shrubs|qq=}}, offering a unique landscape that has been developed for preservation. == Ruins History == * [[1953]] (Showa 28), November 10: Tsukayama Kofun was designation1 as a historic site by Tochigi Prefecture. * [[1966]] (Showa 41): Construction planning for [[National Route 121]] (part of the [[Utsunomiya Ring Road]]) began. The plans were revised to include a tunnel near the kofun group to protect cultural properties. * [[1973]] (Showa 48), April 13: Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun were designation1 as historic sites by Tochigi Prefecture. * [[1976]] (Showa 51): Excavations of Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama East Kofun were conducted due to road construction (reported by the Tochigi Prefectural Board of Education in [[1979]]). * [[1989]]-[[1991]] (Heisei 1-3): Excavations of Tsukayama Kofun were carried out by the Archaeological Research Society of [[Utsunomiya University]] (findings published in [[1995]]). * [[1991]]-[[1992]] (Heisei 3-4): Excavations of the Tsukayama Kofun Group were conducted during road improvement work by the Utsunomiya City Board of Education (findings published in [[1996]]). * [[1995]]-[[1997]] (Heisei 7-9): Excavations of Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun were carried out for historic site conservation by the Utsunomiya City Board of Education, Utsunomiya University, and [[Utsunomiya Bunsei Junior College]] (findings published in [[2003]]). * [[2005]] (Heisei 17), November 7: burial goods excavated from Tsukayama South Kofun were designation1 as tangible cultural properties by Utsunomiya City. == Mound == The area of the mound are as follows{{Sfn|Tsukayama Kofun Group (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}: * Total Kofun Length: 119.2 meters - The overall length of the kofun, including the surrounding moat. * Mound Length: 98.3 meters * Rear Circular Section Diameter: 55.9 meters * Front Section Width: 59.9 meters File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), funkyu-4.jpg|Mound and surrounding moat. File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), zenpoubu.jpg|View from the rear circular section toward the front section. == Tsukayama Kofun Group == The '''Tsukayama Kofun Group''' consists of a cluster of kofun (ancient Kofuns) with Tsukayama Kofun as the main mound. Originally composed of over 10 kofun, it currently includes one [[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped kofun]] (Tsukayama Kofun), two [[Scallop-shaped kofun|scallop-shaped kofun]] (Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun), and one round kofun (No. 6 Kofun). Investigations have identified six small round kofun (Nos. 4, 5, 7, 8, and two within the old shooting range) to the north of Tsukayama Kofun. To the west and southwest, from north to south, lie a mid-sized round kofun (No. 6), Tsukayama West Kofun, and Tsukayama South Kofun. Haniwa sarcophagi have also been discovered in the area, with one featuring an engraved depiction of four deer in alternating male and female pairs. The construction period is estimated to span the mid-5th century to the early 6th century during the mid- to late-Kofun period, following the [[Mobara Kofun Group]] and the {{ill|Higashitani Kofun Group|ja|東谷古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Higashitani Kofun Group|qq=}}. Mound (rear circular section in the center, front section in the background) |alternate_name = |location = [[Tochigi Prefecture|Tochigi]], [[Utsunomiya]] Nishikawada Town Higashihara |type = [[Scallop-shaped kofun]] |area = Mound length: 63.1 m
Height: 6.7 m (rear section) |burial = Unknown |burial goods = [[Haniwa]], [[Sue pottery]] |built = [[5th century]] late |Historic Site = Prefectural Historic Site: "Tsukayama West Kofun" |notes = }} '''Tsukayama West Kofun''' (塚山西古墳) is a kofun located southwest of Tsukayama Kofun. It is [[Scallop-shaped kofun|scallop-shaped]] and designation1 as a historic site by Tochigi Prefecture. The mound has a short front section and a rear circular section, oriented to the south-southeast. The area are as follows{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}: * Total Kofun Length: 74.1 meters (including moat). * Mound Length: 63.1 meters. * Rear Circular Section ** Diameter: 44.5 meters ** Height: 6.7 meters * Front Section ** Length: ~18 meters ** Width: ~22 meters ** Height: ~1.5 meters The mound comprises two or more tiers (upper tiers heavily disturbed){{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. Cylindrical haniwa and Sue pottery (TK208-TK23 styles) were found on the mound's surface{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. A horseshoe-shaped moat surrounds the mound (shallow on the east side due to proximity to Tsukayama Kofun){{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. burial are unknown due to limited findings; no clay or stone structures have been detected{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. The construction period is estimated to be the late 5th century, following Tsukayama Kofun and preceding Tsukayama South Kofun{{Sfn|Tsukayama Kofun Group (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}. === Tsukayama South Kofun === {{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]] |name = Tsukayama South Kofun |image = [[File:Tsukayama Minami Kofun (Utsunomiya), funkyu-2.jpg|280px]]
Mound (rear circular section in the center, front section in the background) |alternate_name = |location = [[Tochigi Prefecture|Tochigi]], [[Utsunomiya]] Nishikawada Town Higashihara |type = [[Scallop-shaped kofun]] |area = Mound length: 58 m
Height: 6.8 m (rear section) |burial = Unknown |burial goods = [[Haniwa]], [[Sue pottery]], [[Haji pottery]] |built = [[5th century]] late |Historic Site = Prefectural Historic Site: "Tsukayama South Kofun" |notes = excavations designation1 as cultural properties of Utsunomiya City }} '''Tsukayama South Kofun''' (塚山南古墳) is a kofun located south of Tsukayama West Kofun. It is [[Scallop-shaped kofun|scallop-shaped]] and designation1 as a historic site by Tochigi Prefecture. The mound has a short front section and a rear circular section, oriented southward. The area are as follows{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}: * Total Kofun Length: 70.6 meters (including moat). * Mound Length: 58.0 meters. * Rear Circular Section ** Diameter: 42.1 meters ** Height: 6.8 meters * Front Section ** Length: 13.5 meters ** Height: 4.1 meters The mound is two-tiered{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. Numerous burial goods, including cylindrical haniwa, figurative haniwa (human, horse, deer, and house types), large Sue pottery vessels, and Haji pottery, were recovered, though no evidence of surface stones was found{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. A horseshoe-shaped moat surrounds the mound (narrower on the northwest side due to proximity to Tsukayama West Kofun){{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. burial have not been fully investigated, but depressions and red-painted stones suggest a vertical burial system at the mound's summit, likely plundered{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. The construction period is estimated to be the late 5th century to early 6th century, following Tsukayama West Kofun{{Sfn|Tsukayama Kofun Group (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}. == Historic Site == === Tochigi {{Coord|36|30|17.93|N|139|51|37.23|E}} | label3 = Tsukayama South Kofun | label-pos3 = left | label-color3 = black | mark3 = 帆立貝形古墳-南.svg | mark-size3 = 60 }} '''Tsukayama Kofun''' (塚山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun|qq=}} located in Nishikawada-machi, {{ill|Utsunomiya City|ja|宇都宮市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Utsunomiya City|qq=}}, Tochigi Prefecture. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/keyhole-shaped kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoenfun|qq=}} and part of the {{ill|Tsukayama Kofun Cluster|ja|塚山古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukayama Kofun Cluster|qq=}}. It has been designation1 as a Tochigi Prefecture-designation1 historical site. This article also covers the {{ill|Tsukayama Kofun Cluster|ja|塚山古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukayama Kofun Cluster|qq=}}, for which Tsukayama Kofun serves as the main mound. == Overview == [[File:100425 Tsukayama Kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|{{center|Aerial view of the Tsukayama Kofun Cluster (2010)}}{{small|Top right: Tsukayama Kofun; Left: Tsukayama West Kofun; Bottom left: Tsukayama South Kofun. {{ill|Aerial photographs of Japan|ja|国土航空写真|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aerial photographs of Japan|qq=}}.}}]] Located in southern Tochigi Prefecture, the mound was constructed on a plateau between the {{ill|Tagawa River (Tone River System)|ja|田川 (利根川水系)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tagawa River (Tone River System)|qq=}} and {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugata River|qq=}}. It is the largest keyhole-shaped kofun in the Tsukayama Kofun Cluster, which includes several mounds such as the scallop-shaped Tsukayama West and South Kofun, as well as {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/haniwa|qq=}}-based coffins. The rear circular section has been partially leveled by road construction. In 1989 (Heisei 1), a survey was conducted, followed by four excavation campaigns from 1989 to 1991. The mound has a "Kenbishi-style" keyhole type with a protruding front section oriented westward. It is constructed in three tiers, with external surfaces featuring {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/fukiishi|qq=}}. Cylindrical {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/haniwa|qq=}}, {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sue pottery|13=User:Immanuelle/Sue pottery|qq=}} (TK216-208 style), and {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Haji pottery|13=User:Immanuelle/Haji pottery|qq=}} have been excavated. The southern neck of the mound features a {{ill|tsukuridashi|ja|造出|1=Platform-style projection|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/tsukuridashi|13=User:Immanuelle/Platform-style projection|qq=}}, and the shield-shaped moat surrounding the mound brings the total length to 119.2 meters. The burial facility remains unexamined, and grave goods are largely unknown. The mound is estimated to date from the mid-5th century, during the middle {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun period|qq=}} (or the late 5th century, according to other estimates). It served as a prominent burial site for regional leaders in the southern Utsunomiya area and is considered critical for studying the political dynamics of the {{ill|Shimotsukeno region|ja|下毛野地方|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimotsukeno region|qq=}}. The site was designation1 as a Tochigi Prefecture historical site in 1953 (Shōwa 28). Today, the mound is adorned with {{ill|Dodantsutsuji shrubs|ja|ドウダンツツジ|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dodantsutsuji shrubs|qq=}}, offering a unique landscape that has been developed for preservation. == Ruins History == * [[1953]] (Showa 28), November 10: Tsukayama Kofun was designation1 as a historic site by Tochigi Prefecture. * [[1966]] (Showa 41): Construction planning for [[National Route 121]] (part of the [[Utsunomiya Ring Road]]) began. The plans were revised to include a tunnel near the kofun group to protect cultural properties. * [[1973]] (Showa 48), April 13: Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun were designation1 as historic sites by Tochigi Prefecture. * [[1976]] (Showa 51): Excavations of Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama East Kofun were conducted due to road construction (reported by the Tochigi Prefectural Board of Education in [[1979]]). * [[1989]]-[[1991]] (Heisei 1-3): Excavations of Tsukayama Kofun were carried out by the Archaeological Research Society of [[Utsunomiya University]] (findings published in [[1995]]). * [[1991]]-[[1992]] (Heisei 3-4): Excavations of the Tsukayama Kofun Group were conducted during road improvement work by the Utsunomiya City Board of Education (findings published in [[1996]]). * [[1995]]-[[1997]] (Heisei 7-9): Excavations of Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun were carried out for historic site conservation by the Utsunomiya City Board of Education, Utsunomiya University, and [[Utsunomiya Bunsei Junior College]] (findings published in [[2003]]). * [[2005]] (Heisei 17), November 7: burial goods excavated from Tsukayama South Kofun were designation1 as tangible cultural properties by Utsunomiya City. == Mound == The area of the mound are as follows{{Sfn|Tsukayama Kofun Group (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}: * Total Kofun Length: 119.2 meters - The overall length of the kofun, including the surrounding moat. * Mound Length: 98.3 meters * Rear Circular Section Diameter: 55.9 meters * Front Section Width: 59.9 meters File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), funkyu-4.jpg|Mound and surrounding moat. File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), funkyu-3.jpg|Mound
{{small|Rear circular section on the left, front section in the right background.}} File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), funcho.jpg|Summit of the rear circular section. File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), kouenbu.jpg|View from the front section toward the rear circular section. File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), zenpoubu.jpg|View from the rear circular section toward the front section. == Tsukayama Kofun Group == The '''Tsukayama Kofun Group''' consists of a cluster of kofun (ancient Kofuns) with Tsukayama Kofun as the main mound. Originally composed of over 10 kofun, it currently includes one [[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped kofun]] (Tsukayama Kofun), two [[Scallop-shaped kofun|scallop-shaped kofun]] (Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun), and one round kofun (No. 6 Kofun). Investigations have identified six small round kofun (Nos. 4, 5, 7, 8, and two within the old shooting range) to the north of Tsukayama Kofun. To the west and southwest, from north to south, lie a mid-sized round kofun (No. 6), Tsukayama West Kofun, and Tsukayama South Kofun. Haniwa sarcophagi have also been discovered in the area, with one featuring an engraved depiction of four deer in alternating male and female pairs. The construction period is estimated to span the mid-5th century to the early 6th century during the mid- to late-Kofun period, following the [[Mobara Kofun Group]] and the {{ill|Higashitani Kofun Group|ja|東谷古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Higashitani Kofun Group|qq=}}. The kofun group is detailed as follows: {| class="wikitable" style="text-align:center;background:#ffffff;white-space:nowrap;font-size:85%" |+List of Tsukayama Kofun GroupTsukayama Kofun Group Pamphlet.Historic Site Information Board. ! Mound (rear circular section in the center, front section in the background) |alternate_name = |location = [[Tochigi Prefecture|Tochigi]], [[Utsunomiya]] Nishikawada Town Higashihara |type = [[Scallop-shaped kofun]] |area = Mound length: 63.1 m
Height: 6.7 m (rear section) |burial = Unknown |burial goods = [[Haniwa]], [[Sue pottery]] |built = [[5th century]] late |Historic Site = Prefectural Historic Site: "Tsukayama West Kofun" |notes = }} '''Tsukayama West Kofun''' (塚山西古墳) is a kofun located southwest of Tsukayama Kofun. It is [[Scallop-shaped kofun|scallop-shaped]] and designation1 as a historic site by Tochigi Prefecture. The mound has a short front section and a rear circular section, oriented to the south-southeast. The area are as follows{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}: * Total Kofun Length: 74.1 meters (including moat). * Mound Length: 63.1 meters. * Rear Circular Section ** Diameter: 44.5 meters ** Height: 6.7 meters * Front Section ** Length: ~18 meters ** Width: ~22 meters ** Height: ~1.5 meters The mound comprises two or more tiers (upper tiers heavily disturbed){{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. Cylindrical haniwa and Sue pottery (TK208-TK23 styles) were found on the mound's surface{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. A horseshoe-shaped moat surrounds the mound (shallow on the east side due to proximity to Tsukayama Kofun){{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. burial are unknown due to limited findings; no clay or stone structures have been detected{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. The construction period is estimated to be the late 5th century, following Tsukayama Kofun and preceding Tsukayama South Kofun{{Sfn|Tsukayama Kofun Group (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}. === Tsukayama South Kofun === {{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]] |name = Tsukayama South Kofun |image = [[File:Tsukayama Minami Kofun (Utsunomiya), funkyu-2.jpg|280px]]
Mound (rear circular section in the center, front section in the background) |alternate_name = |location = [[Tochigi Prefecture|Tochigi]], [[Utsunomiya]] Nishikawada Town Higashihara |type = [[Scallop-shaped kofun]] |area = Mound length: 58 m
Height: 6.8 m (rear section) |burial = Unknown |burial goods = [[Haniwa]], [[Sue pottery]], [[Haji pottery]] |built = [[5th century]] late |Historic Site = Prefectural Historic Site: "Tsukayama South Kofun" |notes = excavations designation1 as cultural properties of Utsunomiya City }} '''Tsukayama South Kofun''' (塚山南古墳) is a kofun located south of Tsukayama West Kofun. It is [[Scallop-shaped kofun|scallop-shaped]] and designation1 as a historic site by Tochigi Prefecture. The mound has a short front section and a rear circular section, oriented southward. The area are as follows{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}: * Total Kofun Length: 70.6 meters (including moat). * Mound Length: 58.0 meters. * Rear Circular Section ** Diameter: 42.1 meters ** Height: 6.8 meters * Front Section ** Length: 13.5 meters ** Height: 4.1 meters The mound is two-tiered{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. Numerous burial goods, including cylindrical haniwa, figurative haniwa (human, horse, deer, and house types), large Sue pottery vessels, and Haji pottery, were recovered, though no evidence of surface stones was found{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. A horseshoe-shaped moat surrounds the mound (narrower on the northwest side due to proximity to Tsukayama West Kofun){{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. burial have not been fully investigated, but depressions and red-painted stones suggest a vertical burial system at the mound's summit, likely plundered{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. The construction period is estimated to be the late 5th century to early 6th century, following Tsukayama West Kofun{{Sfn|Tsukayama Kofun Group (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}. == Historic Site == === Tochigi {{Coord|36|30|20|N|139|51|38|E}} | zoom = 17 | float = right | width = 300 | height = 250 | caption = {{center|Distribution map of the Tsukayama Kofun Cluster}} | map_sizemark = 60 | mark-coord1 = {{Coord|36|30|22.05|N|139|51|39.50|E}} | label1 = Tsukayama Kofun | label-pos1 = top | label-color1 = black | mark1 = 前方後円墳-西南西.svg | mark-size1 = 70 | mark-coord2 = {{Coord|36|30|20.25|N|139|51|36.35|E}} | label2 = Tsukayama West Kofun | label-pos2 = top | label-color2 = black | mark2 = 帆立貝形古墳-南南東.svg | mark-size2 = 60 | mark-coord3 = {{Coord|36|30|17.93|N|139|51|37.23|E}} | label3 = Tsukayama South Kofun | label-pos3 = left | label-color3 = black | mark3 = 帆立貝形古墳-南.svg | mark-size3 = 60 }} '''Tsukayama Kofun''' (塚山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun|qq=}} located in Nishikawada-machi, {{ill|Utsunomiya City|ja|宇都宮市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Utsunomiya City|qq=}}, Tochigi Prefecture. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/keyhole-shaped kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoenfun|qq=}} and part of the {{ill|Tsukayama Kofun Cluster|ja|塚山古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukayama Kofun Cluster|qq=}}. It has been designation1 as a Tochigi Prefecture-designation1 historical site. This article also covers the {{ill|Tsukayama Kofun Cluster|ja|塚山古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukayama Kofun Cluster|qq=}}, for which Tsukayama Kofun serves as the main mound. == Overview == [[File:100425 Tsukayama Kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|{{center|Aerial view of the Tsukayama Kofun Cluster (2010)}}{{small|Top right: Tsukayama Kofun; Left: Tsukayama West Kofun; Bottom left: Tsukayama South Kofun. {{ill|Aerial photographs of Japan|ja|国土航空写真|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aerial photographs of Japan|qq=}}.}}]] Located in southern Tochigi Prefecture, the mound was constructed on a plateau between the {{ill|Tagawa River (Tone River System)|ja|田川 (利根川水系)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tagawa River (Tone River System)|qq=}} and {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugata River|qq=}}. It is the largest keyhole-shaped kofun in the Tsukayama Kofun Cluster, which includes several mounds such as the scallop-shaped Tsukayama West and South Kofun, as well as {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/haniwa|qq=}}-based coffins. The rear circular section has been partially leveled by road construction. In 1989 (Heisei 1), a survey was conducted, followed by four excavation campaigns from 1989 to 1991. The mound has a "Kenbishi-style" keyhole type with a protruding front section oriented westward. It is constructed in three tiers, with external surfaces featuring {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/fukiishi|qq=}}. Cylindrical {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/haniwa|qq=}}, {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sue pottery|13=User:Immanuelle/Sue pottery|qq=}} (TK216-208 style), and {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Haji pottery|13=User:Immanuelle/Haji pottery|qq=}} have been excavated. The southern neck of the mound features a {{ill|tsukuridashi|ja|造出|1=Platform-style projection|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/tsukuridashi|13=User:Immanuelle/Platform-style projection|qq=}}, and the shield-shaped moat surrounding the mound brings the total length to 119.2 meters. The burial facility remains unexamined, and grave goods are largely unknown. The mound is estimated to date from the mid-5th century, during the middle {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun period|qq=}} (or the late 5th century, according to other estimates). It served as a prominent burial site for regional leaders in the southern Utsunomiya area and is considered critical for studying the political dynamics of the {{ill|Shimotsukeno region|ja|下毛野地方|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimotsukeno region|qq=}}. The site was designation1 as a Tochigi Prefecture historical site in 1953 (Shōwa 28). Today, the mound is adorned with {{ill|Dodantsutsuji shrubs|ja|ドウダンツツジ|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dodantsutsuji shrubs|qq=}}, offering a unique landscape that has been developed for preservation. == Ruins History == * [[1953]] (Showa 28), November 10: Tsukayama Kofun was designation1 as a historic site by Tochigi Prefecture. * [[1966]] (Showa 41): Construction planning for [[National Route 121]] (part of the [[Utsunomiya Ring Road]]) began. The plans were revised to include a tunnel near the kofun group to protect cultural properties. * [[1973]] (Showa 48), April 13: Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun were designation1 as historic sites by Tochigi Prefecture. * [[1976]] (Showa 51): Excavations of Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama East Kofun were conducted due to road construction (reported by the Tochigi Prefectural Board of Education in [[1979]]). * [[1989]]-[[1991]] (Heisei 1-3): Excavations of Tsukayama Kofun were carried out by the Archaeological Research Society of [[Utsunomiya University]] (findings published in [[1995]]). * [[1991]]-[[1992]] (Heisei 3-4): Excavations of the Tsukayama Kofun Group were conducted during road improvement work by the Utsunomiya City Board of Education (findings published in [[1996]]). * [[1995]]-[[1997]] (Heisei 7-9): Excavations of Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun were carried out for historic site conservation by the Utsunomiya City Board of Education, Utsunomiya University, and [[Utsunomiya Bunsei Junior College]] (findings published in [[2003]]). * [[2005]] (Heisei 17), November 7: burial goods excavated from Tsukayama South Kofun were designation1 as tangible cultural properties by Utsunomiya City. == Mound == The area of the mound are as follows{{Sfn|Tsukayama Kofun Group (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}: * Total Kofun Length: 119.2 meters - The overall length of the kofun, including the surrounding moat. * Mound Length: 98.3 meters * Rear Circular Section Diameter: 55.9 meters * Front Section Width: 59.9 meters File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), funkyu-4.jpg|Mound and surrounding moat. File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), funkyu-3.jpg|Mound
{{small|Rear circular section on the left, front section in the right background.}} File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), funcho.jpg|Summit of the rear circular section. File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), kouenbu.jpg|View from the front section toward the rear circular section. File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), zenpoubu.jpg|View from the rear circular section toward the front section. == Tsukayama Kofun Group == The '''Tsukayama Kofun Group''' consists of a cluster of kofun (ancient Kofuns) with Tsukayama Kofun as the main mound. Originally composed of over 10 kofun, it currently includes one [[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped kofun]] (Tsukayama Kofun), two [[Scallop-shaped kofun|scallop-shaped kofun]] (Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun), and one round kofun (No. 6 Kofun). Investigations have identified six small round kofun (Nos. 4, 5, 7, 8, and two within the old shooting range) to the north of Tsukayama Kofun. To the west and southwest, from north to south, lie a mid-sized round kofun (No. 6), Tsukayama West Kofun, and Tsukayama South Kofun. Haniwa sarcophagi have also been discovered in the area, with one featuring an engraved depiction of four deer in alternating male and female pairs. The construction period is estimated to span the mid-5th century to the early 6th century during the mid- to late-Kofun period, following the [[Mobara Kofun Group]] and the {{ill|Higashitani Kofun Group|ja|東谷古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Higashitani Kofun Group|qq=}}. The kofun group is detailed as follows: {| class="wikitable" style="text-align:center;background:#ffffff;white-space:nowrap;font-size:85%" |+List of Tsukayama Kofun GroupTsukayama Kofun Group Pamphlet.Historic Site Information Board. ! burial goods designation1 as cultural properties of Utsunomiya City |- |'''No. 4 Kofun'''||[[Enpun|Round kofun]]||Diameter: 8 m||style="text-align:left"|Pottery|| ||(Destroyed)|| |- |'''No. 5 Kofun'''||Round kofun||Diameter: 7 m||style="text-align:left"|Traces of wooden coffins, cylindrical haniwa, pottery, jewelry|| ||(Destroyed)|| |- |'''No. 6 Kofun'''||Round kofun||Diameter: 20 m||style="text-align:left"|Cylindrical haniwa, pottery|| ||None|| |- |'''No. 7 Kofun'''||Round kofun|| ||style="text-align:left"|Figurative haniwa (birds), pottery|| ||(Destroyed)|| |- |'''No. 8 Kofun'''||Round kofun|| ||style="text-align:left"|Cylindrical haniwa, pottery|| ||(Destroyed)|| |- |Two Kofun within Old Shooting Range||Round kofun|| ||style="text-align:left"|Cylindrical haniwa, figurative haniwa (birds, armor)|| ||(Destroyed)|| |- |Five Haniwa Sarcophagi||Haniwa Sarcophagi|| ||style="text-align:left"|Cylindrical haniwa|| ||(Destroyed)|| |} File:Tsukayama Kofun Group (Utsunomiya)-6, funkyu.jpg|No. 6 Kofun === Tsukayama West Kofun === {{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]] |name = Tsukayama West Kofun |image = [[File:Tsukayama Nishi Kofun (Utsunomiya), funkyu-2.jpg|280px]]
Mound (rear circular section in the center, front section in the background) |alternate_name = |location = [[Tochigi Prefecture|Tochigi]], [[Utsunomiya]] Nishikawada Town Higashihara |type = [[Scallop-shaped kofun]] |area = Mound length: 63.1 m
Height: 6.7 m (rear section) |burial = Unknown |burial goods = [[Haniwa]], [[Sue pottery]] |built = [[5th century]] late |Historic Site = Prefectural Historic Site: "Tsukayama West Kofun" |notes = }} '''Tsukayama West Kofun''' (塚山西古墳) is a kofun located southwest of Tsukayama Kofun. It is [[Scallop-shaped kofun|scallop-shaped]] and designation1 as a historic site by Tochigi Prefecture. The mound has a short front section and a rear circular section, oriented to the south-southeast. The area are as follows{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}: * Total Kofun Length: 74.1 meters (including moat). * Mound Length: 63.1 meters. * Rear Circular Section ** Diameter: 44.5 meters ** Height: 6.7 meters * Front Section ** Length: ~18 meters ** Width: ~22 meters ** Height: ~1.5 meters The mound comprises two or more tiers (upper tiers heavily disturbed){{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. Cylindrical haniwa and Sue pottery (TK208-TK23 styles) were found on the mound's surface{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. A horseshoe-shaped moat surrounds the mound (shallow on the east side due to proximity to Tsukayama Kofun){{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. burial are unknown due to limited findings; no clay or stone structures have been detected{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. The construction period is estimated to be the late 5th century, following Tsukayama Kofun and preceding Tsukayama South Kofun{{Sfn|Tsukayama Kofun Group (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}. === Tsukayama South Kofun === {{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]] |name = Tsukayama South Kofun |image = [[File:Tsukayama Minami Kofun (Utsunomiya), funkyu-2.jpg|280px]]
Mound (rear circular section in the center, front section in the background) |alternate_name = |location = [[Tochigi Prefecture|Tochigi]], [[Utsunomiya]] Nishikawada Town Higashihara |type = [[Scallop-shaped kofun]] |area = Mound length: 58 m
Height: 6.8 m (rear section) |burial = Unknown |burial goods = [[Haniwa]], [[Sue pottery]], [[Haji pottery]] |built = [[5th century]] late |Historic Site = Prefectural Historic Site: "Tsukayama South Kofun" |notes = excavations designation1 as cultural properties of Utsunomiya City }} '''Tsukayama South Kofun''' (塚山南古墳) is a kofun located south of Tsukayama West Kofun. It is [[Scallop-shaped kofun|scallop-shaped]] and designation1 as a historic site by Tochigi Prefecture. The mound has a short front section and a rear circular section, oriented southward. The area are as follows{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}: * Total Kofun Length: 70.6 meters (including moat). * Mound Length: 58.0 meters. * Rear Circular Section ** Diameter: 42.1 meters ** Height: 6.8 meters * Front Section ** Length: 13.5 meters ** Height: 4.1 meters The mound is two-tiered{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. Numerous burial goods, including cylindrical haniwa, figurative haniwa (human, horse, deer, and house types), large Sue pottery vessels, and Haji pottery, were recovered, though no evidence of surface stones was found{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. A horseshoe-shaped moat surrounds the mound (narrower on the northwest side due to proximity to Tsukayama West Kofun){{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. burial have not been fully investigated, but depressions and red-painted stones suggest a vertical burial system at the mound's summit, likely plundered{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. The construction period is estimated to be the late 5th century to early 6th century, following Tsukayama West Kofun{{Sfn|Tsukayama Kofun Group (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}. == Historic Site == === Tochigi {{Coord|36|30|20|N|139|51|38|E}} | zoom = 17 | float = right | width = 300 | height = 250 | caption = {{center|Distribution map of the Tsukayama Kofun Cluster}} | map_sizemark = 60 | mark-coord1 = {{Coord|36|30|22.05|N|139|51|39.50|E}} | label1 = Tsukayama Kofun | label-pos1 = top | label-color1 = black | mark1 = 前方後円墳-西南西.svg | mark-size1 = 70 | mark-coord2 = {{Coord|36|30|20.25|N|139|51|36.35|E}} | label2 = Tsukayama West Kofun | label-pos2 = top | label-color2 = black | mark2 = 帆立貝形古墳-南南東.svg | mark-size2 = 60 | mark-coord3 = {{Coord|36|30|17.93|N|139|51|37.23|E}} | label3 = Tsukayama South Kofun | label-pos3 = left | label-color3 = black | mark3 = 帆立貝形古墳-南.svg | mark-size3 = 60 }} '''Tsukayama Kofun''' (塚山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun|qq=}} located in Nishikawada-machi, {{ill|Utsunomiya City|ja|宇都宮市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Utsunomiya City|qq=}}, Tochigi Prefecture. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/keyhole-shaped kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoenfun|qq=}} and part of the {{ill|Tsukayama Kofun Cluster|ja|塚山古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukayama Kofun Cluster|qq=}}. It has been designation1 as a Tochigi Prefecture-designation1 historical site. This article also covers the {{ill|Tsukayama Kofun Cluster|ja|塚山古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukayama Kofun Cluster|qq=}}, for which Tsukayama Kofun serves as the main mound. == Overview == [[File:100425 Tsukayama Kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|{{center|Aerial view of the Tsukayama Kofun Cluster (2010)}}{{small|Top right: Tsukayama Kofun; Left: Tsukayama West Kofun; Bottom left: Tsukayama South Kofun. {{ill|Aerial photographs of Japan|ja|国土航空写真|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aerial photographs of Japan|qq=}}.}}]] Located in southern Tochigi Prefecture, the mound was constructed on a plateau between the {{ill|Tagawa River (Tone River System)|ja|田川 (利根川水系)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tagawa River (Tone River System)|qq=}} and {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugata River|qq=}}. It is the largest keyhole-shaped kofun in the Tsukayama Kofun Cluster, which includes several mounds such as the scallop-shaped Tsukayama West and South Kofun, as well as {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/haniwa|qq=}}-based coffins. The rear circular section has been partially leveled by road construction. In 1989 (Heisei 1), a survey was conducted, followed by four excavation campaigns from 1989 to 1991. The mound has a "Kenbishi-style" keyhole type with a protruding front section oriented westward. It is constructed in three tiers, with external surfaces featuring {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/fukiishi|qq=}}. Cylindrical {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/haniwa|qq=}}, {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sue pottery|13=User:Immanuelle/Sue pottery|qq=}} (TK216-208 style), and {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Haji pottery|13=User:Immanuelle/Haji pottery|qq=}} have been excavated. The southern neck of the mound features a {{ill|tsukuridashi|ja|造出|1=Platform-style projection|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/tsukuridashi|13=User:Immanuelle/Platform-style projection|qq=}}, and the shield-shaped moat surrounding the mound brings the total length to 119.2 meters. The burial facility remains unexamined, and grave goods are largely unknown. The mound is estimated to date from the mid-5th century, during the middle {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun period|qq=}} (or the late 5th century, according to other estimates). It served as a prominent burial site for regional leaders in the southern Utsunomiya area and is considered critical for studying the political dynamics of the {{ill|Shimotsukeno region|ja|下毛野地方|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimotsukeno region|qq=}}. The site was designation1 as a Tochigi Prefecture historical site in 1953 (Shōwa 28). Today, the mound is adorned with {{ill|Dodantsutsuji shrubs|ja|ドウダンツツジ|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dodantsutsuji shrubs|qq=}}, offering a unique landscape that has been developed for preservation. == Ruins History == * [[1953]] (Showa 28), November 10: Tsukayama Kofun was designation1 as a historic site by Tochigi Prefecture. * [[1966]] (Showa 41): Construction planning for [[National Route 121]] (part of the [[Utsunomiya Ring Road]]) began. The plans were revised to include a tunnel near the kofun group to protect cultural properties. * [[1973]] (Showa 48), April 13: Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun were designation1 as historic sites by Tochigi Prefecture. * [[1976]] (Showa 51): Excavations of Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama East Kofun were conducted due to road construction (reported by the Tochigi Prefectural Board of Education in [[1979]]). * [[1989]]-[[1991]] (Heisei 1-3): Excavations of Tsukayama Kofun were carried out by the Archaeological Research Society of [[Utsunomiya University]] (findings published in [[1995]]). * [[1991]]-[[1992]] (Heisei 3-4): Excavations of the Tsukayama Kofun Group were conducted during road improvement work by the Utsunomiya City Board of Education (findings published in [[1996]]). * [[1995]]-[[1997]] (Heisei 7-9): Excavations of Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun were carried out for historic site conservation by the Utsunomiya City Board of Education, Utsunomiya University, and [[Utsunomiya Bunsei Junior College]] (findings published in [[2003]]). * [[2005]] (Heisei 17), November 7: burial goods excavated from Tsukayama South Kofun were designation1 as tangible cultural properties by Utsunomiya City. == Mound == The area of the mound are as follows{{Sfn|Tsukayama Kofun Group (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}: * Total Kofun Length: 119.2 meters - The overall length of the kofun, including the surrounding moat. * Mound Length: 98.3 meters * Rear Circular Section Diameter: 55.9 meters * Front Section Width: 59.9 meters File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), funkyu-4.jpg|Mound and surrounding moat. File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), funkyu-3.jpg|Mound
{{small|Rear circular section on the left, front section in the right background.}} File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), funcho.jpg|Summit of the rear circular section. File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), kouenbu.jpg|View from the front section toward the rear circular section. File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), zenpoubu.jpg|View from the rear circular section toward the front section. == Tsukayama Kofun Group == The '''Tsukayama Kofun Group''' consists of a cluster of kofun (ancient Kofuns) with Tsukayama Kofun as the main mound. Originally composed of over 10 kofun, it currently includes one [[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped kofun]] (Tsukayama Kofun), two [[Scallop-shaped kofun|scallop-shaped kofun]] (Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun), and one round kofun (No. 6 Kofun). Investigations have identified six small round kofun (Nos. 4, 5, 7, 8, and two within the old shooting range) to the north of Tsukayama Kofun. To the west and southwest, from north to south, lie a mid-sized round kofun (No. 6), Tsukayama West Kofun, and Tsukayama South Kofun. Haniwa sarcophagi have also been discovered in the area, with one featuring an engraved depiction of four deer in alternating male and female pairs. The construction period is estimated to span the mid-5th century to the early 6th century during the mid- to late-Kofun period, following the [[Mobara Kofun Group]] and the {{ill|Higashitani Kofun Group|ja|東谷古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Higashitani Kofun Group|qq=}}. The kofun group is detailed as follows: {| class="wikitable" style="text-align:center;background:#ffffff;white-space:nowrap;font-size:85%" |+List of Tsukayama Kofun GroupTsukayama Kofun Group Pamphlet.Historic Site Information Board. ! Mound (rear circular section in the center, front section in the background) |alternate_name = |location = [[Tochigi Prefecture|Tochigi]], [[Utsunomiya]] Nishikawada Town Higashihara |type = [[Scallop-shaped kofun]] |area = Mound length: 63.1 m
Height: 6.7 m (rear section) |burial = Unknown |burial goods = [[Haniwa]], [[Sue pottery]] |built = [[5th century]] late |Historic Site = Prefectural Historic Site: "Tsukayama West Kofun" |notes = }} '''Tsukayama West Kofun''' (塚山西古墳) is a kofun located southwest of Tsukayama Kofun. It is [[Scallop-shaped kofun|scallop-shaped]] and designation1 as a historic site by Tochigi Prefecture. The mound has a short front section and a rear circular section, oriented to the south-southeast. The area are as follows{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}: * Total Kofun Length: 74.1 meters (including moat). * Mound Length: 63.1 meters. * Rear Circular Section ** Diameter: 44.5 meters ** Height: 6.7 meters * Front Section ** Length: ~18 meters ** Width: ~22 meters ** Height: ~1.5 meters The mound comprises two or more tiers (upper tiers heavily disturbed){{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. Cylindrical haniwa and Sue pottery (TK208-TK23 styles) were found on the mound's surface{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. A horseshoe-shaped moat surrounds the mound (shallow on the east side due to proximity to Tsukayama Kofun){{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. burial are unknown due to limited findings; no clay or stone structures have been detected{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. The construction period is estimated to be the late 5th century, following Tsukayama Kofun and preceding Tsukayama South Kofun{{Sfn|Tsukayama Kofun Group (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}. === Tsukayama South Kofun === {{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]] |name = Tsukayama South Kofun |image = [[File:Tsukayama Minami Kofun (Utsunomiya), funkyu-2.jpg|280px]]
Mound (rear circular section in the center, front section in the background) |alternate_name = |location = [[Tochigi Prefecture|Tochigi]], [[Utsunomiya]] Nishikawada Town Higashihara |type = [[Scallop-shaped kofun]] |area = Mound length: 58 m
Height: 6.8 m (rear section) |burial = Unknown |burial goods = [[Haniwa]], [[Sue pottery]], [[Haji pottery]] |built = [[5th century]] late |Historic Site = Prefectural Historic Site: "Tsukayama South Kofun" |notes = excavations designation1 as cultural properties of Utsunomiya City }} '''Tsukayama South Kofun''' (塚山南古墳) is a kofun located south of Tsukayama West Kofun. It is [[Scallop-shaped kofun|scallop-shaped]] and designation1 as a historic site by Tochigi Prefecture. The mound has a short front section and a rear circular section, oriented southward. The area are as follows{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}: * Total Kofun Length: 70.6 meters (including moat). * Mound Length: 58.0 meters. * Rear Circular Section ** Diameter: 42.1 meters ** Height: 6.8 meters * Front Section ** Length: 13.5 meters ** Height: 4.1 meters The mound is two-tiered{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. Numerous burial goods, including cylindrical haniwa, figurative haniwa (human, horse, deer, and house types), large Sue pottery vessels, and Haji pottery, were recovered, though no evidence of surface stones was found{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. A horseshoe-shaped moat surrounds the mound (narrower on the northwest side due to proximity to Tsukayama West Kofun){{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. burial have not been fully investigated, but depressions and red-painted stones suggest a vertical burial system at the mound's summit, likely plundered{{Sfn|Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun|2003}}. The construction period is estimated to be the late 5th century to early 6th century, following Tsukayama West Kofun{{Sfn|Tsukayama Kofun Group (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}. == Historic Site == === Tochigi {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun|qq=}} located in Nishikawada-machi, {{ill|Utsunomiya City|ja|宇都宮市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Utsunomiya City|qq=}}, Tochigi Prefecture. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/keyhole-shaped kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoenfun|qq=}} and part of the {{ill|Tsukayama Kofun Cluster|ja|塚山古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukayama Kofun Cluster|qq=}}. It has been designation1 as a Tochigi Prefecture-designation1 historical site. This article also covers the {{ill|Tsukayama Kofun Cluster|ja|塚山古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukayama Kofun Cluster|qq=}}, for which Tsukayama Kofun serves as the main mound. == Overview == [[File:100425 Tsukayama Kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|{{center|Aerial view of the Tsukayama Kofun Cluster (2010)}}{{small|Top right: Tsukayama Kofun; Left: Tsukayama West Kofun; Bottom left: Tsukayama South Kofun. {{ill|Aerial photographs of Japan|ja|国土航空写真|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aerial photographs of Japan|qq=}}.}}]] Located in southern Tochigi Prefecture, the mound was constructed on a plateau between the {{ill|Tagawa River (Tone River System)|ja|田川 (利根川水系)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tagawa River (Tone River System)|qq=}} and {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugata River|qq=}}. It is the largest keyhole-shaped kofun in the Tsukayama Kofun Cluster, which includes several mounds such as the scallop-shaped Tsukayama West and South Kofun, as well as {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/haniwa|qq=}}-based coffins. The rear circular section has been partially leveled by road construction. In 1989 (Heisei 1), a survey was conducted, followed by four excavation campaigns from 1989 to 1991. The mound has a "Kenbishi-style" keyhole type with a protruding front section oriented westward. It is constructed in three tiers, with external surfaces featuring {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/fukiishi|qq=}}. Cylindrical {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/haniwa|qq=}}, {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sue pottery|13=User:Immanuelle/Sue pottery|qq=}} (TK216-208 style), and {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Haji pottery|13=User:Immanuelle/Haji pottery|qq=}} have been excavated. The southern neck of the mound features a {{ill|tsukuridashi|ja|造出|1=Platform-style projection|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/tsukuridashi|13=User:Immanuelle/Platform-style projection|qq=}}, and the shield-shaped moat surrounding the mound brings the total length to 119.2 meters. The burial facility remains unexamined, and grave goods are largely unknown. The mound is estimated to date from the mid-5th century, during the middle {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun period|qq=}} (or the late 5th century, according to other estimates). It served as a prominent burial site for regional leaders in the southern Utsunomiya area and is considered critical for studying the political dynamics of the {{ill|Shimotsukeno region|ja|下毛野地方|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimotsukeno region|qq=}}. The site was designation1 as a Tochigi Prefecture historical site in 1953 (Shōwa 28). Today, the mound is adorned with {{ill|Dodantsutsuji shrubs|ja|ドウダンツツジ|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dodantsutsuji shrubs|qq=}}, offering a unique landscape that has been developed for preservation. == Ruins History == * [[1953]] (Showa 28), November 10: Tsukayama Kofun was designation1 as a historic site by Tochigi Prefecture. * [[1966]] (Showa 41): Construction planning for [[National Route 121]] (part of the [[Utsunomiya Ring Road]]) began. The plans were revised to include a tunnel near the kofun group to protect cultural properties. * [[1973]] (Showa 48), April 13: Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun were designation1 as historic sites by Tochigi Prefecture. * [[1976]] (Showa 51): Excavations of Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama East Kofun were conducted due to road construction (reported by the Tochigi Prefectural Board of Education in [[1979]]). * [[1989]]-[[1991]] (Heisei 1-3): Excavations of Tsukayama Kofun were carried out by the Archaeological Research Society of [[Utsunomiya University]] (findings published in [[1995]]). * [[1991]]-[[1992]] (Heisei 3-4): Excavations of the Tsukayama Kofun Group were conducted during road improvement work by the Utsunomiya City Board of Education (findings published in [[1996]]). * [[1995]]-[[1997]] (Heisei 7-9): Excavations of Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun were carried out for historic site conservation by the Utsunomiya City Board of Education, Utsunomiya University, and [[Utsunomiya Bunsei Junior College]] (findings published in [[2003]]). * [[2005]] (Heisei 17), November 7: burial goods excavated from Tsukayama South Kofun were designation1 as tangible cultural properties by Utsunomiya City. == Mound == The area of the mound are as follows{{Sfn|Tsukayama Kofun Group (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}: * Total Kofun Length: 119.2 meters - The overall length of the kofun, including the surrounding moat. * Mound Length: 98.3 meters * Rear Circular Section Diameter: 55.9 meters * Front Section Width: 59.9 meters File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), funkyu-4.jpg|Mound and surrounding moat. File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), funkyu-3.jpg|Mound
{{small|Rear circular section on the left, front section in the right background.}} File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), funcho.jpg|Summit of the rear circular section. File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), kouenbu.jpg|View from the front section toward the rear circular section. File:Tsukayama Kofun (Utsunomiya), zenpoubu.jpg|View from the rear circular section toward the front section. == Tsukayama Kofun Group == The '''Tsukayama Kofun Group''' consists of a cluster of kofun (ancient Kofuns) with Tsukayama Kofun as the main mound. Originally composed of over 10 kofun, it currently includes one [[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped kofun]] (Tsukayama Kofun), two [[Scallop-shaped kofun|scallop-shaped kofun]] (Tsukayama West Kofun and Tsukayama South Kofun), and one round kofun (No. 6 Kofun). Investigations have identified six small round kofun (Nos. 4, 5, 7, 8, and two within the old shooting range) to the north of Tsukayama Kofun. To the west and southwest, from north to south, lie a mid-sized round kofun (No. 6), Tsukayama West Kofun, and Tsukayama South Kofun. Haniwa sarcophagi have also been discovered in the area, with one featuring an engraved depiction of four deer in alternating male and female pairs. The construction period is estimated to span the mid-5th century to the early 6th century during the mid- to late-Kofun period, following the [[Mobara Kofun Group]] and the {{ill|Higashitani Kofun Group|ja|東谷古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Higashitani Kofun Group|qq=}}. The kofun group is detailed as follows: {| class="wikitable" style="text-align:center;background:#ffffff;white-space:nowrap;font-size:85%" |+List of Tsukayama Kofun GroupTsukayama Kofun Group Pamphlet.Historic Site Information Board. ! Kofun name ! type ! area ! burial goods ! built ! Historic Site ! notes |- |'''No. 1 Kofun
(Tsukayama Kofun)'''||[[Zenpokoenfun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]]||Mound length: 98 m||style="text-align:left"|Cylindrical haniwa, Sue pottery||Mid-5th century||Prefectural Designation||style="text-align:left"|Survey: 1989
Excavation: 1989, 1990, 1991 |- |'''No. 2 Kofun
(Tsukayama West Kofun)'''||[[Scallop-shaped kofun]]||Mound length: 63 m||style="text-align:left"|Cylindrical haniwa, Sue pottery||Late 5th century||Prefectural Designation||style="text-align:left"|Survey: 1976, 1995
Excavation: 1976, 1990, 1995, 1996 |- |'''No. 3 Kofun
